title: What do you mean All Arrows are Given?
description:
Oops - nearly forgot toi post this! Here's where you can try the amazing All Arrows Are Given by Kainapple: https://sudokupad.app/5y1anz3kmc 
Place 1-6 in each row, column and 3x2 box. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. 
Arrows in this puzzle point either up, down, left or right, they never change direction, and all such arrows are given. That is, you could not draw any more of these straight arrows into the finished puzzle grid (even those that would overlap other arrows or their circles in any possible way).

title: Love Letter from Canada
description:
Here's where you can attempt Love Letter from Canada by SUDOOOOOKUfan87: https://sudokupad.app/esjz6meusc 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a path from r1c9 to r9c1. The path moves orthogonally and visits all 3x3 regions. Adjacent digits on the path must have a difference of at least 4. r1c9 and r9c1 are the only island cells on the path. All cells are either island or water.
Each lavender cell is an island cell; the number in it is the number of cells in that island. Each lavender island must consist of exactly one lavender cell, and a set of non-repeating digits that sum to the total in the lavender cell, if given (r6c8's island total is a prime number). r1c9 (Canada) and r9c1 (Japan) are non-lavender island cells. Both islands' digits have the same product. The digits on the flags are inconsequential. Different islands may not touch orthogonally. The water cells are orthogonally connected and may not contain any 2×2 areas of water. Cage totals are not necessarily in the top left most cell of an island.

title: Minesweeper: The Sudoku!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Do you remember Minesweeper? Well the Microsoft version inevitably could lead to some guessing but the sudoku version is purely logical and absolutely miraculous!! It's by TalkingFredish and Michael Lefkowitz and it is absolutely a contender for Puzzle Of The Year.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/1ru4mm2uq3?setting-nogrid=1

Rules
Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply. (ie place the digits 1 to 6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 box).
MINESWEEPER: Shade some cells ('mines') and leave the others unshaded ('cleared'). Two cleared cells are shown (although one of these still needs its digit to be entered). Each digit in a cleared cell indicates how many mines are in the (up to 8) surrounding cells. No two 2x3 boxes have the same number of mines.

Today's musical introduction is a slightly more practised version of Jigsaw Falling Into Place by Radiohead.

title: Sudoku Helps You Know Your Bits From Your Bytes!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Here's an unusual sudoku tonight: the rules might need a couple of read-throughs but the logic is actually fairly simple once you get your head around it and the puzzle itself is so lovely you can't help but smile. Enjoy Jonesy's Bits And Nibbles!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/xag582l3t0

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply.
Parity Counter Lines: the two digits at the ends of each line indicate the number of odd and even digits in that line, including the end digits themselves. One digit counts odd digits; the other counts even digits.
BitClock: A BitClock is a group of five cells: a central arrow cell and its four orthogonally adjacent neighbours (up, right, down, left). The arrow shows where the pattern starts, and the pattern is then read clockwise around the four neighbours.  The digit in the central arrow cell tells you the odd/even pattern of those four neighbours, using a simple 4-bit code. In those neighbour cells, an even digit means the “bit” is ON; while an odd digit means the “bit” is OFF.  Each arrow cell digit has its own fixed 4-bit pattern (see table below). Eg If a 3 is placed in an arrow cell, its code is OOEE.Starting from the direction of the arrow and reading clockwise, the four orthogonal neighbours must be Odd, Odd, Even, Even.
Digit Codes: 1 → OOOE2 → OOEO3 → OOEE4 → OEOO 5 → OEOE 6 → OEEO 7 → OEEE 8 → EOOO 9 → EOOE

title: In the Mood for Modulo
description:
Here's where you can attempt Modular Masyu by Yttrio: https://sudokupad.app/6me9411h8m 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single non-intersecting loop through the centers of some cells that moves horizontally or vertically and passes through every circle clue. The loop must turn on black circles and pass straight through the cells on either side. The loop must go straight through white circles and turn in at least one of the cells on either side.
The loop acts as a modular line. Each set of three adjacent digits along the loop must be one each from the sets [147], [258], and [369]. The digit in each given circle clue counts the total number of loop cells in all straight loop segments coming off of the cell (counting the cells where the loop turns, and counting the clued cell itself once).

title: The Sudoku House Of Cards: It's Easy Once You "See" It!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
James Sinclair has long been one of the very best constructors in the world. He's known for his beautiful logic and fairly approachable puzzles. Well this one has the former but it's definitely not terribly easy (for this solver at least!). It's called House Of Cards and it behaves just as it sounds... if you can get the first cards toppling, the whole thing will fall apart in the most extraordinary way!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/nam4l5oykp

Rules
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply within the 6x6 grid. (ie place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 box.) Cells outside the grid contain “skyscraper clues”, which indicate the number of digits “visible” in that direction in the 6x6 grid (where higher digits block the view of lower digits). Eg a row reading 216453 would have a clue of 2 from the left (as the 2 and 6 would be visible); and a clue of 3 from the right (as the 3, 5 and 6 would be visible). Each cage sum is the same, and digits may repeat within a cage. Digits in cells separated by a gold dot are not consecutive. (The "solution checker" does not consider the skyscraper clues outside the grid.)
You can find more puzzles by James here:
https://artisanalsudoku.substack.com/

title: Pure Rotational Symmetry!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Rip City by Merdock: https://sudokupad.app/r3n9cwda1t 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on the red line alternate between even and odd digits. White dots separate consecutive digits that are adjacent to each other along the red line. All dots along the red line are given. If two cells both have a red line, but the cells are not adjacent along the path of the line, no dot will be given even if the digits are consecutive. For example, r2c6 and r2c7 both have a red line passing through them, but because the line does not travel immediately from r2c6 to r2c7, the lack of a dot does not mean anything.
There are four single cell cages at the corner of the grid. These individual cages act as a single combined cage. The 4 digits must sum to 16. Digits cannot repeat on the marked diagonal.

title: The Creative Sudoku Genius Of Marty Sears
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
While we wait for the new season of Rat Run, Marty Sears is still busy creating other fantastic sudokus. Tonight's is called Web Design and it introduces us to Cecil The Spider and we have to help him build his web. This is innovative, witty and brilliant - everything we've come to expect from a creative sudoku genius.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/jaw9z4nws6

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Help Cecil the Spider to build a web using silky threads. A single silky thread must start at a white spot and connect to another white spot that is either one or two cells away in a straight line (horizontally, vertically or diagonally.) Any further and the thread will break! Two silky threads may not cross each other. The digit on a white spot indicates how many silky threads attach to it. The two white spots connected by a silky thread may not contain the same digit. If a black insect sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a stripy green insect sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a spotty red insect sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. The digit being thought about by Cecil the Spider indicates how many of the afore-mentioned insects have been caught on silky threads.

title: How To Recover From A Catastrophic Sudoku Mistake
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for masetab and a very original and interesting play on chaos construction sudoku. It's rated 5* for difficulty but, without wanting to give too much away, it's possible to solve much more quickly than the video length...  Why? Well, you'll have to watch to find out!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/x61fnlh3u8

Rules
Fill the grid with digits 1–9 so that each row and each column contains every digit exactly once. Digits also may not repeat within regions. Construct regions made up of orthogonally connected cells such that every region contains exactly one circle. The number of cells in a region must match the number in the region's circle. Each region contains a consecutive set of digits, e.g: {2,3,4},{1},{4,5,6,7,8,9}. The digits do not have to start at 1 and may appear in any order within the region. If a black dot sits between two digits, then one is double the other. The two cells must be within the same region. Not all possible black dots are given. A white dot between two cells indicates the digits are consecutive. The two cells must be within the same region. Not all possible white dots are given. Clues outside the grid, indicated by arrows, show the sum of the digits along the diagonal path of the arrow.

title: The New Sudoku Rule: The Golden Dot
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A really cool innovation today from Patrick Junke and his delightfully named sudoku, The Fireflies' Pairing Dance! It involves a golden dot - which separates two digits that sum to a multiple of 4. Lots of people are loving this puzzle and with good reason - give it a try if you can!

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ruz1c8uhcr

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply ie Each row, column, and 3×3 box must contain the digits 1–9 exactly once. A golden dot between two cells indicates that their sum is divisible by 4. ALL possible golden dots are given. Golden dots take precedence over the black dots ie if two cells could have black dot and a golden dot, only the golden dot is shown. A black dot between two digits indicates that one is double the other. Not all possible black dots are given. A white dot between two digits indicates they are consecutive. Not all possible white dots are given. The sum of two adjacent cells separated by a 3x3 box border are even. Note that the sum of two adjacent cells not separated by a 3x3 box border may still be even.

Sometimes we get wind of sudokus to which injustices have been done. That is certainly the case for The Two Wings Of The Eagle Totem by Jeff Wajes. title: What Sorcery is This?
description:
Here's where you can take on The Good, the Bad and the Ugly by UnnamedSorcerer: https://sudokupad.app/4ljh14tybv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. An arrow outside the puzzle indicates that the X-Sum, Sandwich,
Skyscrapers, and Little Killer clues at that location are identical. Cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive values. Cells joined by a black dot contain values where one is double the other. 
The clue outside the grid represents:
X-Sum - the sum of the first X cells in the row/column from that direction, where X is the first number in the row/column. 
Sandwich - the sum of digits between the 1 and 9 in that row or column. 
Skyscrapers - the number of visible skyscrapers in that row or column as seen from that vantage point, given that the numbers within the grid represent the heights of skyscrapers. 
Little Killer - the sum of digits along the indicated diagonal. 
Digits outside the grid will have to be entered to make the answer check work.

description:

Daniel Naroditsky was a phenomenal chess player. He was also a wonderful teacher to thousands of us who watched his streams and his commentaries. He left us too soon and Jonesy's sudoku, For Daniël., was made as a tribute.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/cveeva5iz3

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the total in the top left corner. Digits in box 5 (ie the central 3x3 box) must not see a digit of the same parity a knight’s move away. A “King's move constraint” is only applied to even digits: ie an even digit cannot repeat a king's move away from itself. Cells connected by an X sum to 10. ALL possible Xs are given. title: The Puzzle of the Golden Bear
description:
Here's where you can try Path of The Golden Bear by SuperSport: https://sudokupad.app/90n1ck63vq 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the yellow line into segments, with the same sum. Every pair of adjacent digits on the brown line has different parities. Any three consecutive digits on a blue line contains one from each of the sets {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, {3,6,9}. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of 1. One digit on a black dot is double the other. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5.
Shade cells in the grid gold such that you create an orthogonal path from one white square to the other (cells off of the path should be shaded blue). Along the path, any three consecutive digits must contain one from each of the sets {1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, {7,8,9}. The path must visit exactly three cells in every box it visits. The sum of digits along the path is 110.

title: The Simplest Sudoku Deduction You'll Never See!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After a very eventful day, Simon is simply pleased to have been able to release this video... Computer problems almost prevented our streak of over 5 years of continual content from being maintained but here we are and with a banger of a puzzle too! Jeff Wajes' Crossroads On Another World is an incredibly good sudoku with some simple logic that is, for this solver at least, pretty tough to see.  How did you get on!?

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ut3m32qtmf

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits along a pink line must form a non-repeating group of consecutive digits, but they may appear in any order along the line. Each grey line can be divided into segments of contiguous cells where the digits in each segment sum to 10. These segments cannot overlap, and every cell is part of exactly one segment. Digits may repeat freely on grey lines and within sums.

title: The Hardest "Easy" Sudoku Ever Made!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Some puzzles are so good they should be in a museum. The one, Fallen Mast In A Storm by Marty Sears, would be in an exhibit called "Controversial Sudokus". It was originally on Logic Masters as a 1 star puzzle - meaning it ought to be close to trivial to solve. It DEFINITELY isn't trivial. That said, as we've come to expect from one of the world's very best constructors, it is MAGNIFICENT!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/68spijnw4s

Rules
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, so that no digit repeats in any row or column. Each 3x3 box must be filled using only 3 distinct digits (with repeats being allowed.) Adjacent digits along a turquoise line always have the same difference. This difference must be determined for each turquoise line. 3x3 box borders divide darker blue lines into segments, which each have the same sum. This sum must be determined for each darker blue line.

title: Oops - Something is Bound to go Wrong
description:
Here's where you can try Oops! All Regions by ChinStrap: https://sudokupad.app/7nrei23yv6 
In the main 7x7 grid fill the cells with the digits 1-7 such that there are no repeats in rows or columns. Build nine 7-cell orthogonally connected regions such that digits do not repeat in a region. Regions will cover both inside grid and outer clue cells (but not the given clues or greyed out outside areas). Two solid black region borders in the grid have been given.
Blank outer clue cells are numbered rooms clues and must contain digits for solution check to work. Outside clues in rectangles are given numbered rooms clues. (A fully grey cell is to be left empty.) A clue's digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position. Circles count the number of outside cells that circle's region contains. All possible circles are given.

title: The Return Of The Miracle Loop Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another ludicrous loop sudoku tonight from yttrio who somehow manages to craft these miraculous puzzles on a regular basis. Again there are hardly any clues that have actual numbers in them but the requirements are somehow enough to allow a solution to emerge. Breathtakingly good.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yttrio/japanese-sum-dutch-loop

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a Dutch Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 4). Japanese Sums: Clues outside the grid give the sums of loop segments in the respective row or column, in order, where cells not on the loop separate segments.  A question mark indicates any digit from 0 to 9, but no clue may have a leading zero.  An asterisk denotes an arbitrary number of Japanese sum clues.  This could be zero, one, or multiple.

Today's intro is Jigsaw Falling Into Place by Radiohead.

There are two bonus videos to watch at the moment:

title: Sail The Ship Around The Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today on the birthday of Eccentric Panda and their puzzle Set Sail, which was inspired by Marty Sears' Rat Run series. This is rated at 3* for difficulty but Simon found it a tad harder but it is has some very beautiful and interesting logic baked into it. Simon is also buzzing because this afternoon he had the pleasure of solving a cryptic crossword with one of the most brilliant and engaging of the chess grandmasters... Watch out for a bonus video on the channel soon.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ik85shpid7

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Sail the pirate ship along a path around the island (green cells) starting and ending at the dock (r5,c6). The path must not cross itself but may travel in any direction, orthogonal or diagonal, except directly into the wind coming from the north (the path must not go straight up). The path cannot enter island cells. The path must pass through every ship along the way. Digits must decrease along the path except when boarding a ship or re-entering the dock cell. The digit on a ship is exactly three (3) greater than the previous digit on the path. The dock with the pirate ship does not have to be three greater than the previous digit.  Digits in shallow water (light blue) sum to the value in the corner if given. The path must not enter any shallow water. The digit 3 represents kraken. Kraken do not appear in island (green) cells nor may the path enter them lest your ship be sunk.

title: Some frightening big digits
description:
This is a RELOAD - for some reason the first version of this video did not fully upload correctly to YouTube! Here's where you can try the pesky BIGITs by Sunnyjum: https://sudokupad.app/9ign5knige 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are multiple BIGITs (big digits) hidden in the grid. The numbers 1 to 9 appear as a BIGIT at least once each. An example of each BIGIT number is given above the grid. BIGITs do not overlap each other. At least one cell within each BIGIT contains the number shown by the BIGIT. Each BIGIT consists of a single line colour. Each BIGIT contains at least one given line segment and each given line segment is part of a BIGIT.
All digits on a purple BIGIT form a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (in any order). Adjacent digits on a red line have opposite even/odd parity. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. Adjacent digits on a blue line have a difference of at least 4. Adjacent digits on a yellow line have the same difference (each yellow BIGIT may have its own difference).

Br1312te always comes up with fascinating sudokus. Her last one was a ridiculously clever miracle sudoku and tonight we tackle a puzzle called Global Warming, which introduces a new type of thermometer constraint. It's a lovely idea and really well executed - don't over-complicate things, there's always an easier way :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/tdr0ywy332

Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 black box borders split grey thermometer lines into segments. Starting from the bulb, the sum of each segment must increase. Additionally, within each segment, starting from the original bulb, digits must also increase. Every 2x2 square of cells completely sitting within a red cage must contain a low digit (1,2,3), middle digit (4,5,6) and high digit (7,8,9). Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive. description:
Here's where you can try today's puzzle Tracking The Triptych by pb45: https://sudokupad.app/vldribkmqp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each sequence of three cells along the peach line there is one digit from each of the groups (1,2,3), (4,5,6) and (7,8,9). Boxes 5 and 9 are magic squares, with the same totals in each row, column and 3-cell diagonal. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. title: Yin-Yang-Yong: YIKES!! [Marty Sears]
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's very rare for the same constructor to feature two days running on the channel but we mentioned yesterday that our testers had been having trouble with Yin-Yang-Yong by Marty Sears and we received several emails overnight requesting that we look at it. So here's Simon's attempt... we can confirm it is quite hard ;)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/k4g3ubb8qe

Rules
Fill each cell with a digit from 1-9. For every row 'n' and column 'n' there are exactly 'n' unique digits. The remaining cells are filled with repeats. Divide the grid into three regions. A region is an area of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 area may be entirely in one region. Identical digits may not appear in different regions. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. No two digits anywhere on a yellow line may be consecutive (or the same). Any group of 3 adjacent cells on an orange line must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6) and one high digit (7, 8 or 9). Adjacent digits on a turquoise line always have the same difference. This difference must be determined for each turquoise line. Digits joined by an X sum to 10. A digit on a blue arrow indicates how many region borders (separating two regions) are seen in the direction of the arrow. (Region edges at the outer perimeter of the grid don't count.)

title: PLEASE Just Try This Sudoku. You Won't Regret It.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Kaktuslav does it again with a simply brilliant sudoku tonight called Satellite. This is such a fantastic puzzle to solve with the interlinking of deductions yielding a whole series of Eureka moments. Magical.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/btl00ki232

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every digit on a line of colour C counts how many times that digit appears on all lines of colour C. For example, if there is a 3 on a green line, then there are exactly three 3s on all green lines combined. German whispers (decorated with squares): Adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Parity lines (decorated with circles): Adjacent digits along a red line  have different parity (i.e., one of them is even and the other is odd). Region sum lines (no decorations): 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments of equal sum. The sum may be different for different lines.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The most evil sudoku rules in history make an appearance this evening in an extraordinary collaboration between some of the brightest minds in the world of sudoku (and therefore some of the brightest minds full stop.) The authors are Jeet Sampat, Myxo, dumediat, damasosos92, Agent, SSG, glum_hippo, Playmaker6174, tallcat, Malrog, mnasti2, Piatato, Christounet, MaizeGator and Shintaro Fushida-Hardy and the sudoku is called Lost and Found. Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/d5s2c3o5j3

Fill the grid with digits 1-9 so that each row, column, and box contains exactly 8 unique digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the attached bulb. Digits along a thermometer must not decrease from the bulb end to the tip. Two cells connected by a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Clues outside the grid give the number of digits visible from the clue's position, given that each digit blocks the view of any digits behind it that aren't larger than it. Along a blue line, box borders divide the line into smaller segments with the same sum. Digits can repeat along a segment if allowed by other rules.

There can't be many more consistently excellent sudoku makers in the world than yttrio. Every single one of his puzzles is brilliant so you basically know you're in for an hour of logical joy when you sit down with one :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yttrio/japanese-sum-whisper-loop

Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. title: What If Your Normal Sudoku Technique Fails?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Two mighty names in the world of sudoku collide today and provide a truly exceptional puzzles: it's called Six Hit Wonder and it's the work of ChinStrap and Marty Sears!! And it's fog of war... and, although he's spent a long time in its company, Simon still has no clue how to efficiently solve it :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/hqa07qdm2h?setting-nogrid=true

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. All circles are outside the grid, and each must be filled with a digit. This digit indicates how many digits in its row or column match their distance from the circle. Eg: if a row with a circle at its left-hand end reads 123459786, then all of the digits except 6 and 9 match their distance from the circle, so the circle would contain a 7. A digit in a circle also indicates how many times that digit appears in a circle. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. Any 3 adjacent digits along a hollow peach line must contain one digit from {1, 2, 3}, one digit from {4, 5, 6} and one digit from {7, 8, 9}. Small white dots divide stripy blue lines into at least 2 segments, with the digits on each segment having the same total. If a black dot sits between two digits, then one is double the other.

title: Whoa-oh - We're Halfway There
description:
Here's where you can try Halfway There by James Sinclair: https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/halfway-there 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a 'halver', and halver cells contain a complete set of the digits 1-9. The value of a halver cell is equal to its digit divided by two.
The sum of the values inside each cage is shown, and digits cannot repeat within a cage (but values can). The sum of the values along an arrow equals the value in the connected circle.
Values on thermometers strictly increase from the bulb. Values in cells separated by a V sum to 5. Values in cells separated by an X sum to 10.

Ten women working in the STEM sectors each have four clues for you to discover, one for each of the four grids below. Each clue must have one of its words modified in a specific way to turn it into a new word. The altered sentence will function properly as a cryptic clue, even if its surface no longer makes much sense. Each numbered row contains an answer reading from left to right somewhere within it. title: Simon's Favourite Sudoku Rule!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
More from the sudoku meme that is Top Right Boi today, this time in the form of a puzzle by PhoenixAki. And it's fog of war and it involves the "regional constraint" idea that has led to so many great constructions over the past few months. This one is original and very clever... can you spot its tricks?!

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/3alsxsnq4t

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Most of the grid is covered in grey fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog underneath that digit and possibly in other parts of the grid as well. 
For every clue in the grid that takes up more than one cell, the rightmost cell of the top row of that clue must have its largest digit. Eg a 2x2 cage requires its largest digit in the top right cell. Similarly, a kropki dot needs its larger digit on the top or right (depending on if vertical or horizontal). 
No digit may appear more than once on each clue type. Eg if a cage contains a 2, no other cage can contain 2s. 
Digits on a pink line must form a consecutive set. 
Digits in cages must sum to the small clue, which is given in the leftmost cell of the top row of the cage. 
A black dot between 2 digits indicates that one digit must be double the other. 
Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5. 
Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in its attached circle. 
Grey cells with outward pointing arrows on their edges must be greater than all orthogonally adjacent cells. (For the avoidance of doubt, only the arrowed cells (not the cells they point to) interact with other rules).

title: I'm Stealing These Sudokus For The Louvre!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely epic series of sudokus tonight by DubiousMobius called Fog And Phantoms. Not only are these probably the most beautiful puzzles of all time but they require an innovative shading mechanic to solve them properly. Highly original and absolutely brilliant!

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/t6465th9zv

Rules
Fog and Phantoms: Raising Sails
by DubiousMobius
Your life changed the day you picked up the heavy iron key that now dangles from a chain around your neck.  At first, it was whispers drifting in from cabins you know are empty.  Then strange shapes dancing at the corner of your vision.  Not a very useful affliction for a ship’s pilot.  Each day the whispers grow louder, and the chain grows heavier.  And when the fog rolled in today, something felt different.  The key feels eager.  Those shadows in the mist that only you can see?  They feel substantial in a way they never have before.  Wherever the key is leading you, you know you’re getting close.  You just need to chart the course.

Rules:
Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and 2x3 box.
Dynamic Fog of War:  The grid is partially covered in fog.  Placing the correct digit in a cell will remove the fog from that cell, and may remove fog from other cells as well.  
Phantoms:  Some clues are phantoms and may only reveal themselves as the grid is shaded, for this reason, you may only shade the grid once allowed to by the following rules.
Nurikabe:  Shade the grid in two colors.  One color will represent the sea, and will form a single orthogonally connected set.  The other color will represent islands. You may only shade a cell once you have determined if it is island or sea.
Each group of orthogonally connected island cells will contain at least one cell with a digit equal to the number of cells in that island.  All such cells will be marked with a circle, although that circle may not be visible until the fog has lifted and the cell is shaded.  Every 2x2 portion of the grid will contain at least one island cell.
Arrows:  Some cells with circles also have lines attached to those circles.  The digits along those lines will sum to the digit placed in the attached circle cell.  Additionally, the cell at the tip of an arrow will always be part of the sea, and will count the number of island cells that can be found in the 8 cells surrounding it.  Arrows only move orthogonally, and cannot branch, except at a circle.  
Note:  Phantoms are tricksy, and will cause some clues to temporarily disappear when the pen tool is open.  Don't worry, the clues will return when the tool is closed, and any markings you have done in the meantime will remain.

Normal sudoku rules apply. Any set of three adjacent digits on a teal line contain one of 147, one of 258, and one of 369. title: This Just Should Not Work... (And Yet It Does!)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight's sudoku is about to turn 1 and, just before its birthday, we have a crack at it. It's called Bread And Pie, it's by Myxo and - as usual with this constructor - it is a VERY special puzzle indeed. And it'll make you hungry :)

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/slicedsudoku/breadandpie

Rules
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells, such that every cell is part of exactly one region. Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in each row, column and region. Brown clues to the left and above the grid are Sandwich clues: They indicate the sum of the digits between the 1 and 9 in that row or column. In rows and columns that have a Sandwich clue, all the digits between the 1 and 9 must be in the same region, and the 1 and 9 must not belong to that region. All regions that do not touch the edge of the grid are Pie filling: Black clues below the grid indicate the sum of the digits within Pie filling in that column.

title: MantaRay and the Joy of Maths
description:
Try this intriguing puzzle called Some Balancing Product by MantaRay here: https://sudokupad.app/e7ssrztfgn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 region within the puzzle is entirely shaded or unshaded. Within a cage, digits do not repeat. The cage may show its sum. Every cage in the puzzle contains at least one cell of each shading. Within a cage, the sum of the unshaded cells is equal to the product of the shaded cells. For clarity, if only one shaded cell exists within a cage then the cage's product value is that cell's digit. No two cages have the same sum/product value.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
IcyFruit is the answer! And in this video Simon tackles their latest sudoku, Overlooked - which uses the "lighthouse" constraint IcyFruit invented a few weeks ago. It is, of course, a quite brilliant puzzle, which also has the ability to make this solver of it feel absolutely inadequate!!

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/7t1yva729p

title: Sudoku Lines that Lie!
description:
Here's where you can try Escape the Foggy Liar by PhoenixAki: https://sudokupad.app/eiqitcx105 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Purple lines are liar lines. Cages touched by a liar line may or may not sum to their given total. The number of lying cages per liar line is specified by the grid's central digit (R5C5), which must be deduced. Liar lines do not branch or cross each other. If a cage is touched by a liar line, all cells of the cage will be touched by the line (in other words, cages are either completely filled with liar line segments, or they have 0 liar line segments).
Cells in dotted-line cages (if they tell the truth) sum to the number shown. Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5.Digits on a thin grey arrow sum to the number in its attached circle. Cells connected by a black dot must have one digit be double the other. Cells connected by an X or V sum to 10 or 5 respectively. Thick grey lines are thermometers which require digits to increase from the bulb end. Placing correct digits will progressively clear away the fog in the grid, at least in that cell and often in other parts of the grid as well. Some cells have green arrows on their edges/corners, these are purely cosmetic.

title: Bittersweet Symphony Sudoku 🐍
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Over two years ago the constructor Lutterot released this sudoku "Serpent With A Lisp". We didn't hear too much about it at the time but it's been recommended to us recently and it's FANTASTIC. Not too tricky but with beautiful and original logic throughout. You won't regret giving it a try!

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/czjmyqmipr

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that they form a snake ie a one-cell wide string of orthogonally connected cells. The snake doesn't touch itself orthogonally, its head and tail are the grey circles, and it visits each 3x3 box at least once. The snake only bends and ends on the digits 1 and 9. The straight parts of the snake are thermometers ie digits are in increasing order along each straight part. The white circles are not on the snake and each contains a different digit. These digits indicate how many of their orthogonally and diagonally adjacent cells are snake cells.

title: The Lowest Rating But Could This Be 'Sudoku Of The Year'?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's been a long time (if ever) since we've featured a puzzle with a rating this "low" (80%)! We can only assume this one (Think Inside The... by Kennet's Dad) has been trolled because this is absolutely brilliant from start to finish. Astonishingly clever and simply wonderful. 100% in fact!!

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/cki7pvc7ts

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. No domino in the grid can contain digits summing to 10. There is some fog in the grid; placing a correct digit might remove it. No guessing is required. Digits in a grey box cannot repeat. There are lines in the grid that connect boxes; the digits in a box are summed to arrive at a value. That value applies to the following rules: 1) Zipper: when box values equidistant from the centre box on a pink line are summed together, they are equal to the centre box's value on that line. The centre box is notated by a pink circle; 2) Modular: every run of three boxes on a teal line must have a different remainder when divided by 3 (ie one value from each of 0 mod(3), 1 mod(3), and 2 mod(3)); 3) Box values on a purple line make up at a set of consecutive, non-repeating values; 4) The box values connected by a blue line must be the same; 5) Box values joined by a white dot have a difference of 1.

title: Can YOU Count To N?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's been a little while since we did a chaos construction on the channel but we put that right tonight by attempting mellowrobinson's fantastic Chaos Construc - to - N. This has a very original ruleset but this gives rise to some wonderful logic and an almost miracle-esque quality to the solve.

Please also check out our new app: Classic Sudoku 2 (links below)!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/g7mtvua99q

Rules
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Fill every cell with a digit 1-9 without repeats in any row, column, or region. A clue outside Row or Column N indicates the sum of all digits up to the cell that contains the digit N. (The digit N itself is not included in the sum.) Eg The 24 clue in row 4 gives the sum of the digits up to (but not including) the 4 in that row. A question mark (?) stands for any number greater than zero. Additionally, all digits up to the digit N are in the same region, and the digit N is in a different region.

title: Is This The Second Great Sudoku Series?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Two weeks ago we attempted the first of gdc's "infection"-themed sudokus - it was great but we hadn't realised it was the first of a series. Today we try the second - Under The Microscope - a 4/5 difficulty puzzle which is every bit as interesting as the first... Roll on No. 3!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/qqfj59akio

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Each digit matching its box number is an "inoculation site". Each row and column contains an inoculation site. They are infected. Infected cells infect every orthogonally adjacent cell with a smaller digit. Infections keep spreading until no infected cell has a smaller uninfected orthogonal neighbour. (Every infected cell can be traced back to one or more inoculation sites.) All uninfected cells form one orthogonally connected area. Each orthogonally connected group of infected cells touches the grid's edge. A digit in a blue circle is uninfected and counts the number of infected cells in its 8 surrounding cells. Green lines connect 2 infected digits that differ by 5 or more. Pink dots join consecutive uninfected digits.

Here's the incredible sudoku Simon & Mark tackled in Stratford at the weekend:

title: This Really is Twisted
description:
Here's where you can attempt Twisted by ThePedallingPianist: https://sudokupad.app/f4e7jjoad0 
In each NxN grid, place the digits 1-N once in every row, column and box; in the slanted 6x6 grid, digits should be entered only in the middle of cells. Each arrow contains a 2-digit number, with the 10s digit on the shaft and the 1s digit on the head; the number on an arrow gives the sum of the first X digits seen in a straight line in the indicated direction, where X is the first digit seen. Arrows only see cells that contain digits, i.e. blank spaces, such as those not belonging to any grid, are not seen.

title: The Hidden Arts Of Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
So much to say... Stratford was incredible - THANK YOU to everyone who attended. Tonight's puzzle is also incredible: yttrio's Island Sum Lines - well worth its 99% rating. Oh and we're streaming again tonight at 10pm UK time! Oh and the outro to today's video is Simon's reading of the first part of Under Milk Wood. Oh and the musical intro is Peace by O.A.R. Oh and yesterday's astonishing puzzle from Stratford, Third Order Logic by Die Hard is also linked below.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/f9wcvtflo1

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Nurikabe: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected (water), but no 2x2 area is entirely shaded; groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands. An island may be of size 1. Every cell with a circle clue is unshaded, and each island contains exactly one circle cell.  The digit in this circle cell gives the size of the island.  Note that an island may occupy a full 2x2 area (unlike water). Digits may not repeat within an island. Every blue line must contain at least one shaded and at least one unshaded cell. Switching between shaded and unshaded cells divides each line into segments with the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by other rules.

Die Hard's Third Order Logic:

title: The Sudoku Graveyard Of Solvers' Hopes!!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
On Halloween for the last several years we've tackled one of fjam's Graveyard sudoku series. These puzzles are seriously clever and very challenging. Today's is called The Graveyard Of Emptiness and Simon thinks it would be reasonable easy to make a logical error when solving this one... but did he?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9gk44l9w5x

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell in each row, column and region is a nullifier cell. Nullifier cells have a value of zero. In graves (cages), values must sum to the day, month or year of the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. Escape the graveyard by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path between the green and red cells. The path may not cross the highest or lowest values in a grave.

Marty's extraordinarily creative brain has come up with yet another stone-cold classic puzzle tonight in the form of Colour Coordinated Differences. It's only a 2/5 difficulty sudoku but don't think it's a pushover - it's got all the guile and wit you'd expect from Mr Sears!

Normal sudoku rules apply. The two digits on an arrow give the coordinates of a particular target cell somewhere in the grid. The digit on the arrow's shaft indicates the target cell's row, and the digit on the arrowhead indicates the target cell's column. title: This Sudoku Is Total Genius.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Kaktuslav's sudokus have proved over the last few months to be of such high quality that Mark was considering this one for our Stratford slot coming up on Sunday. It's called Modular Zigzag and is apparently 2/5 on the difficulty scale. Simon thinks he may have missed something here but this is an extraordinary puzzle (where even knowledge of Kaktuslav's previous tricks may not be enough!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/urooueeutg

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat along the marked diagonal. Every 2×2 square of cells must contain all three possible remainders modulo 3 (i.e. at least one digit from each of the sets {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, and {3,6,9}). Draw a path starting in the top-left corner cell and finishing in the bottom-right corner cell, visiting every 3×3 box at least once. In a single step, the path may move only east (→) or southwest (↙). Any three consecutive digits along the path must have three different remainders modulo 3. Box borders divide the path into segments; each segment is a renban, i.e. it must contain consecutive, non-repeating integers in any order.

title: Sudoku Stops The Pandemic!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An original and brilliant sudoku tonight from gdc called Patient Zeroes in which our job is to help stop the spead of a deadly virus. We're seeing some incredible Halloween-themed puzzles already this year (with a few more to come!) and this is right up there (indeed it has a perfect rating!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/27v1lv24c3

Dr. Norma L. Dokes! A virus is spreading and causes people to eat each others brains! Please perform some measurements in the village and bring the results to the hospital. We need to see how severe the spread is. But be careful - It is highly contagious!

NORMA L DOKES - Normal sudoku rules apply.

INFECTIONS - The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order, 1 to 9. Each digit matching its own box number is a 'patient zero'. Each row and column contains a 'patient zero'. Patient zeroes are infected. Infected cells infect every orthogonally adjacent cell with a smaller digit. Infections keep spreading until no infected cell has a smaller uninfected orthogonal neighbour. (Every infected cell can be traced back to one or more patient zeroes.)

PATH - Draw a 1-cell wide path from the doctor () to the hospital (). The path only moves orthogonally and may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The path may not contain infected cells.

MICROSCOPES () are on the path and count the number of infected cells in the (up to 9) surrounding cells.

KROPKI TABLETS (white dots) join consecutive uninfected digits.

title: The Perfect Logic
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Is there a constructor more reliable to produce a beautiful loop puzzle than yttrio? We sincerely doubt it. This one, Same Sum Entropic Loop, has the distinction of a perfect 100% rating despite only being of average difficulty - this is SO hard to achieve but it's well deserved. This is gorgeous.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yttrio/same-sum-entropic-loop

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as an entropic line. Each set of three adjacent digits along the loop must be one low [123], one medium [456], and one high digit [789]. The loop must enter every cell of every cage. The sum of all digits in any given cage is the same for every cage (that sum must be determined by the solver).

title: When The Secret Of Sudoku Doesn't Work...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A breathtakingly clever puzzle tonight from ChinStrap called Accounting Circles Tessellation. The rules are surprisingly simple but the implications need to be thought through carefully. It's got some fascinating depth to it this one!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zeu960ln92?setting-nogrid=true

Rules:
Fill each cell with a digit from 1-9. Cells sharing an edge can't have the same digit. Each horizontal row and vertical column contains a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (like 23456) in any order. The blue circles and red squares combined form a complete set of the digits 1-9. A digit in a blue circle indicates how many of that digit appear in the entire puzzle. A digit in a red square indicates that the digit does not appear exactly that many times in the puzzle. EG if there were four 4s and six 5s in the grid, the 4 would go into a circle and the 5 in a square.

title: One Computer Trick Solves This Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A real surprise tonight in the form of this puzzle, Bits And Arrows by Jonesy. It has a very unusual ruleset that might concern you at first glance and yet it's actually incredibly natural and quite lovely when you see how it works. We predict there will be some very quick times by computer programmers on this one!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/wut7orsq8b

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A binary code is a sequence of numbers (“bits”) that are either on or off. In this puzzle, Odd digits represent bits that are 'OFF'(O) and Even digits represent bits that are 'ON'(E). This gives us the following representation of the digits 1-9:
1 → OOOE
2 → OOEO
3 → OOEE
4 → OEOO
5 → OEOE
6 → OEEO
7 → OEEE
8 → EOOO
9 → EOOE
The digit in an arrow cell dictates the parity (odd or even) of its four orthogonal neighbours. These four neighbours must match the binary code of the digit with the small arrow. The arrow points to the first bit of the binary code. (read from left to right.) The full code must wrap around the central cell clockwise. Eg If a 6 is placed in an arrow cell, its code is OEEO. Therefore, its four neighbours (starting from the arrow direction, moving clockwise) must be Odd, Even, Even, Odd.

(If you are unfamiliar with binary numbers please watch Simon discuss the rules.)

*** NUMBERPHILE VIDEO ***
There is a new  @numberphile  video featuring Cracking The Cryptic. Thanks so much to Brady Haran. You can find it here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eB0-vG6rSM4

title: IcyFruit's Fog Of War Sudoku = Astonishing
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
And now for something completely different... IcyFruit is perhaps the most terrifying of all constructors and Simon is justifiably a bit scared when he sees IcyFruit's name by a sudoku. But one thing you know is that an IcyFruit puzzle is an EVENT. They seem to all have unusual logic that makes you think in new ways. Lighthouses is the one we attempt today and it's everything you might expect. Magnificent.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/cn5h6c34mo

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partly covered in fog. Placing correct digits may clear fog revealing other clues. No guessing is required. A digit in a square indicates the total number of digits smaller than itself that it 'sees' in all the four cardinal directions (North, East, South, West) along its row and column. In each direction, it 'sees' ALL digits smaller than itself until vision is blocked by a digit greater than itself or the edge of the grid. (For clarity it does not see itself). If a black dot separates two digits, one of those digits is double the other.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a "doubler", and doubler cells contain a complete set of the digits 1-9. A cell's value is equal to its digit, except that a doubler cell may or may not have a value equal to its digit multiplied by two. The same cell may have different values for the purpose of different clues.
The sum of the values inside each cage is shown. The sum of the values along an arrow is equal to the value in the connected circle. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum of values. Along a green line, values differ from their neighbors by at least 5. title: But This Sudoku Grid Is Practically EMPTY??
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Kaktuslav has been wowing us for months now and we had a strong recommendation to try this puzzle, Picking Blackcurrants. Only then did it emerge that hardly anyone has managed to solve it... This certainly has a miracle quality and it's an absolutely remarkable piece of construction.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/qx6r0v9p4f

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 

Draw a directed path through the centres of some cells in the grid, starting in one blue circle and ending in the other. The path may move only orthogonally north (↑), orthogonally east (→), or diagonally southwest (↙), and it may not visit any cell more than once. The path must function both as an entropic line and as a region sum line. Every black dot in the grid must be crossed by the path. A white dot joins two cells - neither of these cells may be visited by the path. 

Along an Entropic line, every set of three consecutive cells along the line must contain one low digit (1,2,3), one middle digit (4,5,6), and one high digit (7,8,9). 

Along a Region sum line. the 3x3 box borders divide the line into segments; and all such segments must have the same sum. 

A white dot between two digits means they must be consecutive. If two digits are separated by a black dot one is double the other. One of the dots contains an inequality sign pointing to the smaller digit.

description:
Here's where you can attempt Junk Drawer by Sotehr: https://sudokupad.app/pdnc0ckv87 
Place the digits 1-9 at most once in every row, column, and 3x3 box. There are nine 3x3 boxes, which overlap at the dashed lines. Adjacent cells on a green line have a minimum difference of 5. Adjacent cells on an orange line have a minimum difference of 4. Any three adjacent digits on a teal line cannot be from the same set of modulo 3 residuals, that is {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, or {3,6,9}. Any three adjacent digits on a peach line cannot be from the same set of low, middle, or high digits, that is {1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, or {7,8,9}. Cells separated by a black dot have values in a ratio of 1:2. Cells separated by a white dot have values with a difference of one. Cells separated by an X sum to 10; cells separated by a V sum to 5.

title: How Easy Is This Fog Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Br1312te returns to the channel tonight with a lovely Halloween-themed puzzle called Creatures In The Dynamic Fog. This is fog sudoku at its best and perhaps a smidge harder than the 2/5 difficulty rating suggests.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ey3tqoay3j

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply, but once again strange things are afoot... 
Fog has filled the land, thicker than ever before, and within it, lurk many Creatures of the night!
Yet fear not! If you can find them, friendly Wisps will aid you in navigating the fog. There is one Wisp in each row, column, and 3x3 box, marked by a pale blue dot. Cells containing a Wisp contain either their row, column or box number (read in normal reading order). No two Wisps can contain the same digit. Fog cleared by Wisps leaves an eerie blue light.
The Monsters:
Zombies: marked by a green dot, zombies have an infectious bite. Orthogonally adjacent cells are even when the zombie's number is even, or odd when the zombie's number is odd.
Vampires: marked by a red dot, vampires suck the power from their victims. Orthogonally adjacent cells sum up to the vampire's number.
Headless Horsemen: marked by an orange dot, horsemen have a knight's reach. Cells a chess-knight's move away from the horseman can't contain the same digit as the horseman's number.
Poltergeists: marked by a grey dot, poltergeists throw everything into disarray. Orthogonally adjacent cells are either all higher than the poltergeist's number, or all lower.
Fog: the land is covered in dynamic fog. Putting in correct digits will clear the fog for that cell. Finding a Wisp will clear more fog. No guessing is required. The monster under your bed will know if you cheat!

The intro today is Vincent by Don McLean. RIP Daniel Naroditsky.

Here's where you can have a go at Surprising Stars by Ryan Adams: https://sudokupad.app/i3a78tp386 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. All possible X clues have been given. Digits in a cage sum to the total in the top-left corner of the cage. The fog in the puzzle will clear once all occurrences of the missing digit have been placed.

title: This Sudoku Is Not Very Easy!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Taiga by IceFruit remains one of the most challenging sudokus we've solved in the channel's history. Qodec decided it would be a good idea to make a puzzle with the same ruleset but add his own twists... which was very kind of him. This result is challenging and brilliant (and not for the faint hearted!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/g248qi5g6d

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each row, column, and 3x3 box contains two 'indexer' cells: a 'row indexer' and a 'column indexer'. The digit in a row indexer gives the position of the column indexer in that row. The digit in a column indexer gives the position of the row indexer in that column. Positions are counted left-to-right in rows and top-to-bottom in columns . Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the upper left corner, if given. Indexer cells cannot appear in cages.

The intro today is another piece of Liam Clancy's And The Band Played Waltzing Matilda.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Outside clues are Sandwich clues, indicating the sum of the cells between the lowest & highest values (usually 1 & 9) seen in their row or column. Cells across white dots contain consecutive values. Cells across black dots contain one value double the other (1:2 ratio).

title: Ghosts In The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Halloween is approaching fast and we've received a lot of puzzles on that theme so we're starting early with James Kopp's Ghosts In The Fog - a clever and interesting sudoku full of lovely logic.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/mm4b2w1a65

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Adjacent cells cannot sum to 10. Grey lines are palindromes that read the same in both directions. If two digits are separated by a black dot one is double the other. Not all possible black dots are necessarily shown. A cell marked with a grey circle contains an odd digit. No guessing is required.

The intro today is Liam Clancy's And The Band Played Waltzing Matilda.  (A longer version was in the outro but copyright struck.)

*** NUMBERPHILE VIDEO ***
We've just found out that there is a new  @numberphile  video featuring Cracking The Cryptic. Thanks so much to Brady Haran. You can find it here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eB0-vG6rSM4

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage has a two-digit total to be placed by the solver inside the cage. title: Can You Solve This Before Time Runs Out?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
That was the task facing Simon tonight as he attempted a 100%-rated sudoku, Shanghai Skyline by Black_Doom! This is a BRILLIANT puzzle with some fascinating ideas from start to finish but it is terrifying to do it against a hidden clock!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/6hc3f9hbqu

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. If two digits are separated by a black dot one digit is double the other. Additionally, a black dot always separates a shaded and an unshaded cell. Not all dots are necessarily given. Shaded digits in the grid represent skyscrapers of that height, with taller skyscrapers obscuring smaller ones. A clue outside the grid shows the number of all visible skyscrapers from the clue's direction. Unshaded digits do not affect the outside clues.

title: A Sudoku With Only 3 Given Digits - Or Is It?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The return of Aad van de Wetering tonight with his new puzzle Who's Afraid Of 13! It's a classic Aad sudoku, full of lovely logically steps and, if you don't get a phone call in the middle of it, it's a smooth solve ;)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/s34y05j3cz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of two orthogonal neighbours is at most 13 (ie no domino in the grid can sum to more than 13). The sum of two 'point symmetric' cells is always 10. (Point symmetric cells are pairs that are mirror images of each other across the exact centre of the 9x9 grid (the middle of the central 3x3 box). ie Rotating the grid 180° around this central point maps a cell directly onto its symmetric partner). So, for example, r7c1's symmetric counterpart is r3c9.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. The segment sum is a concatenation of the two digits on the extreme ends (e.g. a line with segments summing to 36 will have a 3 on one end and a 6 on the other). title: The Miracle 5x5 Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The last week of puzzles on the channel has been extraordinary and we want this incredible run to continue so we're attempted a sudoku called Full Rank 20.JV - Mod 3 by Justin Vitanza. It's really quite amazing that these lines create a solvable puzzle and yet...

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/n197tdko1c

Rules:
Within the main grid (inside the thick border), fill every cell with a digit from 1-5 such that digits do not repeat in a row or column. Full Rank: A value in an external cell represents the rank of the number formed by reading the digits in that row or column from that direction, where (1) is the lowest such row or column and (20) is the highest. Mod 3 lines: Any 3 adjacent cells along a line must contain a complete set of residues modulo 3 (there will be a residue 0, 1, and 2, with residue defined as the remainder of the cell value after dividing by 3). N.B. If two ranks are tied, the value in both external cells is the lower of the two ranks being shared. For example, if the lowest four ranks are "12453", "13524", "13524" and "15432", the values in the relevant external cells would be (1), (2), (2) and (4) respectively.

title: The World's Hardest Jigsaw.
description:
*** NUMBERPHILE TODAY ***
We've just found out that there is a new @numberphile video today featuring Cracking The Cryptic. Thanks so much to Brady Haran. You can find it here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eB0-vG6rSM4

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
You've seen those jigsaw puzzles which consist of only sky or baked beans? They look pretty difficult it's fair to say but they're a walk in the park compared to this sudoku jigsaw by Kaktuslav. We only have to place 49 digits but good luck with that :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/y9rdy75smw

Rules:
Place each digit 1–7 exactly once in each row and column of the 7×7 grid. The grid is covered by 16 jigsaw pieces. Each piece covers the same sum. If a cell is covered by more than one piece, its digit is split between those pieces proportionally to the area covered. Eg if R4C4 contains the digit x, then this cell contributes ¼·x to the sum of the piece covering R3C3, ½·x to the sum of the piece covering R3C5, and ¼·x to the sum of the piece covering R5C5.

Tonight's musical intro is Mess Is Mine by Vance Joy.

title: You Can't Have More Fun In 25 Cells!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What to say about tonight's sudoku... one of the most fun puzzles we've can remember in a long time. We won't spoil anything in the introduction but we think you'll all remember Losing Your Marbles by ThePedallingPianist :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/nw96zee4xk
If you are playing on a mobile then please use this link:
https://sudokupad.app/gzuqo7nzg1

Rules:
Divide the grid into five regions, each containing 5 orthogonally connected cells. Place a digit from 1-5 in each cell so that digits do not repeat in a row, column or region. 'Marbles' join cells that share a region, and no two marbles share a region. Draw a 'Marble Run' from any cell in the top row to a 3 in a bottom corner. The marble run line is formed entirely of L-shaped line segments: a downwards movement (to gain speed) and then a horizontal movement of the same distance. Adjacent cells on the Marble Run are in different regions. Use the pentomino information provided around the grid to discover a secret code and enter it at the top of the grid to reveal the final rule.

title: This Sudoku Must Be Impossible?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Myxo is a constructor whose planet-sized brain has come up with some extraordinary puzzles over the years. This one, Wanddeko, is one of his hardest and MOST extraordinary. The amount of information available seems wholly inadequate for there to be a unique solution... let alone one findable by a human being... luckily we're not sure whether Simon qualifies...

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/2004fp6a0r

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. A black dot sits between two digits where one is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. Inequality signs between two cells point towards the smaller digit.

Normal sudoku rules apply. title: Where  Pinball Collides with Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can try Extra Ball by Blobz: https://sudokupad.app/blobz/extra-ball 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat, and sum to the clue in the top left corner. Four pinballs start at the top of the grid, trace a path around the table, and finish at the bottom of the grid. The number of cells visited by each path (including start and end cells) is given in the associated end cell.
Each ball may move sideways or downwards (diagonally or straight) any number of times, but may NOT move upwards, on its journey. Balls may not enter any cell more than once. Balls may not enter a grey shaded cell or a "bumper" cell (given digit). Each ball must visit both of the "target" cages (shaded yellow) along the way.
No path shares any cells, and while they may cross other paths diagonally, no path crosses itself. Box borders divide the BLUE path into segments with the same sum. Adjacent digits along the GREEN path must differ by at least 5. Digits along the RED path must be 5 or higher.

title: This "Sudoku" Is An Actual Miracle.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon opens tonight's puzzle live - it turns out to be by ThePedallingPianist and Michael Lefkowitz (Juggler) and it's one of the strangest and most wonderful things you'll ever see in puzzle space. Full Rank Tessellation is its official title but we'll just called it The Miracle Puzzle.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/q83v6obrdn

Rules:
Fill each cell (octagons and squares) with a digit from 1-9. Cells sharing an edge can't have the same digit. Each horizontal row and vertical column contains a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (like 2345678) in any order. A value in an external cell represents the rank of the number formed by reading the digits in the indicated 5-cell diagonal from that direction, where (1) is the lowest such row or column and (20) is the highest. If two ranks are tied, the value in both external cells is the lower of the two ranks being shared.Eg, if the lowest four ranks are '12453', '13524', '13524' and '15432', the values in the relevant external cells would be (1), (2), (2) and (4) respectively.

title: This EVIL Sudoku Should Carry A Health Warning!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears is a puzzle making genius and his sudokus are usually clever, witty and relatively approachable. This one is clever, witty and absolutely NOT approachable :) It was apparently made as a "present" for fellow constructor Lake (who invented the RBC rule used) and it's called Gross Misconduct. Good luck!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/rvzdb6nk86
Or, if playing on Mobile, please use this link:
https://sudokupad.app/ln6peautd7

Rules:
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, plus the letters R, B and C, so that no letter or digit repeats in any row, 3x4 box, or column.
3x4 boxes are numbered 1-12 in normal reading order.
The value of an R equals its row number.
The value of a B equals its box number.
The value of a C equals its column number.
BLACK KROPKI: If two values are joined by a black dot, one is double the other.
RENBAN: Values along a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive sequence, arranged in some order.
GERMAN WHISPER: Adjacent values on a green line have a difference of at least 5.
ARROWS: Values along an arrow sum to the value in the attached circle.
SAME DIFFERENCE: Adjacent values on a turquoise line have the same difference. This difference may be different for different turquoise lines.

title: One Of The Most Fun Puzzles For Months!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon absolutely loves this new sudoku by Kaktuslav. It's called Hamiltonian Killer Thermo and involves an innovative ruleset and the most beautiful ideas in the solve path. Phenomenal.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/wcq666h4y2

Rules:
Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row and each column of the grid. Draw a directed path that moves orthogonally between cell centres and visits every cell of the grid exactly once. Each of the 27 cages can be entered by the path at most once (i.e. the path must visit all cells of a cage in a single continuous run before leaving it). The path acts as a thermometer with respect to cage totals: as the path moves away from its starting cell, the sums of the cages it visits must strictly increase. Digits may not repeat within a cage.

title: Each Shape Must Have A "Top Right" Cell!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Occasionally on Saturdays we enjoy an excursion into non-sudoku puzzles but only when those puzzles are exceptionally good. Today is one such Saturday - we try Shintaro Fushida-Hardy's Top Right Boi: a region-building puzzle in which every shape MUST have a top right cell... 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/5dhw33gsql

Rules:
Standard Fillomino rules apply: divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells, and place a number in every cell equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells that region contains). Regions of the same size cannot share an edge. Some numbers are already given. Every Fillomino region contains a unique cell (called the Top Right Boi!): looking at the region, there can be no cell in the region that is either further to the east or further to the north than the Top Right Boi cell.

title: Hedge Fun
description:
Here's where you can attempt Hedge Fun by vfig: https://sudokupad.app/8zj1gqnxkd 
Or here in PuzzleTV software: https://tinyurl.com/HedgesFun 
Oliver is lost in the hedge maze, and must find a way out. Normal sudoku rules apply.
Draw a path between cell centers from Oliver's starting point in The Origin to one of the exits at the cardinal points of the grid. The path cannot branch, nor cross itself, nor enter any cell more than once. The path may go orthogonally or diagonally, but must never touch any hedges (green walls). Adjacent digits along the path must differ by at least 5.
The hedge maze must be mapped out by placing all nine pieces into the grid, one into each box, without overlapping. The pieces may not be rotated or flipped. One piece has been placed already and may not be moved. Hedges do not need to match up between adjacent pieces.
All the fountains (blue circles) must be reassembled by joining two halves. The path may not go diagonally through a fountain.
Sumflowers only grow between a pair of digits that sum to 10. Oliver visits exactly one of the cells beside each sumflower, but must never visit both its cells.
Apple trees only grow between a pear of digits that sum to 5. Oliver is very hungry, and must collect all the apples from the maze by visiting each cell with an apple. A tree without fruit does not have to be visited.

description:

Snackdoku Title Puzzle by Panthera: https://sudokupad.app/tkn1nytyis or (cookie version) https://sudokupad.app/a8g3wxoga1
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
Hairgrips by Malrog: https://tinyurl.com/MalrogFood or (cake version): https://sudokupad.app/bpxqqx422g
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a thermometer must strictly increase from the bulb end. Digits in a grey square must be even. Digits on a black dot must be in a 2:1 ratio.
Taste the Rainbow  by Sandra & Nala : https://sudokupad.app/7hi72ze6yz or (cake version) https://sudokupad.app/2bmc4e9lie
Normal sudoku rules apply. Arrows have been detached from their circles. Some arrow tips have been detached from their shaft piece(s) as well, which now appear as a loose line in the grid. Each arrow has its own color. Elements of the same color belong to the same arrow.  Digits on the detached arrows must sum to digit in the corresponding circle. 
Austrian Heat by Palfly Kampling: https://sudokupad.app/c98uker73j or (cake version)  https://sudokupad.app/izbozr9wp5
Normal sudoku rules apply. The lines with bulbs can be either Thermometers or Odd German Whispers (or possibly both): Digits along a thermometer must increase from bulb to tip; For an Odd German Whisper: Digits in cells directly connected by a line must differ by at least 5. If a line can only be a German Whisper the digit placed in the bulb must be odd.
Irregular SudoCake by I Love Sleeping: https://sudokupad.app/eq9yb6t05e or (cake version) https://sudokupad.app/0s2fhkkfg5
Fill each row, column and region with the numbers 1-9 once each. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Region borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum. Digits along a red line alternate between odd and even.
Clarification: The lines don't go on top of each other.

title: "No Guessing Is Required": The Fog Sudoku Challenge
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Kaktuslav's Giza was a sensational puzzle (see yesterday's Bonus video) so, when we saw another of his Fog sudokus, we knew we had to try it. YouTube won't let us type the title but that's not so important... what you need to know is that this is an amazing solving experience!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/3cm1bpm2jv

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin-Yang: Shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. A shaded cell containing digit x has value x+10; an unshaded cell has value equal to its digit. Region sum lines: Blue lines are divided into segments by box borders. All segments along a single line must have the same sum of values (this sum may differ between lines). Cells connected by a black dot have values, one of which is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals their own cell and may also lift fog elsewhere in the grid. No guessing is required.

title: A Viewer Solves Sudoku With Simon: Episode 8
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Last month, Michael won our competition and, very kindly, agreed to make a sudoku video with Simon.  Mark selected the puzzle Giza by Kaktuslav.  This is another amazing puzzle from Kaktuslav - who seems an expert at setting perfect sudokus for these viewer solves!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/2vnskp4zft

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every constraint in the puzzle is a straight line: every horizontal line is a renban, every vertical line is a German whisper, and every diagonal line is a region sum line. Different lines of the same type do not share cells. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is required. A renban line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Adjacent digits on a German whisper line must differ by at least 5. Box borders divide a region sum line into segments each of which must have the same total (different lines may have different totals).

title: This Puzzle Has Been Solved 3 Times. Can He Make It 4?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A crazy sudoku tonight from SSG called Lines Lines. The rules are mad, the idea is mad but the puzzle itself... well it's totally incredible. Only 3 solves were registered before Simon's attempt... will he make it 4?

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/qhx16aqc8i

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
Lines: Draw two non-branching lines in the grid - one green and one blue - that connect the centres of cells. The lines must only move orthogonally (i.e. not diagonally). Neither line may touch itself, even diagonally. The two lines may, however, touch or cross each other, but only at discrete points (i.e.if the two lines meet in the centre of one cell they cannot continue in the same direction into the centre of their next cell). The green line must form a closed loop; and, the ends of the blue line may not be on any intersections with the green line.
Projected Sums: Clues outside the grid give the sum of digits on lines along the indicated direction. Coloured clues count only the line of that colour. Black clues count digits on both lines. If both lines pass through a cell, that cell's digit only counts once in the projected sum.
German Whispers: Along the green line adjacent digits must differ by at least 5.
Modular Lines: Along the blue line, in every run of three cells, the three digits in those cells must each have a different remainder when divided by 3.
Clones: The two cages are exact clones of each other. They contain the same digits in the same positions and they contain the same lines (including colour) in the same positions. Digits may repeat within the clone if otherwise allowed.
