title: I LOVE This Setter's Sudoku Puzzles.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolute banger tonight from Scojo called Loopy Circles. This is a really fascinating puzzle with so many clever ideas involved in its logic. Well worth thinking about and well worth attempting :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/2vyqqhy6ky

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Draw a 1 cell wide loop through the centers of some cells. The loop only moves orthogonally and cannot branch or touch itself, even diagonally. A digit in a circle on the loop indicates how many circles on the loop contain that digit. Similarly, a digit in a circle off the loop indicates how many circles off the loop contain that digit. Black dots separate digits where one is double the other. Additionally, exactly one cell touching a black dot is on the loop, and the other is off the loop. White dots separate consecutive digits. Additionally, the two cells touching a white dot are either both on the loop, or both off the loop. Not all dots are necessarily given.

*** MONDAY'S BLUE PRINCE STREAM ***

title: 47 Cells Of Lines And An 8??!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The maths professor Dorlir returns to the channel this evening with one of his top 3 sudokus - which is a high bar indeed! None other than Marty Sears has recommended this one too and with good reason. This is a brilliant puzzle with one or two moments of total genius in it.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zy1s9y2qi8

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Every run of five digits on the yellow line contains a digit from {1,6}, a digit from {2,7}, a digit from {3,8}, a digit from {4,9}, and the digit 5. The grey line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap. Digits an equal distance from the centre of the purple line must sum to the digit in the centre of that purple line. Adjacent digits along the green line must differ by at least 5. Digits on the pink line form a set of consecutive integers in some order.

description:

8x8 Latin Square: Fill the grid with the digits 1-8 so there are no repeats in any row or column. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in large white circles must appear in the four surrounding cells.

Deduce a set of four values, and fill the 4x4 grid with them so that values do not repeat in a row, column, or box.  Values separated by a large white dot (quadruple clue) are consecutive. title: Stop this Bomb Going off!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Bomb Defusal by Deckatron: https://sudokupad.app/0pzyej3gwf 
A bomb is set to detonate! Your task is to cut the wires in the correct locations and complete the grid to defuse the bomb. The colored circles show the number of times each wire of the matching color needs to be cut. No wire may be less than 4 cells long once cut. Once cut, the rules of the wires listed below remain but now act as separate wires.
Adjacent digits along a green German Whisper wire must differ by at least 5. Box borders divide the blue Region Sum wire into segments with the same sum. Different wires may have different sums. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. Cells joined by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2 (one digit is double the other).

title: Isn't All Sudoku a Process of Elimination?
description:
Here's where you can try A Process of Elimination by Trufflebear: https://sudokupad.app/mmayk15ji7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If the digit N appears in a circle, then exactly N circles contain the digit N. Cages come in three sets: red, green and blue. All cages in the same coloured set have the same total, to be determined for each colour. These three totals are all different. Digits may not repeat within a set of cages of the same colour. For each set of cages, all possible two-cell combinations are used in the grid to reach that set's total. 
The digits not represented in the red cages, together with those not in the blue cages, and those not in the green cages, do not repeat. They are exactly the same set of digits as those to be found in the circle cells.
A white dot between two cells indicates that their digits differ by 1.

title: One Of The "Most Enjoyable" Fog Sudokus!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An original and brilliant sudoku tonight and a debut on the channel for MCMCHammer whose puzzle Hungry Rabbit In The Fog carries more than an echo of Marty Sears' popular Rat Run series. What's so fascinating about this one is that each box asks new questions of the solver - which they definitely won't have been asked before! Wonderful from start to finish.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zqpxetdz7a

Rules:
Poppy the hungry rabbit wants to find a path through the grid to find the carrot, without being eaten by any nasty predators.

Rabbit's path: Poppy follows a one-cell wide path through the grid, moving orthogonally. The path may not branch or touch itself, not even diagonally.

Hungry rabbit: Poppy eats each number she finds along its path, and therefore values on the path are cumulative. The value of any cell on the path is equal to the sum of all digits visited within that box, up to and including the existing cell. Crossing a box border resets the count (don't ask what Poppy does with the previously eaten numbers). Cells not on the path are unaffected.

For example, if the rabbit's path visits cells with digits 1, 4, 6 within a box, then the values associated with those cells are 1, 5, 11. If the rabbit then crosses into a new box and visits a cell with a 2, then that cell's value is 2.

Normal sudoku: - place the digits 1 to 9 in each row, column and box of the grid.

Fog of war: Placing correct digits in the grid may clear fog elsewhere in the grid.

White dots: A white dot connects cells whose values differ by 1.

Black dots: A black dot connects cells whose values are in a ratio of 1:2 (ie one cell's value is double the other).

Black killer cages: The value in the top left corner of a killer cage indicates the sum of the values of all cells within that cage.

Odd/even: Cells marked with a grey square have an even value. Cells marked with a grey circle have an odd value.

X/V: Two cells are separated by a black X must have values which sum to 10. Two cells separated by black V must have values which sum to 5.

Minimum: A cell containing inward pointing arrows must have a lower value than all surrounding cells.

Arrow: The value of the circled cell is equal to the sum of all values along the arrow.

Thermometer: Values along a grey thermometer must increase from the circled bulb to the tip.

Region sum line: Within each box, the total value of all cells along the blue region sum line must be equal.

Palindrome: Along a grey palindrome line, cells an equal distance from the centre of the line must have the same value.

German whispers: Along a green German whispers line, adjacent values must differ by at least 5.

Renban: A purple renban line consists of a set of consecutive values in any order.

Red security cage: The value hidden within the red security cage is a dangerous predator, and must not appear anywhere along the path.

title: The Puzzle Of "The Popular Pond"
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We indulge in a rare treat in the form of a pencil puzzle (which might have the name 'Anglers') called The Popular Pond by 99%Sneaky. This has a 99% rating appropriately enough and it's just so much fun to solve.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/c0rebcbl3j

Rules:
From each clue outside the grid, draw a path which begins in the nearest cell of the grid and then travels orthogonally from cell to cell until arriving at a fish. All empty cells must be used by a path. Paths may not cross themselves, each other, or fish. A number at the beginning of a path indicates how many cells in the grid the path occupies, including the cell with the fish. To avoid confusion among the anglers, no two fishing lines of the same length may touch. This includes both orthogonal and diagonal touching.

Answer Check: For each ? clue, fill each cell along the corresponding path with the digit equal to the length of the path. If the length is a double digit number, fill the cells with the one's digit of the length.

The cryptic clue Simon mentions at the start of the video:
Box that might arrive at any time? (6)
is answered at the base of this video description!

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Apologies about the length of tonight's video but this is a sudoku we're delighted we attempted. It's called Diagonality, it's by The Book Wyrm and it is definitely one of the cleverest puzzles we've ever seen. How just 4 given digits somehow disambiguate such a symmetrical grid is mind-blowing. Another unforgettable sudoku.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zhrcbbe8jx

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
Diagonality - Every diagonal contains at most 3 distinct digits.
Renban -  digits on a magenta line form a set of consecutive digits in any order.

title: An Agricultural Puzzle by Jane Street!
description:
Learn more about the Jane Street internship at https://jane-st.co/CTC-intern25. Play Farm to Market at https://jane-st.co/CTC-farmtotable

The puzzle contains three 5x5 farms, divided into fields as shown. On each farm:
Place the digits 1-5 once each in every row and column, such that no two fields on that single farm contain exactly the same digits.
Draw fences to partition the farm into orthogonally connected groups of fields that have the same sum. All fields with the same sum must be connected as part of the same group.

Thanks to Jane Street for sponsoring this video! 

Jane Street is a quantitative trading firm that uses techniques from machine learning, distributed systems, programmable hardware, and statistics to trade on markets around the world. Their love of puzzles and challenges has led them to sponsor this video!
If you're interested in Jane Street, they’re currently accepting applications for their 2026 internship program in three of their exciting office locations - New York, London, and Hong Kong. See the link above.

title: A 100%-Rated Sudoku Debut!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After yesterday's madness we're delighted to bring you a debut on the channel for Phil The Hat whose puzzle Quadrank Arrows has been awarded a perfect rating over at Logic Masters Germany. This is a very original idea that works wonderfully well AND the rules, though original, won't break your brain (unlike yesterday!!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/pd589n0d3g

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each circle has a value equal to the four digits around the clue arranged in ascending order. Eg if the four digits were 4,3,6,4 then the value of the circle would be 3446. Assign each circle a rank according to its value's position in a list of the all of the circles' values. The lowest rank would have rank 1, the next lowest would have rank 2 etc. Place each circle's rank into the cell at the tip of the arrow emerging from that circle. NB clues with the same value would have the same rank and would have the same digit in the tip of their circle's arrow. Digits in a cage sum to the given total.

title: "One Of The Finest Puzzles Ever Made"
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Ouch. That is what your brain might say when trying to solve this extraordinary sudoku by Oddlyeven! It's called Two Truths And A Different Truth and, if you can understand it, we don't think you'll ever forget it.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/cdifwlxo10

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 may be all shaded or all unshaded. A cell that is a ‘doubler’ has value equal to twice its digit. Two Truths and a Different Truth: For all the following constraints, if shaded cells are treated as doublers and unshaded cells are normal then two of the clues are correct and the third is incorrect. If unshaded cells are treated as doublers and shaded cells are normal then the same two clues are incorrect and the third is correct: a) Renban: Values on a pink line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats; b) Arrows: Values on an arrow sum to the value in that arrow's circle; 3) Values on an X sum to 10; 4) Values on a white dot are consecutive. Values on a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); 5) A value on a grey circle is odd. A value on a grey square is even.

title: Where Poker and Sudoku Meet!
description:
Here's where you can try Pokerface by Villse: https://sudokupad.app/rhgtkqogf2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Hands in poker, which consist of five cards (cells), are represented by the cages. If a cage does not contain five cells, cages with the same value in the top-left corner belong to the same poker hand. Every poker hand listed below is represented once (eg. if a cage consisted of all odd digits and also had three of the same digit, that would represent either a flush or three of a kind, not both). 
High card: All digits are different. 
Pair: One set of digits is the same. 
Two pair: Two sets of digits are the same. 
Three  of a kind: Three of the digits are the same. 
Straight: All the digits are consecutive. 
Flush: All the digits have the same colour. 
Full house: Three of the digits are the same and the other two are the same. 
Four of a kind: Four of the digits are the same. 
Even digits represent black cards, and odd digits represent red cards. The digits in a poker hand sum to the number in the top-left corner. Digits can repeat in a cage.

title: Solving Under The Influence...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Sorry, we couldn't resist the pun in the video title :)

Marty Sears returns tonight with a sudoku he apparently designed to be so quintessentially Marty that no-one could think anything else. And he totally succeeded. It's original, clever and actually very funny!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/m408yajamc

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. INFLUENCER CELLS: The grid contains nine 'influencer cells', each in a different row, column and box, and each containing a different digit. Every cell in the grid has a value equal to its own digit plus the digits in any orthogonally adjacent influencer cells. Eg: a cell containing a digit 2 would have a value of 10 if it neighbours an influencer 3 and an influencer 5, because 2 + 3 + 5 = 10. CAGES: The small clue in the corner of a cage indicates the total value of the cells in that cage. REGION SUM LINES: 3 x 3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The values on each segment have the same sum, though this sum can be different for different lines.

title: This Sudoku Looks Easy... Oops...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Oddlyeven's sudoku, Befuddlement, seems innocuous at first but it doesn't take long to live up to its name. This is a BRILLIANT fog-of-war puzzle that will leave you scratching your head (as well as tearing your hair out!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/w6uzuj1m0m

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit will remove the fog from its cell and possibly other cells in the grid. One cell in each row, column and box is a doubler. The value of a doubler cell is equal to twice its digit. Each of the digits from 1 to 9 appears in a doubler cell. On each of the constraints below, *values* do not repeat anywhere in the puzzle. For example, if there is a 2 on a parity line, 2 or double 1 can't appear anywhere else on a parity line, but double 2 could because it has a value of 4. 1) Adjacent values on a thin green line differ by at least 5; 2) Values on a thick purple line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats; 3) Adjacent values on a hollow red line must alternate between odd and even; 4) A value on an orange circle must be greater than 5; 5) A value on a blue square must be lower than 5.

title: This. Sudoku. Is. Insane.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Kaktuslav is setting some incredible puzzles and this is apparently his favourite! It's called Blue Arrow and, well, there is a very very crazy arrow in the grid! What a sudoku this is - so many moments of "wait... doesn't that mean...." :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/qz9m4zn7nf

Rules:
Divide the grid into 9 regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in every row, column, and region. The digits along the arrow sum to the three-digit number displayed in the attached pill. The arrow passes through the centres of all cells that are not part of the pill (note that consecutive arrow cells are not necessarily adjacent; for example, a portion of the arrow follows r7c1 → r7c3 → r8c1). The arrow functions as a ‘region sum line’: along the arrow, every maximal sequence of digits within the same region has the same sum. I.e. when all non-pill cells are arranged in sequence according to the order in which the arrow visits their centres, this sequence will be composed of disjoint contiguous segments with equal sums. Two consecutive cells in this sequence belong to the same segment if and only if they are part of the same region. The inequality sign points to the smaller digit.

Rockratzero's "Elements" Kickstarter can be found here 
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/rockratzero/periodic-puzzle-project

description:
This is the message from Heliopolix: "My son was diagnosed with leukemia last Saturday.  The cancer grew aggressively and overwhelmed his vital organs, and he passed away on Friday. Fill the grid with digits from 1-9 so that no digit repeats in any of the 9 rows, 11 columns, or 9 boxes. Along each of the 6 grey lines, digits increase in one direction. If a line has a bulb, the bulb is the smaller end. Digits touching a white dot are consecutive. Digits touching a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio.

title: It's Time For Advanced Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Please note that the rules displayed during the video omit the very important word "Grey" when discussing the 10-lines.  ie ONLY the grey lines are 10 lines. The rules are correctly stated below.

Yesterday we solved an incredible puzzle and that's always a tough act to follow but Jeff Wajes has done it! This sudoku is called Right Twice A Day and it's a fascinating interaction between 10-lines, German Whispers and Renbans. Don't miss this one!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/aadq3z8j80

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each pink line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, which can appear in any order. Each grey line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap; every cell is part of exactly one group. Lines may share endpoints, but otherwise don't overlap.

title: "One Of The Best Things I've Seen In Sudoku..."
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
So says the constructor Black Doom about today's offering from Scojo called Deja Vu. This is a series of puzzles with a quite extraordinary common thread running through them...  We won't tell you how many puzzles there are but, rest assured, you're mind will be blown before the end!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/pnyv6sn7qm

Rules (for puzzle 1):

Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and 2x3 box.
Doublers: Place one Doubler in every row, column, and box. Each Doubler must contain a different digit. The value of a Doubler is 2 times the digit in its cell. The value of a non-Doubler is the digit in its cell.
Standard Region Sum Line, Renban, Nabner, Thermo, Kropki, XV, and Quadruple rules apply, with respect to cell values ie:
Region Sum Line: Box borders divide the blue line into segments with equal sums of values.
Renban: Values along the pink line must form a set of non-repeating consecutive values in any order.
Nabner: The two values on the yellow line must have a difference of at least 2.
Thermo: The value on the tip of the thermometer must be larger than the value on the bulb.
Kropki: Values separated by the white dot are consecutive. Values separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio.
V: Values separated by the V sum to 5.
Quadruple: The value 2 must appear at least once in the four cells surrounding the white circle.

title: One of the Tastiest Sudokus around
description:
Here's where you can taste the menu by Niclas Kupper: https://sudokupad.app/ydtwtpul8o 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If a white dot separates digits, they are consecutive. If a black dot separates digits, one is double the other. If X separates digits, they sum to 10. If V separates digits, they sum to 5. Cells in the (blue) thermometer are increasing away from the bulb. Adjacent cells along the orange (Dutch whisper) line have a difference of at least 4. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. The digit in a green cell is larger than its orthogonal neighbours. The digit in a blue cell is smaller than its orthogonal neighbours.

title: Save the Sinking City!
description:
Here's where you can try Sinking City, a brilliant puzzle by MonkeyApprentice: https://sudokupad.app/tsxhzpwal7 
Every row column and box must contain the digits 0 to 8.Digits in the grid represent the heights of skyscrapers. Clues outside the grid indicate how many skyscrapers are visible in the direction of the clue in its row/column, where taller skyscrapers obscure shorter ones. There are 9 cells consisting of a set of the digits 0-8 representing condemned skyscrapers throughout the grid. There is exactly one condemned skyscraper in every row, column, and box. The height of a condemned skyscraper is considered to be zero for all clues. A skyscraper with a height of 0 is never visible to a clue outside the grid. Heights of skyscrapers connected by a white dot must be consecutive and the height of one skyscraper on a black dot must be equal to two times the height of the other skyscraper on that dot. Not all possible dots are given.

title: The New Sudoku Rule... It's Back!
description:
▶ NEW COMPETITION JUST OUT ON PATREON!!! ◀
At 4pm this afternoon we released Blobz new sudoku hunt, Back To The Future!! One of the best films ever now has its sudoku tribute - join us for as little as $2 a month to play. Closing date 20 September 2025.

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We celebrate Visumation's birthday by tackling the sixth in his popular fog-of-war series, Unique Under The Fog 6.0! This is quite approachable and will just make you smile. Gorgeous!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/hvtrbv1n24

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog; placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a renban line contains a 5, then no other renban line cell in the puzzle  may contain a 5: 1) Little Killer: Black numbers with an arrow outside the grid give the the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal; 2) X-Sums: Red numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits in that row or column, where X is the first digit in that row or column; 3)  Digits on a purple Renban (RB) line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits NB All Renban lines are exactly three cells long; 4) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference of at least 5; 5) The 3x3 box borders divide blue Region Sum (RS) lines into segments. Each segment along a line has the same sum.

title: These Nine Lines are Enough to Unlock this Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can attempt Nine Lines by Buttons: https://sudokupad.app/opx74hsg2p
Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot appear in cells a chess knight's move apart. In every 3x3 box, a digit cannot appear in its corresponding cell - as an example: the digit '1' cannot appear in the 1st cell of every 3x3 box.
Cells on a RED line are prime numbers.
Cells on an ORANGE line are composite numbers.
Cells on a YELLOW line are greater than 5.
Cells on a BROWN line are less than 5.
Cells on a GREEN line are odd. 
Cells on a BLUE line are even. 
Cells on a PINK line are square numbers.
Cells on a PURPLE line are triangular numbers.
Cells on a BLACK line are equivalent.

title: A Daily Diet of Three Puzzles!
description:
Here's where you can try these excellent puzzles by Bartok_the Magnificent:
Zip: https://sudokupad.app/a15tt4jnj4
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Place the digits 1-6 in each row, column, and box. The solver must draw a Parity Line (digits alternate between even and odd) that moves orthogonally and visits every cell in the puzzle including the six bubble digits in order. The line starts at the 1 bubble and ends at the 6 bubble. The Parity Line visits each cell exactly once and does not cross itself. The Parity Line cannot pass through thick black lines. The solver must determine which bubbles contain 2, 3, 4 and 5. Bubble digits must be followed by or preceded by a digit with the same residual modulo (14, 25, 36).

Queens: https://sudokupad.app/f7vz1zvw81 
Place the digits 1-6 in each row, column, and region. In each row, column, and region, there is a Queen Cell. Queen Cells may not be touching, even diagonally. All Queen Cells must not be orthogonally adjacent to any digits that form a 2:1 ratio with or are consecutive to the Queen Cell's digit. Digits separated by a black dot form a 2:1 ratio.

Tango: https://sudokupad.app/nuoopvuie9 
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Place the digits 1-6 in each row, column, and box.Shade some cells (Yellow) such that each row and column within the grid contains three shaded, and three unshaded cells (Blue). There cannot be three consecutive cells that are all shaded or unshaded in a row or column.
Cells separated by a black dot contain digits that form a 2:1 ratio and include one shaded and one unshaded cell. Cells separated by a white dot include consecutive digits that are either both shaded, or both unshaded. Digits in a cage must sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage. Shaded cells count as negative values towards the sum.

The constructor gdc is one of the most consistently brilliant in the world of sudoku: every single one of their puzzles is epic. And so we're delighted to attempt Harmonic Split tonight - a puzzle involving yin yang and equal split lines (surely a constraint we'll see a lot more of!) Oh, and it's everything we were expecting!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade each cell light or dark so that cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected and each 2x2 contains both colours. Dark cells have double their digits as values. title: Marley & Simon: Take The Sudoku Dog For A Walk
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A bizarre and brilliant new ruleset tonight in the form of the Doppel-Dog loop!? The puzzle is called Can I Pet That Dog, it's by aqjhs and it's absolutely wonderful.  Lots of you have recommended this one and we totally understand why :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/7llvcaivec

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Doppel-Dög loop: Draw an orthogonal non-branching closed loop that doesn't cross or touch itself, not even diagonally.  The loop "starts" at the cell marked with the dog and is considered to be oriented in the direction indicated by the arrow (i.e. r6c6 and r6c7 are in the loop). A cell on the loop with a digit D will have a value equal to the cell D steps away along the loop in the orientation given by the arrow. Cells not on the loop will have a value equal to the digit in them. Adjacent digits (not values) along the loop must have a difference of at least 5. Values in a cage sum to the indicated total. Cells marked with a circle are not part of the loop and have a digit that equal to the count of the, up to 8, neighbouring loop cells. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the values of the loop cells in the indicated row/column.

An example of the Doppel-Dog rule can be found here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000NAH

We've had lots of recommendations to try this sudoku, Once And For All by 99%Sneaky. And it's got this "constraint" rule (ie where no digit can repeat on a single constraint type) which we've been enjoying so much in recent months. One of the remarkable things about this puzzle is how little information we seem to be given and yet it all unfolds rather miraculously!

https://sudokupad.app/tjl67sygqk

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle E.g., if an orange line cell contains a 5, then no other orange line cell in the puzzle may contain a 5. Constraint types: 1) A digit in a grey square is even; 2) A digit in a grey circle is odd; 3) For digits in cells separated by a white dot, one must be one greater than the other; 4) For digits in cells separated by a black dot, one must be double the other; 5) Adjacent digits along an orange line must differ by 4 or more.

description:
Here's where you can attempt CTC Country Club by Dali: https://sudokupad.app/30jk32po6i 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The puzzle employs 4 different line constraints (explained below). Each line respects exactly 1 or 2 of these constraints. Each possible combination is represented exactly once.
Renban: Contains a set of consecutive digits,in any order.
German Whispers: Consecutive digits along the line must differ by at least 5.
Thermometers: Digits explicitly rise along the line from the bulb end. The bulb may be in any position along the line which may therefore branch. The solver must locate the position of the bulb.
Arrows: The digits along the line sum to the total in the circle. The circle may be in any position along the line which may therefore branch. The solver must locate the position of the circle.
A white dot separates cells containing consecutive digits.

title: The Sudoku Maker Who ALWAYS Delivers!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE *** 
In June, we published a sudoku hunt competition on Patreon which proved to be one of the most popular and well-reviewed rewards we've ever put out.  It was by yttrio - a constructor who simply always makes first-rate puzzles.  Tonight we try his Sightline Sum Whisper Loop - which, as usual, does what it says on the tin!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yttrio/sightline-sum-whisper-loop

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). Cells with small numbers in the corner are on the loop.  This number gives the sum of all loop cells (including itself) seen from that cell in all horizontal/vertical directions combined, where non-loop cells block the vision.  Digits may repeat in a sum if allowed by other rules.

title: Slicing and Dicing ... the Keypad!
description:
Here's where you can try Keypad Cross Out by Greenscribble24: https://sudokupad.app/kllmj2p8f7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the marked diagonal do not repeat. A thick grey line connected to two circles contains digits between the values of the digits in those circles. A colored line (teal OR peach) is BOTH an entropic and modular line.
Entropic Lines: Every set of three contiguous digits on an entropic line contains a low digit (1, 2, or 3), and middle digit (4, 5, or 6), and a high digit (7, 8, or 9). In other words, each set of three consecutive digits on a line must have one digit from each row of a keypad.
Modular Lines: Every set of three contiguous digits on a modular line contains digits with different remainders after being divided by 3 ({1, 4, 7}, {2, 5, 8}, and {3, 6, 9}). In other words, each set of three consecutive digits on a line must have one digit from each column of a keypad.

title: Kylo Ren: The Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A great debut on the channel today for father-and-son duo Melashenkos! It's called Kylo Ren and it's a nice day to do it as it's father Jay's birthday (and we know this because of son Jaden!) The puzzle itself is seriously clever too with some really original ideas.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/cf66mq38as

Rules:
Deconstruction:  Within the 11x11 grid, there exist nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions which must be located by the solver. Each region contains the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column, or 3x3 region. Cells outside these regions do not contain digits, but have a value of 0.
Kylo Renban Lines: Values on a purple Kylo Renban line must be a set of consecutive non-repeating values. The values may be in any order. Treat intersecting lines as a single Kylo Renban line.
Killer Cages: Values in a cage must sum to the total in the upper left-hand corner of the cage. Non-zero values may not repeat in a cage.
Thermometers: Values along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end.

title: 4x4 Sudokus Are Easy... Right?!
description:
*** LIVE CRACKING THE CRYPTIC SHOW ***
On 2nd November Simon & Mark will be doing a live episode at the Stratford Literary Festival.  Please book early to avoid disappointment, this event sold out quickly last year due to the venue size. (Also please do bear in mind that the event is in Stratford Upon Avon (and not the London Stratford!))

https://www.stratfordliteraryfestival.co.uk/events/simon-anthony-and-mark-goodliffe

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
How hard can a 4x4 sudoku be?! Well, we're not sure. But this puzzle by Burak Alver called Unique Ratios is certainly not trivial :) This is a super-interesting idea and might be very simple for some mathematicians but we really enjoyed it and think it's clever!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/eco0hsqvv4

Rules:
Place subsets of the digits 1-9 into every row, every column, and every 2x2 box so that no digit is repeated in any row, column, or box.
Kropki Dots: Digits separated by white kropki dots are consecutive, and digits separated by black kropki dots have a 1:2 ratio. ALL possible dots are given. For the avoidance of doubt, a 1:2 ratio is NOT present anywhere in the puzzle (so no domino can contain 1&2 or 2&4 or 3&6 or 4&8).
Digits in a cage sum to the clue in the top left corner of the cage.
Unique Ratios: The ratios of adjacent cells are unique, e.g., if R1C1 is 1 and R1C2 is 3, then there cannot be any pair of (horizontally or vertically) adjacent cells that have 1:3 ratio anywhere else on the grid.

title: The Greatest Sudoku You've Never Heard Of
description:
*** LIVE CRACKING THE CRYPTIC SHOW ***
On 2nd November Simon & Mark will be doing a live episode at the Stratford Literary Festival.  Please book early to avoid disappointment, this event sold out quickly last year due to the venue size. (Also please do bear in mind that the event is in Stratford Upon Avon (and not the London Stratford!))

https://www.stratfordliteraryfestival.co.uk/events/simon-anthony-and-mark-goodliffe

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
"One of the most extraordinary puzzles we've ever seen". That's what we think about tonight's sudoku: Magic Matryoshka by Nahileon. It is based on the crazy idea that a sudoku grid can contain nested magic squares and it's quite simply amazing.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/bupkl5df4h

Rules:
Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and irregularly-shaped marked nine-cell region. Cells separated by a black dot contain two digits where one digit is double the other. A magic square is a square of NxN cells in which each row, column and both main diagonals sum to the same total. (In this puzzle digits CAN repeat in a magic square.) The entire 9x9 grid is a magic square. In the centre of the 9x9 magic square is a 7x7 magic square. In the centre of that is a 5x5 magic square. And in the very centre is a 3x3 magic square. The dotted lines clarify the positions of the magic squares.

title: Possibly The Most Astonishing Miracle Sudoku We've Seen
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Since Mitchell Lee's original Miracle Sudoku we've seen a whole variety of puzzles with seemingly not nearly enough information given to yield a unique solution. Tonight's puzzle - Stinky Stuffing by the_cogito - is right up there in terms of madness. When you start to think about what you've been given, it doesn't seem possible that it can be remotely sufficient... and yet!! This is breathtaking.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/fawimvf33u

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the indicated diagonal. Numbers outside the grid are simultaneously full rank clues and sandwich clues. A '?' can be any number. Full rank Each complete row and column can be read from both directions to form 36 distinct 9-digit numbers. The clues outside the grid give the rank of the 9-digit number read from that position when all the numbers are ranked from smallest (1) to highest (36). Sandwich: A number outside the grid represents the sum of the digits sandwiched between the '1' and '9' in its respective row or column.

title: Sudoku Beauty = 100%, Sudoku Difficulty = 5/5: ✔✔✔✔✔
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Lots of recommendations and requests to tackle this puzzle! It's called Beyond and it's the work of MaizeGator. It's earned the "perfect" rating: 100% for beauty and 5/5 for difficulty and features an original but fascinating ruleset. There are a couple of moments in the solve which will have you shaking your head in admiration for the setter.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/kfzjh67o5i

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Nurikabe: Shade some cells (representing water) such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, but never fully cover a 2x2 area. Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands. Two separate islands cannot touch one another orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. Digits may not repeat on an island.  Each island contains exactly one numbered clue, which gives the product of the sum of the digits on the island and the size (number of cells) of the island, e.g. an island filled with 346 is would have a '39' clue (13x3). A '?' may represent any number (not necessarily single-digit). A cell with arrow(s) may be land or water, and the digit gives the total number of island cells in the indicated directions combined, not including itself. Not all arrows are given.

PLEASE NOTE: The version Simon solves in the video is slightly different to a new link that has appeared on Logic Masters for this puzzle. It might be that the version we were recommended has evolved and MaizeGator prefers the new version. This new version is below for anyone interested:

title: No Calculator Is Required. Can You Solve It?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The constructor Kaktuslav came to Simon's attention just a few days ago but since then we've been inundated with requests and recommendations to try more of their puzzles. Today Simon tackles Roots In The Fog and it's every bit as good as the last sudoku we did. There's a little bit of maths here but you DON'T need a calculator!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/jbliq30p6u

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly nine cells in the grid are "rooters". The value of a rooter equals the square root of its digit (in all other cells, the value equals the digit). No two rooters share a row, column, box, or digit. A black dot connects two cells where one value is double the other (not all such dots are necessarily given). Values on thermometers strictly increase from bulb to tip. The sum of the values along an arrow equals the value in the attached circle.  Along green lines, neighbouring values differ by at least 5. On each purple line, the set of values consists of consecutive integers in any order. All cages have the same product of values (digits or values may repeat within a cage if allowed by other rules). The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear some fog (not necessarily beneath or around the entered digit). No guessing is required.

title: Another Marty Sears' Sudoku Masterpiece!!
description:
*** LAST NIGHT'S BLUE PRINCE STREAM ***
You can (re)watch last night's Blue Prince stream here:
https://youtube.com/live/vkWsgzPtszM

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears returns tonight with one of his masterpieces (and there have been many). It's really quite extraordinary that this solves and there's one moment in particular where the logic must have been sent from heaven.  That said (Simon blames the heat), it's possible to go down the wrong track... what happens then?!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/s7221r2i0r

Rules:
Divide the grid into eight non-overlapping 2x4 regions, which can each be placed either horizontally or vertically. It must be determined which one of the digits 1-9 is missing from the grid. The other eight digits should each appear once in every row, column and region. RENBAN (pink) - digits along the pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set, which can appear in any order. NABNER (yellow) - no two digits on the yellow line may be consecutive (or the same.) REGION SUM (darker blue) - on the blue line, digits in each region have the same total. GERMAN WHISPER (green) - adjacent digits on the green line must have a difference of at least 5. PARITY (red) - digits on the red line must alternate between odd and even. PALINDROME (grey) - the string of digits on the grey line reads the same in either direction. SAME DIFFERENCE (turquoise) - each pair of adjacent digits on a turquoise line has the same difference. This difference value can be different for different turquoise lines. KROPKI - two digits connected by a black dot have a 2:1 ratio (ie one is double the other.)

A debut on the channel for the setter Kaktuslav tonight and their puzzle Red + Blue = Purple. It is hard to believe we've not heard more about Kaktuslav before now such is the almost unbelievable quality of what's going on in this sudoku. This is simply stunning.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon solves a gorgeous sudoku called Limitations 8 by Md88keys in tonight's edition. If you enjoy Fog Of War puzzles then this one is for you - it's not too difficult but features a whole series of satisfying and fun deductions!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/ndo5ff4agt

Rules:
Place nine non-overlapping 3x3 boxes in the grid. All cells containing any clue (line/dot/etc) must be included in a 3x3 box. Place the digits 1-9 in each 3x3 box. Digits may not repeat in a row or column. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. The four digits in a quad circle appear in the four surrounding cells. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle: 1) 3x3 box borders divide a blue region sum line into segments with the same value. The value of a segment is the sum of its cells; 2) a purple line contains a set of consecutive digits; 3) adjacent digits on a green German Whisper line have a difference of 5 or more; 4) adjacent digits on a red line alternate parity (odd/even); 5) adjacent digits along a grey line have the same difference. (Separate lines may have different differences); 6) black dots connect cells where one digit is double the other; 7) white dots connect consecutive digits.

NB For the Solution check function to work, enter a 0 into every cell in the grid that is not part of a 3x3 box.

One of life's great treats is a new sudoku by Marty Sears - this one is called NOT ON and features Marty's usual innovative brilliance.  Simon found it a fascinating puzzle but not terribly easy - see what you think!

title: Modness In The Sudoku Fog?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Lost In The Modhouse may send you to the madhouse as you do battle with Kennet's Dad (KMD)! As always with the best fog-of-war sudoku puzzles, it sometimes doesn't seem like there's enough information in the unfogged cells to make any progress... and yet...!!

A very interesting puzzle - enjoy :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/buum97646q

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog; placing a correct digit will clear the fog in that cell and possibly elsewhere in the grid. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a parity line contains a 5, then no other parity line cell in the puzzle  may contain a 5: 1) Digits in a cage must sum to the total given; 2) Digits joined by an X sum to 10; 3) Adjacent digits along a red parity line (PR) must alternate between odd and even digits; 4) A purple renban line (RB) must contain a set of consecutive digits in any order; 5) A yellow nabner line (NB) must contain a set of nonconsecutive digits in any order; 6) Any set of three digits along an orange entropic line (ENT) line must contain one digit from each of the following sets: 123; 456; 789; 7) Any set of three digits along a teal modular line (MOD) must contain one digit from each of the following sets: 147; 258; 369; 8) Pairs of digits equidistant from the centre of a pink zipper line (ZIP) must sum to the digit in the centre of that line, notated by a small circle. Lines in the puzzle never intersect or share cells.

description:
Here's where you can try Sudocube by BlueBirdBrokenLeg: https://sudokupad.app/twavox6vat 
Normal sudoku rules apply.
Orange Square: The sum of the digits inside the square must equal the number in the top-left corner. Can have repeated digits.
Green Square (“Whisper Line”): A digit in a green cell differs by at least 5 from a digit in an orthogonally adjacent green cell.
Red Square (Quadruple): A digit inside the circle appears at least once in the four cells touching that circle.
Blue Rectangle (“Renban Pink Line”): Contains a set of digits that are consecutive and all different. 
Yellow Square (Palindromic Lines): The shape X are two diagonal palindromic lines, reading the same forwards and backwards.
White Dot: A pair of cells connected by a white dot contains consecutive digits. 
Diagonal Line: Digits may not repeat along the marked diagonal.

title: Counting The Constraints! Fog Sudoku Magic
description:
*** AUGUST SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION TOMORROW ***
Tomorrow we launch a brand new sudoku hunt competition on Patreon. It's our own hunt and is based around The Labours Of Rostam - a Persian legend.  

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Erin Toler was an early guest on our Viewer Solves series and she isn't just a brilliant solver judging by tonight's puzzle. It's called Counting Constraints and it's a bit of fog sudoku magic!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/erin-toler/counting-constraints

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placing digits may clear fog somewhere in the puzzle. Correct digits do not necessarily clear fog from their own cells. Counting constraints: A digit on a constraint indicates the total number of times that digit appears on ANY of the constraints below. No cell contains more than one constraint. A) German whispers: Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5; B) Dutch whispers: Adjacent digits along an orange line must have a difference of at least 4; C) Nabner lines: No two digits on a yellow line may be the same or consecutive; D) Renban lines: Pink lines are filled with a consecutive set of non-repeating digits; E) Counting circles: A digit in a black-outlined counting circle indicates the number of times that digit appears in a counting circle; F) Odd circles: A digit in a gray circle must be odd; G) Kropki: Digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2 (i.e. one is double the other).

title: The Programmer's Sudoku Dream!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Michael Lefkowitz ("Juggler") is one of the most original minds in the sudoku universe and he's come up with another completely new idea for tonight's puzzle. It's called Change Log and we need to navigate a robot through the grid but keeping track of our path as we go...  One thing's for certain - we haven't solved anything quite like this before!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0zns8fzorv

Rules:
Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply. ie Place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 rectangle. Draw a path along interior gridlines from the robot to the exit. The path cannot touch itself. The robot computes the difference between each pair of digits it passes between, and writes these differences to the grey memory cells in reading order. (All memory cells must be written to and no difference goes unrecorded).

Numbers on lines outside the grid (to be determined) are Hitpoints clues: a clue's value equals the sum of all digits in that row/column which equal their distance from the clue.

title: Up to my Neck in the Fog!
description:
Here's where you can have a go at Up to Something by Sujoyku: https://sudokupad.app/zbgub1jtmx 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Correctly placing a digit will clear any fog in its own cell, and potentially clear fog in other cells too. Each row, column, and 3x3 region contains exactly one given digit whose exact location is to be deduced. No two givens are identical digits, i.e. each of the digits 1 to 9 is given exactly once. A clue outside a row or column indicates the sum of all digits up to the given digit (the given digit itself is not included in the sum).
Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle from which the arrow emerges. Digits joined by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.

title: A New Role for the Black Dots ...
description:
Here's where you can try Krazy Kropki by Dave Brenn: https://sudokupad.app/n528pv2c16 
Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column and 3x3 box. All digits in a cage are summed together and treated as one value for the purpose of Kropki relationships. 
Each 3x3 box contains a UNIQUE multiplier. The value of the multiplier is the digit in the upper left square of that box. (Eg. if r1c4 is 5, the multiplier for box two is 5). Cage totals separated by a black Krazy Kropki dot are in a ratio of X:1 (one digit or cage total is X times the value of the other), where X is the multiplier for the 3x3 box containing that dot. If a Krazy Kropki dot lies on the border between two boxes, the player must determine which of the two box multipliers to use for that dot. (Eg, if the multiplier for box five was 3, and box six was 7, a Krazy Kropki dot between those two boxes could be either a 3:1 ratio or a 7:1 ratio). Cage totals separated by a white dot are consecutive.

title: The Maths Professors' Sudoku Challenge
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We are a little late with this puzzle which was meant to appear on March 29 - oops - to celebrate the birthday of one of the constructors, Neil!  The sudoku is by FullDeck (Eliza) and Missing A Few Cards (Neil) who are maths professors over in the US. https://sudokupad.app/1cwnilmrp0

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the value shown in the upper left corner of the cage. Each line in the puzzle is EXACTLY TWO of modular, entropic, or parity. Modular Lines: Any set of three adjacent digits along a modular line has three different remainders when divided by 3. Entropic lines: Any set of three adjacent cells along an entropic line must contain a low digit (123), a middle digit (456), and a high digit (789). Parity Lines: Digits along parity lines alternate odd/even.

title: What Might Sudoku Look Like in Another World?
description:
Here's where you can try Another World by Artham: https://sudokupad.app/00tjfy70pd 
Normal sudoku rules do NOT apply. Fill the grid with the digits 1 to 9, nine times each. A digit might repeat in a row and/or column, but then all its occurrences must be adjacent. There is a maximum of ONE block (orthogonally connected area) of adjacent occurrences for each digit in the whole grid.
The center region can't contain a digit twice. The digit in a cell of this region indicates exactly how many odd digits are in the corresponding outer region (the top left cell points at the top left region, etc.). No two adjacent cells sum to 10. Cells separated by a green dot contain both an even and an odd digit. Lines contain digits in order with a constant difference, like 4-4-4, 5-6-7 or 9-5-1. A clue at the edge of the grid shows the sum of the first X digits, where X is the first seen digit.

title: Forget Most of what you know about Normal Sudoku Rules ...
description:
Here's where you can try Detached Regions of Seven by Md88keys: https://sudokupad.app/okh6idt7fe 
Place the digits 0-6 once in every row, column, and seven-cell region. Only one marked region has seven orthogonally connected cells. The six remaining regions are split into two orthogonally connected groups of cells (a 2 cell group paired with 5 cell group etc). Digits in a cage may repeat, and sum to 5.
Orthogonally adjacent pairs of cells that sum to 10 are marked with an X. All X clues are given. Orthogonally adjacent pairs of cells that sum to 5 are marked with a V, except for pairs of cells that exist within the same cage. All V clues (outside of cages or on cage boundaries) are given.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid contains nine "three-sum" cells, one in each row, column, and 3x3 box. Each digit from 1-9 is a "three-sum" exactly once. “Three-sum” digits count as their nominal value increased by 3. For example, a “three-sum” 7 would have a value of 10.

description:

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Playmaker6174 returns to Cracking The Cryptic tonight with an absolutely BRILLIANT sudoku full of original ideas - even though the constraints in the ruleset have been used many times before! The consensus from those who've recommended it is that this is a masterpiece and it might just be.

title: Zombie Logic Is HERE!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A brand new hybrid logic puzzle for our non-sudoku Saturday series from Shintaro Fushida-Hardy! It's called Zombie! and merges Araf and Yin-Yang - it sounds mad and it is, in all the best ways :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/rn6u1h8v9k?setting-conflictchecker=0

Rules:
Yin-Yang: Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 is entirely shaded or unshaded. Araf: Divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions, each containing exactly two number clues. The number of cells in each region is strictly between its two number clues.
1. Each Araf region is itself a valid Yin-Yang. In other words, all shaded cells within a region are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells within a region are orthogonally connected.
2. In each Araf region, one clue is shaded and one clue is unshaded.
3. One of the clues in an Araf region gives the exact count of shaded cells in its region. This clue may be shaded or unshaded.
For answer-check, in all unshaded cells without a given number, enter the size of the Araf region containing that cell. (Enter only the 1s digit for two-digit numbers.)

An example puzzle is available here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000MKE

title: What does this Grid Marking even Mean?
description:
Here's where you can try XV Inequality Sudoku by Gugunut: https://sudokupad.app/nxbw6uuei0 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent cells containing digits summing to 5 are marked with a 'V', and adjacent cells containing digits summing to 10 are marked with an 'X'. Adjacent cells without a marking must not contain digits summing to 5 or 10.
Additionally, some inequality signs are marked between adjacent cells that are not marked with 'V' or 'X'. The inequality signs indicate the relationship between digits in those cells. Inequality signs are visually identical to the 'V' clues. It is part of the puzzle to distinguish between the two.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. A white diamond between two cages means that the difference between their cage totals is equal to the topmost/leftmost digit in the column/row in which that diamond appears. title: Sudoku at the Tour de France!
description:
Here's where you can try TDF Odd Mountain Stage by Palpot: https://sudokupad.app/7qo4oi3fi3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line in the grid represents the path of a different rider. Riders earn 1 point for every odd digit on their path. A digit in a cell with a rider indicates the amount of points earned by that rider. The Red rider (R4C5) doesn't share a cell with its line.

title: Sudoku's Cycles Of Time And Tide (zetamath)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's always a great day when you get to tackle a new zetamath puzzle so TODAY is a great day!! It's called Cycles Of Time And Tide (do let us know the reference) and it's the usual stunning fare from one of the most brilliant minds in sudoku.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/z417emg43r

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A black dot sits between two digits where one is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. The single grey line is a palindrome ie its digits read the same forwards and backwards. Blue lines in the grid are Region Sum Lines ie The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; each segment along a line has the same sum. (NB Different lines may have different sums). Eg r5c2+r5c3+r6c2+r6c3=r7c2+r8c2=r7c3+r8c3. 
The salmon coloured lines in the grid are entropic lines ie Any set of three sequential cells along an entropic line must contain a low digit (123), middle digit (456) and high digit (789). Digits may repeat on a line, if allowed by other rules.

title: Another Extraordinary Fog Sudoku Deduction!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
SamuPiano's new fog-of-war sudoku does contain a lengthy ruleset - which we might normally disapprove of very slightly. However... what this ruleset allows is a solve of such beauty and interest that all is forgiven.  (One point in particular is quite unbelievable!) Bravo!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/r38cxr9nhu

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear fog from surrounding cells. 𝗖𝗮𝘃𝗲: Shade some cells such that all unshaded cells form a single orthogonally connected region and all shaded cells are connected to the edge of the grid. Digits in circles either give the size of the shaded region in which it lies or the total number of unshaded cells which can be seen in all directions from the unshaded circled cell, including the cell itself. Shaded cells block vision. 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁: Some circled cells are endpoints of lines in the grid. All lines move orthogonally. Lines do not cross or branch, except at circled cells. The digit in a circle gives the total number of cells along each line attached to the circle of the same shading as the circled cell, including the endpoints. 𝗦𝗽𝗹𝗶𝘁 𝗣𝗲𝗮𝘀: Digits along a line strictly between two circles must sum to a two-digit number, where the tens digit is in one circle and the ones digit is in the other. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all X or V are given.

title: Impossible Sudoku: Is This Logic Correct?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fascinating sudoku tonight from Justin Vitanza called Trasfer Right By 2. There are some incredibly interesting ideas underpinning this one and Simon is still grappling with them several hours after the recording!  A memorable and brilliant puzzle for sure but was his logic valid?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yvfa2jpnew

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Mod-3 Rows: Each row in the puzzle is a mod-3 line. That is, any set of three horizontally adjacent digits must contain one digit from (1,4,7), one digit from (2,5,8), and one digit from (3,6,9). 159 Indexing: Digits in columns 1, 5, and 9 indicate the column in which the digits 1, 5, or 9 (respectively) appears in that row. (Eg if r4c5 is an 8 then r4c8 is a 5 as the 5 must appear in the 8th column). Renban: Each purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Little Killer: Digits along the positive diagonal sum to a value that is (strictly) less than 24.

Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1 to 9, once each, in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Additionally no digit may be used more than once among all the cages of the same sum, even if that sum is not explicitly given. Eg if the r2c3 cage contained digits summing to 8, neither of these digits could be either of the digits used in the r6c7 8 cage.

title: Olympic Brains From An Olympic Athlete!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Fenners is an Olympic athlete but it's also emerging an Olympic-level mind too. This is an absolutely brilliant puzzle tonight using a small twist on the "only one digit per constraint" ruleset. Very original and highly recommended!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/8b7y7246mu

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. No two instances of the same constraint type may share digits. So, although digits may repeat on a clue, they may NOT repeat across different occurrences of that clue type. Eg if an arrow has the digit X, X may repeat along that arrow, but X may not appear on any other arrow. Clue types: 1) Quadruples: In an orange circle, the question mark contains the set of all the (possibly repeating) digits appearing in the surrounding cells. 2) Renban: Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. 3) Arrows: Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. 4) White dot: Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. 5) Black dot: Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).

[We had to re-upload this because of an extremely dubious copyright strike from the earlier version (and not from Radiohead but from someone impersonating them we might add!) So, if you could take the trouble to Like or Subscribe to THIS video, we'd be really grateful.]

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
There is some strange meme going on in the sudoku world at the moment to do with somebody called "Top Right Boi".  This Boi features in this puzzle by Scojo - which someone called Top Right Boi says is the "best puzzle I've ever solved"!?  What's going on?!?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/uhbdfuaf2r

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Top Right Boi's Path: Draw a path of orthogonally connected cells from Top Right Boi in row 9 column 1 to his home in row 1 column 9. The path may not touch itself, not even diagonally. Other than his starting position, Top Right Boi MUST NEVER visit the bottom left corner of any 3x3 box. Conversely, Top Right Boi MUST visit the top right corner of every 3x3 box before returning home. The 9 top right corner cells in the grid must all contain different digits. As the bottom left corner cells are lawless wastelands, there is no such restriction on their digits.

Any cell Top Right Boi visits will have it's value modified to be equal to Top Right Boi's current value, regardless of the digit in that cell. When Top Right Boi visits a cell in the top right corner of a 3x3 box, his value changes to be the digit in that cell, and will remain as that value until the next top right corner cell he visits (For clarity, this means that all top right corner cells have their digits as their values). Because Top Right Boi is beginning his journey from the horrid bottom left of the grid, his value will be 0 until he reaches the first top right corner cell along the path. Cells not on the path retain the value of their digits.

Cages: Values in a cage must sum to the number in the top right corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage, but values may.

Kropki: If two values are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. If two values are separated by a white dot, they are consecutive.

XV: If two values are separated by an X, they sum to 10. If two values are separated by a V, they sum to 5.

Not all possible Kropkis or XVs are necessarily shown.

title: Is This Puzzle Is As Easy As ABC....?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for oskode with a sudoku called It's ABC (All Basic Calculation!) This is a lovely idea, executed with consummate skill and it's certainly not trivial to solve. See how you go!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/7iiikykquy

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A letter indicates the same whole number whenever it appears (eg the letter B could represent the number 10 throughout the puzzle); and each letter represents a different number. Digits in a cage sum to the total in the cage’s upper left corner. Red numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of all digits along the indicated diagonal. Black numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the first N digits in that row or column (counting from the direction of the clue), where N is the digit in the first cell in that row or column (closest to the clue.)

title: The Extraordinary Power Of Parity
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most consistently brilliant constructors in the world of sudoku is yttrio.  Tonight we try his Pointer Arrow Parity Loop which is so ridiculously clever it's barely creditable. A few short arrows is all that's needed to make this unique and the logic required... well, try it yourself and see :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/gx4a6r7xzq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a parity line: digits along the loop must alternate between even and odd digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's bulb, and all bulbs are on the loop. Additionally, arrow tips point towards a cell containing the digit within the arrow's bulb, and this cell with the pointed-to digit is also on the loop. The digit in the arrow tip indicates the distance from the arrow tip to the pointed-to cell.  There may be other instances of the same digit between this cell and the arrow tip.

title: The Best Mathematical Sudoku Ever.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Nearly 5 years ago a constructor called joecat released a sudoku on Logic Masters Germany called "Rainy Day Sudoku 12² & 35". In the meantime this puzzle has been solved only a handful of times despite maintaining a perfect 100% rating (and a 5* difficulty rank).  The rules are simple. The logic however is not. It may be joecat's only published sudoku but it's one of the best we've ever seen.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/qm4anii4zz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. With one exception, every cage has a product that both is a multiple of 144 and is not a multiple of 35. *** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Last month, Sophie won our competition and, very kindly, agreed to make a sudoku video with Simon.  Mark selected the puzzle Don't Repeat Yourself by DedaKosta.  This is a phenomenal fog-of-war sudoku - and it turns out that Sophie is rather good at solving!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/fx2o4cl240

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each unique clue type listed below cannot contain more than one instance of each of the digits 1-9. Clue types: a) Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive; b) digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio, ie. one digit is double the other; c) digits in cages sum to the total in the upper left corner, if given; d) digits on a pink line form a set of consecutive digits IN ORDER. Eg 123 and 321 are valid length-3 lines but 132 is not; e) digits outside the grid give the sum of the digits on the diagonal pointed to by the arrow; f) each segment on a blue line sums to the same total. Box borders separate a line into segments. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digit in a cell may reveal some of the fog, possibly revealing more clues.

title: The Mad Lad Scientist Strikes
description:
Here's where you can try Scientist's split-arrows! by LNOMISL: https://sudokupad.app/fmoz7mzj21  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every arrow passes through a teleporter (dotted cage). Digits on one side of a teleporter must match the digit on the other side (E.g. If an arrow enters a teleporter with the digit 5, it must exit another teleporter also with a 5). Every arrow must go through a teleporter. Note that the teleporter in the middle box is used by 2 different arrows.
The digits on an arrow sum to the number in the circle. 3 arrows have only 1 unique digit (E.g. 444), 2 arrows have only 2 different digits (E.g. 122 and 225) and 1 arrow has only 3 different digits (E.g. 1566), plus there is one more arrow that whose pattern must be deduced.
Digits strictly increase along a thermometer. White dots indicate consecutive digits.

title: The Best New Ruleset In Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Belamis invented the ruleset where a particular constraint type cannot have a repeated digit on it. It's led to a whole genre of outstanding sudokus (many of which are by Belamis!) Tonight we try Belamis' new one, Breadcrumbs, which is also a fog-of-war puzzle.  The sheer range of deductions in this one is outstanding - this is a SERIOUSLY good puzzle.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/jfyralmfoe

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. The first correctly placed digit on each constraint will remove fog from other cells. Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g. If one cell on a parity line contains a 5, then no other cell on a parity line may contain a 5. Constraints: a) Along a red line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even; b) Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner if given; c) digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); d) pairs of digits equidistant from the centre of a lavender zipper line must sum to the digit in the middle of that line (noted by a dot); e) digits along a thermometer increase from bulb to tip; f) a cell with arrows pointing inward must be smaller than all other cells that share its edge; and g) a digit in a grey square is even. Each listed constraint type appears at least once in the puzzle.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're very fortunate tonight to be able to showcase an unpublished sudoku from the wonderful James Sinclair! It's called Unveil and combines James' usual simple rules with interesting and accessible logic :)
Don't miss this one - it's great!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/unveil

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits inside each cage is equal to the small number in the top left corner. Each purple line contains a pair of consecutive digits. title: Incredible New Sudoku Rule: Pick-Up Sticks!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another fog-of-war sudoku tonight - this time from the inimitable Marty Sears, who has introduced a very cool idea called Pick-Up Sticks!  The idea is that sticks that lie on other sticks must have higher totals and it leads to some really cool logic!

Apologies about the musical outro today. For a much better version listen to Karine Polwart's Follow The Heron!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/pc6ejr0nze

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. The grid is covered in fog. Entering correct digits might clear fog somewhere in the grid. A stick always has a lower total (the sum of its digits) than any stick which lies on top of it. Sticks that aren't grey have an additional rule: A yellow ENTROPIC stick must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6), and one high digit (7, 8 or 9.); a teal MODULAR stick must contain one digit from each of the sets (1,4,7), (2,5,8), and (3,6,9); a pink RENBAN stick must contain a set of consecutive digits – these can be arranged in any order; along an orange DUTCH WHISPER stick, adjacent digits must have a difference of at least 4; along a red PARITY STICK, digits must alternate between odd and even.

title: Unique Under The Fog: Sudoku Class!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've been loving Visumation's Unique Under The Fog series.  We now tackle puzzle 3 (having already done 1, 4 and 5!) and it's every bit as good as the others we've tried. [The link to Simon's Sister-In-Law's new embroidery site is below!]

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/44t9pol5x3

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Each unique clue type listed below cannot contain more than one instance of each of the digits 1-9. 
Clue types: a) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference of at least 5; b) Every set of three sequential cells on a mint modular (MO) line must contain one digit from (1,4,7), one digit from (2,5,8), and one digits from (3,6,9); c) Neighbouring digits on an orange Dutch Whisper (DW) line must have a difference of at least 4. (DW); d) Neighbouring digits on a red parity (P) line must alternate parity (odd/even); e) Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the clue in the top left of that cage (if given); f) Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other); g) Cells with a grey square contain an even digit; h) Cells with a grey circle contain an odd digit. 
Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.

It feels like months before we've enjoyed a zetamath puzzle on the channel but the great man returns today with his latest, Frankenstein! This is his normal class fare and you'll need to think about how these lines interact to make any progress :)

Normal sudoku rules apply. The lavender lines are zipper lines.  Each pair of digits equidistant from the centre digit has a sum equal to that centre digit.  For instance, 16827 would be a valid fill for a zipper line because 8 = 1 + 7 = 6 + 2. The darker off-green kind-of-unpleasant-looking lines are modular lines.  Each set of three adjacent digits along a modular line must contain one of 147, one of 258, and one of 369.

title: Croakz the Frog plays Sudoku!
description:
Here's where you can try Feeding Friendsy by Sujoyku: https://sudokupad.app/pdywima58n 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Help Croakz to chase the fly by drawing his path from water lily to water lily! The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any sharp rocks (the thick grey walls). As well as moving orthogonally, Croakz may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through rounded rock on the corner of a cell.
The grid contains nine (9) water lilies that must ALL be part of the path (of which you must determine the order). No water lily may contain the same digit. Digits separated by a brown twig sum to 5. Digits separated by a leaf have a difference of at least 5. Digits separated by a round frog egg have a 1:2 ratio.
Water lilies divide Croakz' path into "split pea" segments. A segment between two water lilies must sum to a two-digit number formed by both digits. For example, if the water lilies containing the digits 1 and 2 are joined by a segment, that segment must sum to either 12 or 21. The segment from Croakz' starting position to the first water lily must sum to the digit on that water lily — this includes the digit on Croakz' starting position itself.

title: Can you Find Treasury Island?
description:
Here's where you can have a go at finding Treasury Island by SUDOOOOOKUfan87: https://sudokupad.app/5y0k8sp8ev
Normal sudoku rules apply. All cells are either island or water. Each purple cell is an island cell. Each island must contain exactly one purple cell. Different islands may not touch orthogonally. The water cells are orthogonally connected and may not contain any 2×2 areas of water.
Each island also contains a set of non-repeating digits that sums to the purple cell total if given. If no total is given, the sum is 6, 9 or 25. The number in the purple cell is the number of cells in the island. Totals are not necessarily in the top left most cell of an island.
All islands are normal except one - Treasury Island, which has no given total. On this island, X's mark the spot - i.e. Treasury Island can be evenly divided into non-overlapping dominoes that each sum to 10; also, the purple cell's digit is inconsequential and digits may repeat.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In 2015 Dr Joseph Yeo's question in the Singapore and Asian Schools Math Olympiad (SASMO) went viral - it involved trying to work out Cheryl's birthday. Elytron has produced a sudoku version in one of the most original and brilliant puzzles we've ever seen.  What a gift on Simon's birthday (and viewers will need to tell us whether this is more or less difficult than the original!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/g337cy04rc

Rules:
Albert, Bertrand, Carl and David are perfectly logical Sudoku solvers. They are shown the following 4×4 Sudoku grid with these rules: Normal 4×4 Sudoku rules apply; digits in cages sum up to the value in the top left and MAY repeat if allowed by other rules. Each solver is privately told the value of one cage total: Albert is told A, Bertrand is told B, Carl is told C, and David is told D. They then have the following conversation:

Albert: 'Nobody here can place any digits yet.'
Bertrand: 'Well, now I can.'
Carl: “No one else was told the same number as I was.”
David: “Someone here knows more digits than I do.”

After this exchange, one of the four solvers completes the Sudoku. Can you do the same?
