title: Your Mission: Solve This Sudoku In 45 Minutes...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Ethan, your mission, should you choose to accept it, it to complete the diamond heist in 45 minutes.  This introduction will self-destruct in 5 seconds.

We love everything about this new puzzle from Marty Sears - the graphics, the logic, the wit and the idea that we have a limited time to complete the mission! 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/2od7bk8x77?setting-digitoutlines=0

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Escape from the diamond vault by finding a path from the ventilation shaft (r9c9) to the door (r2c1). Your path may only move orthogonally, and may not visit any cell more than once. You may not pass through any coloured display plinths. Also, stepping on any floor tiles with an even digit will trigger the alarms, so don't do that. The digit on a diamond equals the sum of the digits on all the keys that match its plinth colour (and letter). No two diamonds have the same digit. Discover these diamond digits to steal them, and find the path to escape the room. You have 45 minutes!

description:
Here's where you can try Foggy Unique Constraints by Pychael: https://sudokupad.app/1cwhkyc8be 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in dynamic fog; placing a correct digit may clear fog elsewhere in the puzzle. 
Adjacent digits along (striped) green lines must differ by at least 5. Digits on a (thick) purple lines must form a set of consecutive digits. Box borders divide a (thin) blue line into segments with the same sum (all region sum lines cross at least one border). Digits joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. Digits joined by a V sum to 5. Digits joined by an X sum to 10. A digit in a square is even.
Each unique constraint type above contains no repeated digit anywhere within its specific constraint type.

title: 3 is such a Magic Number
description:
Here's where you can try 3 is a Magic Number by KWOG: https://sudokupad.app/yv9zbsgm7n 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered with fog. Placing digits correctly will clear the fog. Box 3 is a Magic Square: all the rows, columns and 3-cell diagonals within the box sum to the same total. A white dot separates consecutive digits. A black dot separates digits in a 1-to-2 ratio. Digits along an arrow sum to the total in the circle.
For the digit 3 alone, there is an anti-knight’s move constraint and a negative constraint on Kropki dots. This means that a 3 cannot be within a knight’s move of another 3, or next to a 2, 4 or 6 without a Kropki dot chaperoning them.

title: What's Under The Sudoku Fog?!
description:
*** JUNE SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION IS LIVE ***
Yesterday we launched a brand new sudoku hunt competition on Patreon. It's a hunt by yttrio and features a story and 13 puzzles.  Closing date 20 June :)

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We really enjoy these Unique Under The Fog puzzles from Visumation.  This is 5.0 (so we must have missed a couple) and it's every bit a good as the early ones in the series. The idea is that any constraint (eg arrow) cannot have a repeated digit anywhere in the puzzle and it leads to some lovely ideas. Enjoy :)

[Today's musical intro and extended outro is 3am by Boyce Avenue covering Matchbox Twenty.]

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/3dnyh2rdg2

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 

Constraints: A) Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle; B) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper line (GW) must have a difference of at least 5; C) Digits on a purple Renban line (RB) form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits; D) Grey Ten-lines (T) must be divided into non-overlapping segments each of which sums to 10; E) Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other). Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. Eg. If one renban line contains a 5, then no other renban line may contain a 5.

Digits cannot repeat on the positive (SW-NE) diagonal. Digits cannot repeat on the negative (NW-SE) diagonal. Digits cannot repeat in cells with blue squares. Cells with an opaque grey circle contain odd digits. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.

title: Magnus, Please Help With My Sudoku...
description:
*** JUNE SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION TODAY ***
This afternoon we launched a brand new sudoku hunt competition on Patreon. It's a hunt by yttrio and features a story and 13 puzzles.  Closing date 20 June :)

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon was scheduled to try a different sudoku today but we had a recommendation to check out this new puzzle from ThePedallingPianist and, once he saw it, he had to try it! There are many things one could say about this one... but just know that this is ridiculously clever.  Ridiculously.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/lwoj3vaj4e

Or, with a less graphical representation:
https://sudokupad.app/e3ypqq87ck

Rules:
Place a digit from 1-8 in every cell such that a digit does not appear twice in a row, column, 2x4 box. Cells separated by a single king’s move cannot contain the same digit. The diagram shows a Chess game after 5.0 moves (5 white moves and 5 black moves); draw lines representing each move that has been made up to this point; all lines are straight except any representing a knight's move (which is represented as a single line that moves two orthogonal steps in one direction followed by one step in a perpendicular direction); all lines are considered distinct from each other, even if they share cells with other lines. The lines representing the odd-numbered moves (i.e. each player's 1st, 3rd and 5th moves) are Region Sums Lines ie 2x4 box borders divide a Region Sums Line into segments, whose digits have the same sum. The lines representing even-numbered moves are Renban Lines (ie  dgits on a Renban Line form a non-repeating consecutive set). Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.

title: Marty's Snake-Run Sudoku!
description:
*** JUNE SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION TOMORROW ***
Tomorrow afternoon, we launch a brand new sudoku hunt competition on Patreon. It's a hunt by yttrio and features a story and 13 puzzles.  

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today it is Marty Sears' birthday! And many of you have written in to wish Marty many happy returns and express warm wishes to this incredible sudoku constructor. We've been tipped off that Marty would like us to try and solve his puzzle Ophidiophobia... so that's what Simon tries to do!  This may be more Snake Run than Rat Run but it's got all the usual brilliance!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zmckmtohx1

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw 4 snakes, moving orthogonally through the grid. Snakes may not move diagonally, branch, enter cages, cross themselves, or share cells with each other. But they may touch themselves and each other in any way they like.

Each circled digit lies at one end of a snake, and indicates how many marked 3x3 boxes that snake visits. Digits in a cage sum to the clue in the corner (if one is given.) Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Each snake follows ONE AND ONLY ONE of the four rules below (breaking all the other rules at least once.) Each snake follows a different rule.

• ALTERNATING PARITY: Digits along the snake alternate between odd and even.
• GERMAN WHISPER: Adjacent digits have a difference of at least 5.
• PALINDROME: The snake reads the same in either direction.
• NON-VENOMOUS: No pair of adjacent digits anywhere along the snake sum to exactly the 'venom value'. The venom value (which is the same for any snake) is to be deduced.

title: Two AIs Compete At Variant Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've been working for over a year with Sakana AI on ideas around improving reasoning in AI.  So far no AI has been able to make any decent progress with even the most basic variant sudoku (in terms of solving it in a human way). Last night's puzzle (The Composite Thread by palpot) contains some really clever initial logic that might be obvious to many human solvers.  Can the latest AIs spot it and use it to solve the puzzle?

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/15rywuvxz9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 box). The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. (Eg r2c6+r3c6=r4c7+r4c8+r4c9). The digits along each line must sum to a unique number, and the sums of these lines must form a set of consecutive numbers.

The prompt Simon gives to Grok3 and Gemini 2.5 Pro was as follows:

"Imagine a blank sudoku grid. In this grid are five lines:
A line passing through the centres of r3c2, r2c2, r2c3, r1c3, r2c4, r1c5, r1c6, r2c7, r1c8, r1c9. On this line, the sum of the first four cells=the sum of the next three cells=the sum of the final three cells. 
A line passing through the centres of r2c5, r3c5, r4c5, r5c6, r5c7, r5c8, r6c9, r7c9, r8c9. On this line, the sum of the first two cells=the sum of the next two cells=the sum of the next three cells = the sum of the final two cells.
A line passing through the centres of r2c6, r3c6, r4c7, r4c8, r4c9. On this line the sum of the first two cells = the sum of the final three cells.
A line passing through the centres of r7c2, r7c1, r6c1, r6c2, r5c3, r6c4, r6c5, r7c5, r7c6, r7c7, r7c8. On this line, the sum of the first two cells=the sum of the next three cells=the sum of the next two cells=the sum of the next two cells=the sum of the final two cells.
A line passing through the centres of r9c1, r8c2, r7c3, r8c4, r8c5, r8c6, r9c7, r8c8. On this line, the sum of the first three cells=the sum of the next three cells=the sum of the final two cells. 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. In addition, the digits along each line must sum to a unique total; and the sums of these lines must form a set of consecutive numbers."

title: Drunk Sudoku Expert Attempts Musical Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon has been out to lunch... And, well, he was a little late starting this recording.  Thanks are due to Chip Sounder who recommended this puzzle, Three In The Spotlight by sshrpe. It's a lovely, approachable fog-of-war sudoku - with musical theming throughout.  Will tipsy Simon stumble through it?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ocw0x2hxdd

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Fill the grid such that the digits 1-9 appear once each in every row, column and 3×3 box. Three in the Corner/Three in the Spotlight: Every 3x3 box must have a 3 in the centre, or in one of its four corners. Every Whisper: Every instance of a constraint (ie a single line, single dot, or single cage) must include at least one 3. Three’s Company: Every 3 must be horizontally adjacent (i.e. to the left or right) to at least one multiple of 3. I Can Three Clearly Now the Fog Has Gone: The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in any cell on the grid will clear fog from that cell. Placing a 3 correctly will also clear fog from cells elsewhere on the grid. Digits along a pink line cannot repeat, and must form a set of consecutive numbers. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Every set of three adjacent digits on a striped teal line contains one digit each from the sets {147}, {258}, and {369}. Digits cannot repeat within a cage, and must sum to the small number in the corner. Cells separated by a white dot must contain digits which are consecutive. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits such that one is double the other.

description:

We absolutely love this new idea from ChinStrap and Calvinball in which a cell next to a 2 gets its value converted to 2!  It's like a religious experience in the form of sudoku :)

title: The Immortal Sudoku Snail Assassin
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most amusing and brilliant puzzle ideas ever today from VikingPrime who recalls the internet meme about the immortal snail assassin! (?!)  It was originally invented on @roosterteeth over 10 years ago and you can read more about it here:
https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/immortal-snail

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/fleyhg6tnu

Rules:
Chiki the Monkey has taken the forbidden bargain! He has obtained immortality and vast wealth but will forever be hunted by a snail assassin who will draw ever closer. Help keep Chiki alive while he collects his earnings and settles in for the night.
Fill the 9×9 grid so that every row, column and marked 3×3 box contains the digits 1-9 without repeats. Mangoes separate two consecutive digits, while Coconuts separate two digits where one is double the other. Not all fruit has been given.
Draw a path for Chiki through the centre of grid cells, towards the feast of fruit awaiting him. Chiki may move orthogonally or diagonally — if there is room to do so —but may not revisit or cross his own path, nor can he pass through any bright blue maze walls.
The snail that hunts him has spoiled one of the digits in the grid. This forbidden digit — the "poison digit" — must be avoided at all costs. 
Chiki's path is separated by box borders into segments; each segment acts as a "thermometer" and must strictly increase numerically from where he enters (the "bulb") to where he leaves (the "tip"). Chiki must collect ALL Golden Coins, which represent an almost complete set of the digits 1-9 (excepting, of course, the poison digit). These must also be collected in numerical order, starting low and ending high.
You may think this task trivial but do not become overconfident, for there's yet one problem...decoy snail. Decoy snails are safe to cross, of course, but what if it isn't a decoy...?

title: Is This A Sudoku? A New Discovery
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A philosophical question today in response to one of the most extraordinary grids/discoveries.  This time it's Michael Lefkowitz (Juggler) who has come up with something amazing: it's called Square Of Squares and, as one commentator wrote, "If puzzles like this don’t make you see the beauty of math I don’t know what will..."!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0o823lt42s

Rules:
LATIN SQUARE - Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row and column. LATIN SQUARES - Subdivide the grid into smaller latin squares, which can be any size except 1×1. An N×N latin square contains exactly N unique digits selected from 1 to 9 (such that those N unique digits do not repeat in any row/column of their latin square). Latin squares with the same size may not have the same digit in the same relative position. (Eg if a 4×4 latin square has a 7 in its upper left corner, no other 4×4 latin square may have a 7 in its upper left corner). Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.

description:

title: Possibly The Best Fog Sudoku We've Seen!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another fog sudoku with the "uniqueness" rule tonight - this time from Visumation.  It's apparently the 4th puzzle in a series and it's so good. Every deduction feels novel and clever - don't miss this one!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/sq3rfco0oe

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference of at least 5. B) Neighbouring digits on an orange Dutch Whisper (DW)  line must have a difference of at least 4. C) Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. D) Along purple zipper (Z) lines, pairs of digits equidistant from the centre of the line have the same sum. On odd-length zipper lines, this sum is the value of the digit in the central position. E) Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the clue in the top left of that cage (if given). Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in this puzzle. Eg. If 2 appears on a GW line then no other 2 may appear on any GW line in the puzzle. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.

title: The New Fog Sudoku Rule We LOVE!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We solved the original sudoku by Belamis with this ruleset a while ago and this is the latest in the series: the idea is that each constraint type must not have a repeated digit on it. It leads to some lovely logic and, although this is not the hardest puzzle we've ever showcased, it's right up there in terms of the amount of joy it'll give you!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/gavbek5s69

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Kropki: Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Killer: Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner if given. Thermo: Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip. Dutch Whispers: Along orange lines, digits must differ from their neighbors by at least 4. German Whispers: Along green lines, digits must differ from their neighbors by at least 5. Parity: Along a red line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even.  Each constraint type above may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g. If one Thermo contains a 5, then no other Thermo may contain a 5 etc. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placing digits will clear the fog around that cell. No guessing is required.

title: A 100% Rated Sudoku That's 'Smooth As Butter'!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A ridiculously good sudoku tonight from yttrio combing yin yang with something called "internal x-sums" - a complicated phrase for something relatively simple!  This puzzle is one of VERY few on the whole of Logic Masters that has a 100% rating but only a 3* or less difficulty rating... so do give it a go if you can!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ck24rsi50z

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. Small numbers in the corners of cells are ‘internal X-Sum’ clues: The digit in a cell with a clue gives the total number of cells (including itself) of the same shading as itself seen in all horizontal/vertical directions combined (cells of the opposite shading block the vision).  Those cells sum to the number given by the clue.  Digits may repeat within a sum if allowed by other rules.

This week, in support of myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME)/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, you may be interested in checking out Simon's brother Mike's JustGiving page.  Mike has been running marathons in Europe for over a decade in support of liME (Invest in ME Research) :

title: Marty's Foggy Sudoku Mischief
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
There can be few things better to combine in sudoku than Marty Sears and Fog-Of-War! Tonight's puzzle does just that - it's called Mischief and it's perfectly wonderful from start to finish!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/6dugnv08rk

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Entering a correct digit will clear the fog in that cell, and maybe some others too. No guessing is required. Spots divide lines into segments. A 'segment total' is the sum of the digits in that segment. Digits may not repeat within a segment. Along a BLUE LINE, each segment has the same total. Along a PINK LINE, all the individual segment totals form a non-repeating consecutive sequence, but the segments can appear in any order (eg: 11, 13, 10, 9, 12.) Along a yellow line, any two segment totals anywhere on the line may not be consecutive or the same (eg: if there is a segment whose cells sum to 12, then no other segment may have a total of 11, 12 or 13.) One of the digits 1-9 (to be determined) is the 'mischief digit.' Every line follows one of the three line rules above, but any line containing the mischief digit has been painted the wrong colour. (Any line NOT containing the mischief digit is the correct colour.)

title: This IS an Absolute Banger!
description:
Here's where you can try Whispering Internal Loop Skyscrapers by Yttrio: https://sudokupad.app/kwf3g2ne92 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). Each cell on the loop represents a skyscraper with a height equal to its value (non-loop cells are not skyscrapers). A digit in a clued cell gives the number of skyscrapers visible in the indicated direction (not including the cell itself), where skyscrapers block the view of skyscrapers with the same or lower height behind them. The clued cell may or may not be on the loop.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Scojo's last sudoku was a total joy and, on his birthday, he's done it again! Hungry Hungry Hippos is a wonderful take on the children's game of the same name and will make you smile from start to finish!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/65113ete79

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The four hungry hungry hippos on the edges of the grid are fighting to eat all of the large circles in the grid. If a circle is entirely within the colored territory of a single hippo, that circle will be eaten by that hippo. If a circle is on the border between multiple hippos' territories, which hippo eats that circle must be determined. A number on a hippo shows the sum of all circles that it eats. A digit on a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit. Digits separated by a small white dot are consecutive. These dots are too small for the hippos to care about, so they are not eaten. title: This Will Be One Of The Puzzles Of The Year.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon opens tonight's sudoku live and is faced with a completely original ruleset from SeveNateNine called Productivity Killer.  The fact that this grid exists at all is extraordinary enough but the varied and wonderful logic that the constructor has baked into it makes this VERY special indeed.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/egdqy9d7al

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A cage is a set of orthogonally connected cells which do not contain repeated digits. Cages may not overlap each other. The sum of digits in a given cage is equal to the product of all individual side-lengths of that cage. (NB This does not necessarily equal the area of that cage). Circles appear in cages and count the total number of cells in that cage. Squares indicate that a cell is not in any cage. All possible Circles and Squares are given.

title: Unique Digits Under The Sudoku Fog!
description:
*** MONDAY'S BLUE PRINCE STREAM ***
You can (re)watch last night's stream here:
https://youtube.com/live/CFbzCGnr1K8

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Fog Of War sudoku returns tonight with a brilliant puzzle from Visumation called Unique Under The Fog. We love this sort of ruleset (which was invented, we believe, by Belamis) as it leads to some fresh and fun logic. Nothing not to love here, give it a go!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/4fimlq2cm2

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 1) Digits on a purple Renban (RB) line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits. 2) The 3x3 box borders divide blue Region Sum (RS) lines into segments with the same sum. 3) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference if at least 5. 4) Neighbouring digits on a red line (P) must alternate parity. 5) Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). 6) Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. 7) Cells with a grey square contain an even digit. Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in this puzzle. Eg. If one renban line contains a 5, then no other renban line may contain a 5. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid.

title: Construction in the Fog!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Foggy “Pair”-rows by Visumation: https://sudokupad.app/yk82v3oj6m 
The grid is partially covered in fog. The fog will clear from surrounding cells when a digit is placed correctly. There are nine 3x3 regions in the grid which have to be located – each contains the digits 1-9. No row or column can repeat a digit. A clue outside the grid indicates how many cells belong to regions in the direction pointed to, and those cells must sum to a multiple of the clue. 
A digit in a cell with arrows indicate the sum of the digits in the cells N steps away in the directions pointed to, where N is the digit in the cell with the arrows. Empty cells do not contribute to the “steps”-count. A black dot separates digits with a 1:2 ratio.

title: Sudoku's Holographic Principle
description:
*** MAY SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION JUST OUT ***
Our new competition launched TODAY. It's a sudoku hunt from Blobz called Oil and Water. The prize this month is a chance to make a sudoku video with Simon that will appear on the channel!

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Congratulations to Shintaro Fushida-Hardy on defending his PhD yesterday and becoming a Doctor of Mathematics! We're celebrating by attempting his breakthrough sudoku, Holographic Principle, which has some original and beautiful logic.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/e27trjd6zv

Rules:
The digits 1 to 9 occur exactly once each in every row, column, and region. Regions cannot overlap and each consists of nine orthogonally-connected cells. The region borders must be deduced. A digit in a cell with arrow(s) gives the total number of cells in the same region as the arrow cell in all indicated directions combined (NB this count includes the arrow cell itself.) Cells in different regions to the arrow cell immediately block vision (and therefore prevent any cells further along the arrow’s path in that direction from contributing to the arrow cell’s count).

You can see an example of how the rules work here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000IZX

The musical introduction today is Indiana by the sensational Adrianne Lenker.

title: Fog Sudoku: Looks Insanely Complex, Solved with Simple Math!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Not just a debut on the channel today but the first ever puzzle created by Scott Buckley! It's called Mod Prod In The Fog and it's a gem. Lots of fundamental ideas from basic arithmetic come into play and don't be fooled into thinking you need to do lots of difficult calculations to solve this - none are necessary!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/1ej6condot

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
(Modulo) Product Lines: Digits along a line of any colour multiply (mod 10) to the digit in the attached circle of the same colour. "Mod 10" means we just take the last digit of the product. For example, 3 * 9 * 4 = 8. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by other rules. Lines do not revisit cells or cross themselves. 
Weak Kropki: Cells separated by a grey dot have a difference of 1 or 2. 
Most of the grid is covered by a grey fog. Placing the correct digit in a cell will reveal that cell and sometimes other cells. Guessing is never necessary. 

Hint: You will never need to calculate large multiplications in your head to solve this puzzle; you can take the last digit at each sub-step. For example, for 3*9*4*2, you can calculate 3*9=7, then 7*4=8, then 8*2=6.

title: Marty's Taxi Rank Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In a tribute to his friend, ThePedallingPianist, Marty Sears riffs on the full-rank sudoku ruleset with a puzzle called Taxi Rank.  This is extremely clever fare and not too tricky - though Simon's quest to finish it was troubled by a wasp...

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/61f9s2wmr3

If you find the grid above too small then this link will allow you to play:
https://sudokupad.app/zupg2dog2w

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each coloured route can be read as a 6-digit 'route number', starting at the square and finishing at the spot. These nine route numbers can be ranked from lowest to highest. A circled yellow taxi on a route indicates that route's rank. (A '1' taxi would be on the route with the smallest 6-digit route number. None of the route numbers are the same, so there are no tied ranks.) Box borders divide a BLUE ROUTE into segments whose digits have the same sum. Adjacent digits on a GREEN ROUTE have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a PINK ROUTE form a non-repeating, consecutive set in some order.

*** MONDAY'S BLUE PRINCE STREAM ***

title: Matt Parker Sets Us A Challenge!
description:
Thanks to Jane Street for sponsoring this video. 

You can apply to their WiSE program in New York, London or Hong Kong: https://jane-st.co/wise-CTC

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're both big fans of Matt Parker, the mathematician, comedian and author behind the YouTube channel @standupmaths. So it was a thrill when it turned out he had a challenge for us!!  It stems from a puzzle in this year's MIT Mystery Hunt called Maze Of Lies by Becca Chang & Denis Auroux. (Thanks too to Egregious Error for creating a sudoku version out of the original puzzle.) This is one complicated quasi-sudoku and Matt used his programming skills to crack it.  Could two "human beings" solve it without computer-assistance??!  Let's see!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/bo3con7363

Rules:
Note that to solve this puzzle from scratch you first have to determine which of the characters in the maze is telling the truth and which is lying. Matt's team found this part of the puzzle straightforward so he tasked us with the sudoku part ie revealing who the truth-tellers were at around 12minutes into the video). If you want to solve the WHOLE puzzle then you will need to deduce the liars/honest characters from the text below:

Normal sudoku rules may apply. You find yourself in a maze of regions connected by doors. Each region is made of rooms connected by passageways.
You encounter some helpful people along your travels through the rooms. Here's what they have to say:
Stephanie: Some rules apply to the whole maze. Others apply to regions.
Some people tell only lies. Some only tell the truth.
All true statements about region specific rules apply to different regions.
Daniel: Everyone lies all the time. In particular Stephanie lies all the time. Only listen to me.
I'm pretty sure Stephanie didn't even tell you the truth about what you're supposed to do here.
Some rooms contain a digit from 1-8 while others are empty.
Rooms in the same column or row containing the same digit must be further apart than the value of that digit.
Rooms containing the same digit can not touch diagonally.
Maurice is a liar.
Maurice: All rooms contain a digit from 1-9 such that no digit is repeated in a row, column, or region.
Only one digit is still visible, a five. In fact, once you know the rules of the regions you will be able to immediately place 2 more fives in the grid. Please help us find all the missing digits.
Patrick: Maurice and Helen are both telling the truth.
There is a region with a single door to the West in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must contain digits at least 4 apart.
There is a region in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must contain digits that differ by a power of 2.
There is a region in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must contain digits that are non-consecutive.
Caroline: In one region with only 2 doors the largest and smallest digits on the shortest path between the doors are next to the doors.
In another region with only 2 doors the digits on the shortest path between the doors strictly increase from one door to the other.
In yet another region with only 2 doors along the shortest path between the doors the digit next to one of the doors is equal to the sum of the remaining digits.
By the way, Annabelle is a liar.
Vladimir: Patrick is a liar.
There is a region with a single door to the South in which all numbers formed by reading the digits from North to South or West to East from wall to wall (or door) are perfect squares.
Another region read this way contains prime numbers.
A third region read this way contains multiples of 7.
Helen: Exactly one of Jessica and Annabelle is a liar.
One region of the maze is an exact clone of another, but may be rotated.
Annabelle: In one region with only 2 doors the digits on the shortest path between the doors alternate between odd and even.
In another region with only 2 doors the digits on the shortest path between the doors form a prime number when read in one direction.
In yet another region with only 2 doors the product of the digits on the shortest path between doors is a perfect square.
By the way, Caroline is a liar.
Jessica: There are either 3 or 4 liars here.
There is a region with a single door to the North in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall must not both contain prime numbers.
There is another region with a single door to the East in which orthogonally connected rooms not separated by a wall contain digits that either have a difference of 1 or one is double the other (or both!)

title: Can A Sudoku Be Super-Connected?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We had a recommendation from maths professor Dorlir for a puzzle made by a friend of his.... the sudoku is called The Wolf and the author is Fiton.  This is the first puzzle Fiton has ever made - it is an astonishing puzzle full-stop but, for this to be a debut sudoku, is absolutely extraordinary. Welcome to the world of super-connectivity!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9v0kvw4azl

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A region of shaded cells is called super connected if, in addition to being orthogonally connected, it has the property that for any two shaded cells that are in the same row or in the same column, all the cells between them are also shaded. Shade some cells so that the resulting shaded region is super connected. The number of shaded cells in each box of the grid must be at least one and must be equal to the largest digit that is shaded in that box. Different boxes must have a different number of shaded cells. In the middle box, any two digits that are consecutive must also be orthogonally adjacent. Digits connected by a black dot are in 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the value of the other).

title: Absolutely Insane. In The Best Possible Way!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today is the birthday of Malrog and yttrio, two setters we've featured many times individually over the years.  However, they have set one puzzle as a collaboration and it seems fitting to attempt that one today!  So here's Simon's battle with Kurodoku - basically a 100%-rated puzzle from last July. It is absolutely insane!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ydykj28b2l

Rules:
Place the digits from 1 to 9 exactly once in every row, column, and region. Regions consist of a set of nine orthogonally connected cells and must be determined by the solver. Shade two groups of orthogonally connected cells in each region. These groups can consist of a single cell or multiple cells. Both of a region's groups must have the same size and shape, but may be rotated or reflected. Shaded groups may not be orthogonally adjacent. Cells with arrows are not shaded, and indicate the size of a group of shaded cells which occupies the adjacent cell in the indicated direction(s). (Note: a 2 in a cell with two arrows would indicate that there was a group of size 2 in BOTH directions.) For each region whose shaded groups consist of multiple cells, one shaded group must contain a set of consecutive digits in any order, and adjacent digits within the other shaded group must differ by at least 5. The solver must determine which is which.

title: A Sudoku With Only 8 Given Digits?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Titles like these have become synonymous with the Dutch sudoku wizard Aad van de Wetering - and this one is no different. A classic "Aad" puzzle - with an original ruleset - and some beautiful logic to boot!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/i7jrq9g9oz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box.) Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. In a 3x3 box every horizontal threesome contains one digit from {1,2,3}, one from {4,5,6} and one from {7,8,9}. A positive diagonal is any diagonal going from South-West to North-East. When normal sudoku rules allow neighbouring digits on a positive diagonal to be equal they MUST be equal. eg r2c4, r3c3 and r4c2 must contain the same digit; r6c2 and r7c1 must contain the same digit; etc.

title: The Author Of 'The Miracle Sudoku' RETURNS!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy Easter! Recently Mitchell Lee, author of The Miracle Sudoku - the puzzle that featured in one of our most popular videos, invented a new type of puzzle called Fractional Sudoku.  He and Michael Lefkowitz have now crafted five puzzles showcasing this new idea and Chameleon has been good enough to make these puzzles playable in his software!

Play the puzzles at the links below (if you start with the first puzzle and finish it, you’ll be given the link for the second etc):

https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#1-close-quarters
https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#2-mitosis
https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#3-funky-town
https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#4-superposition
https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#5-fractionally-harder

More information including an example picture is here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000MX0

Rules:
This puzzle is a 4 × 4 grid of cells, which are arranged in four rows and four columns of four cells each. Cells are divided into "cell pieces" by grey lines. Write a digit from 1–4 in each cell piece. Digits may not repeat in a cell. In each row, column, and box, the total area of the cell pieces containing the digit 1 must equal the area of a single cell. The same is true for the digits 2, 3, and 4. When cell pieces in the same cell have equal size, you may enter their digits in either order.

Here's where you can try One of the Two by Oskode: https://sudokupad.app/ayk7228tr8 
Oskode says: I placed a bunch of constraints in my puzzle but I was stupid enough to use the same colors for similar looking constraints... Can you help me check if the puzzle is still solvable? I know that:
Normal sudoku rules apply. One cage sums to 15; the other one is a Look-and-say cage, that says it has “one 5”. One of the orange dots joins consecutive digits; the other joins digits with a 1:2 ratio. One of the Y's joins two digits that sum to 5; the other joins two digits that sum to 10. Along one of the blue diagonals digits may not repeat; box borders divide the other one into segments with the same sum. One red line contains a sequence of digits, in any order; along the other one adjacent digits have a difference of at least 5. Along one of the lines connected to the grey bulb digits increase from the bulb; along the other the digits sum to the digit in the bulb. One orientation of the grey triangles (pointing up/down) contains even digits; the other orientation contains odd digits. One dark blue line reads the same in both directions; along the other each three digits include one from {147}, one from {258}, one from {369}. On one green line digits on the line must be between the number in circles; on the other digits on the line sum to the total of the two circles.

title: Simon Faces Sudoku's Big Bad Wolf...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
About once a month, Simon battles with the sudoku genius IcyFruit.  These videos are longer than normal because IcyFruit's puzzles are VERY HARD.  Many of you have requested this one... it's called Big Bad Wolf and, although Simon does find it very challenging, he would like it noted that this is a GENIUS construction.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/8cs9gx5dfg

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Place a digit from 1-9 in every cell such that each digit appears exactly once in every row, column, and region. Region boundaries divide the line into segments. The digit in the Nth cell of a segment indicates the position of the digit N on that segment. Positions are counted starting from 1 at an end of the segment which much be determined. Different segments may count in different directions relative to the line.

title: It's Sudoku But It's In 3D!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What happens when you combine the brains of two of the most inventive setters in the sudoku world?!  Madness!!  Shintaro Fushida-Hardy and Michael Lefkowitz have come up with the idea of "layered sudokus" featuring some windows that look through to lower layers.  This puzzle isn't too tricky and will probably make you laugh :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/t9yym962w0?setting-nogrid=1

Rules:
In each of the four stacked grids, normal 4x4 Sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 4, once each, into every row, column and 2x2 box.) The value of a cell with a window is the sum of its digit and the digit in the cell from a different grid that can be seen through the window. title: That's 4 in the Corner!
description:
Here's where you can attempt There's a 4 in the corner!  by Md88keys: https://sudokupad.app/c63io2bpp2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line form a set of consecutive digits in any order. Neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. Neighbouring digits along an orange line have a difference of at least 4. Box borders divide a blue line into segments which have the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. Digits in cells joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.

title: This Sudoku Has Invisible Lines!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears and Justin Vitanza have created an absolutely amazing sudoku with invisible lines!  There is ample opportunity during Simon's solve for him to use one of his favourite words, as well as for him to apparently go mad when reading through the rules...!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/j0e1hqfsp4

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 3x3 box contains an invisible 'index line' whose route must be determined. The index lines are all 9 cells long, only move orthogonally (not diagonally), and don't cross any 3x3 box borders. They don't cross themselves, or pass through any black or green spots. Each row, column and box contains exactly one hidden diamond, which lies at one end of its index line, and contains its box number. (Boxes are numbered 1-9 in normal reading order from top left to bottom right.) The digit in position N along an index line (starting at the end with the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N should be placed. Eg: if the 1st digit is a 3, then the 3rd digit will be a 1. Digits separated by a black spot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Digits separated by a green spot have a difference of at least 5.

title: This Sudoku's Solve Count Is WILD!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Sometimes we solve a sudoku and think "wow, that would be enjoyed by a LOT of people".  Today is such a day.  Belamis' puzzle Foggy Regional Constraints is a sequel to a wonderful sudoku from a few days ago but this one incorporates the fog-of-war mechanic beautifully. 

(As an aside, the solve count for this one is wild after only a day.  We wonder if any of the wizards out there could explain to us how our thumbnail could automatically update once a day to show the current solve count?!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/3w7wprj07z

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in dynamic fog. Correctly placed digits may remove fog from other cells. Guessing is not required. German Whispers: Along green lines, digits must differ from their neighbours by at least 5. Killer: Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner if given. Renban: Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Parity: Along a peach line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even. Kropki: Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Each constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g. ALL renban cells must contain no repeated digits, ALL cells connected by a kropki dot must contain no repeated digits etc.

title: Who Is In The Sudoku Penthouse?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears and Lorena team up today with a fascinating idea about tessellating a fog-of-war sudoku grid into tetrominoes, pentominoes and Ocho (the cat)! It's called Penthouse and Simon recommends reading the rules - it can help with solving the puzzle ;)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/rpdtjt36r7?setting-nogrid=1&setting-hidebgimage=0&setting-digitoutlines=0

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered with fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. Five tetrominoes (shapes made of 4 orthogonally connected cells) have just moved into a large house with 12 pentominoes (shapes made of 5 orthogonally connected cells). No two characters are exactly the same shape (rotations and reflections count as the same, e.g. there is only one L tetromino). There is also a pet cat called Ocho, who occupies just one cell. Fit all 18 occupants into the grid so that none of them overlap. Outlines of characters are shown with a thick black line. A small clue appearing anywhere within a character indicates the total sum of all the digits in that character. No two characters have the same total. Digits never repeat on a character. Around the grid are photos of some (not all) of the characters. Each photo shows a character as it appears in the grid, unreflected (i.e. photos are not mirrored). It also shows one of its digits, with its correct orientation and position within the character. (Each character must be placed in the grid so that its given digit is up the right way.)

https://youtube.com/shorts/Ukbboeudbm8?feature=share

title: The Most BONKERS Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Complete insanity tonight from ICHTUES, whose puzzle SET features one of the sparsest grids and weirdest rulesets we've seen.  The logic hidden in this one is rather beautiful - if you can find it!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/929l9v2qt5

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a marked diagonal cannot repeat. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Cells with the same relative position within a 3x3 box must contain different digits. (Eg the middle-left position of r2c1, r2c4, r2c7, r5c1, r5c4, r5c7, r8c1,r8c4 & r8c7 must all be different). Let a digit's entropy describe if it is low (123), medium (456), or high (789). Let its modularity be its remainder when divided by 3. Let a SET be a set of three digits such that their entropy and modularity are either all the same or all different. Some examples of SETs are: 789 (same entropy, different modularity), 258 (different entropy, same modularity), 168 and 348 (different entropy and different modularity). In this puzzle, the three rows and three columns of each box all form SETs.

title: Under the Radar, Hidden by Fog
description:
Here's where you can attempt Under the Radar by Guru: https://sudokupad.app/vr35ejkt5p 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Hidden in the grid (to be placed by the solver) are 9 radar cells; one in each row, column and 3x3 box. A radar cell looks out at the edges of the grid in each of the orthogonal directions and potentially scans the cell at each edge. The digit in a radar cell indicates the number of cells scanned by the radar cell. The value of a radar cell is the total of the digits in the cells scanned by the radar cell.
Example: Suppose R4C5 was a radar cell. It would then be looking at R1C5, R4C1, R4C9, and R9C5 as the cells it may scan. If the digit in the radar cell was a 2, that would indicate that 2 out of those 4 cells are being scanned and the value of the radar cell is the total of those 2 cells. Note that a radar cell never scans itself.
The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit will clear the fog from that cell and potentially from other cells somewhere in the grid. Adjacent VALUES on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Adjacent DIGITS on a brown line must have a difference of at least 5. Values on a pink line form a set of non-repeating consecutive numbers in any order. Digits within a cage do not repeat and the values within a cage sum to the clue in the top left corner of the cage. Values separated by a black dot have a 2-to-1 ratio. Values separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are necessarily given.

title: Family Trees can be Puzzling!
description:
Here's where you can try Binary Trees by Azvaril: https://sudokupad.app/02n5l1x503 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Circles and lines form binary trees. One tree is a min binary tree and the other is a max binary tree. Which is which is up to the solver to determine. 
In a min binary tree, each parent node is smaller than its children. IN a max binary tree, each parent node is larger than its children. Digits on the tree do not repeat.
A black dot between two cells indicates that one of the digits is twice as big as the other digit. 
ALL possible black dots are given.

title: Can You Solve The Fog Sudoku Murder Mystery?!
description:
*** APRIL SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION TOMORROW ***
Our April Fools themed sudoku hunt went live YESTERDAY.  You could win Emily Williams' homemade sudoku cushion cover!!  

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Visit the Lost Village today and try to solve the murder mystery from .proxz14 in a seriously clever fog sudoku.  It doesn't seem like this one should be too complicated but the logic is surprising and interesting throughout.  Do give it a try!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/cm62bq81c2

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. There are 4 types of cages in this puzzle, all of which appear at least once. Digits in a cage, regardless of its type, can't repeat. 1) Killer Cages: Digits in a killer cage sum to the value given in the top left corner. There is only one killer cage in the grid. 2) Suspect Cages: The sum of the digits in a suspect cage must be 1 away from the value given in the top left corner. 3) Framed Cages: The sum of the digits in a framed cage must be 2 away from the value given in the top left corner. 4) Innocent Cages: The sum of the digits in an innocent cage must be at least 10 away from the value given in the top left corner. The grid is covered by fog. Placing correct digits will gradually uncover the rest of the grid. Guessing is not required. The fog will never uncover two cages of the same type at once, including the starting cages. To help with tracking, cages that were *fully* uncovered at the same stage have the same colours.

description:
*** APRIL SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION ***
Our April Fools themed sudoku hunt will go live on 1 April at 4pm UK time.  (It will - this is NOT an April Fool!)

Two lines we've seen before but not together make an appearance in Graded On A Curve by ChinStrap and sujoyku tonight.  The interactions are beautiful in this quite lovely sudoku. Enjoy!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/3i3xlin7gl

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each turquoise line is an Index Line, i.e. the digit in the Nth cell along such a line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example, if a diamond cell contains a 3, the third cell along that line must have a 1. The yellow lines are Nabner Lines, i.e. on such a line there may not be consecutive or repeated digits. For example, if a 5 lies on a Nabner line, this line may not contain another 5 and neither a 4 nor a 6.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. No two adjacent cells (orthogonally or diagonally) may contain the same digit. No two cells which are a camel's move away from each may contain the same digit. title: Modular Mayhem: Understanding Maths With Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Two maths professors suggested we try this puzzle by Toomas_!  It's called Modular Mayhem and it involves modulo 9 - don't worry if you're unfamiliar with the mathematics here - Simon has to learn it all too!

It took our two maths heroes (FullDeck & Missing a Few Cards) a little time to solve this one so don't be alarmed if you don't fly through this in 20minutes :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

Mathematical instruction version (which Simon attempts in the video):
https://sudokupad.app/n3s05tso9a

Version with instructions written for non-mathematicians:
https://sudokupad.app/3i9fb2ozk1

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply (ie Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column, and 3x3 box). All clues must be calculated modulo 9. (ie if you divide a number by 9, it is the “remainder” that is considered for the purposes of the clues.  eg 16 is 7 mod 9 because 9 divides in 16 once with a 7 remainder; 27 is 0 mod 9, etc). Two digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive, i.e. one of them is equal to one more than the other modulo 9. Two digits separated by a black dot must be in a 2:1 ratio, i.e. one of them is equal to twice the other modulo 9. Two digits separated by a red dot must be BOTH consecutive AND in a 2:1 ratio. ALL possible red dots are given. The digits in a cage do not repeat and their sum is equal to the digit in its top-left corner, modulo 9. The sum of the digits along the leading diagonal is equal to 1 modulo 9. (Mathematicians may prefer the word “congruent” instead of “equal” in these instructions).

title: One Of My Favourite Puzzles In Months!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon and Mark know a few adjectives but they are struggling to properly express their admiration for Scojo's new sudoku: Rapuzzle.  It's got everything: a beautiful theme; super logic; wit AND it's not especially hard (whilst still being clever).  Hard to know what more you could get from a sudoku - do give this one a go!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/annx3u5j3p

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single chess knight's move cannot contain the same digit. Cells that are part of the grey tower must be greater than all orthogonally adjacent non-tower cells. Note: any cell that the tower even partially covers is considered a tower cell. Every group of 3 cells along Rapunzel's hair must contain one low digit (1, 2, 3), one medium digit (4, 5, 6), and one high digit (7, 8, 9). Note, for the avoidance of doubt, that Rapunzel's hair begins in row 4 column 2.

title: I'm Just a Teenage Vampire, Baby
description:
Here's where you can try Teenage Vampire Slayer by Blobz: https://sudokupad.app/blobz/teenage-vampire-slayer 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each wooden stake (line) sums to either 16 or 17. Each grave (cage) sums to the value shown. There are 9 vampires (digits 1-9 once each) in the grid; one in each row, column and box. There are also 9 victims (digits 1-9 once each) in the grid; one in each row, column and box. For purposes of cage and line totals: (a) vampire cells have a value equal to the sum of their digit plus the digit of the victim cell in their box, and (b) victim cells have a value of 0.

title: A Simple and BRILLIANT Twist On Killer Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An exceptional idea and execution tonight from Belamis in the form of their puzzle Smallest Chaotic Killer.  The idea is that the smallest digit in a cage indicates how many regions enter that cage and it works phenomenally!  Definitely a sudoku that will bring you a lot of joy - give it a try if you can.
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/frb3c5cxkr

Rules:
Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region contains the digits 1-9 once each. The smallest digit in each cage counts the number of different regions that enter that cage.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today is the day marking 5 years since Mark and Simon started doing 2 videos every day (ie the start of the first COVID lockdown in the UK). We thought it would be appropriate to pick an older puzzle so here is Quines by Manus Hand - which we certainly ought to have looked at a long time ago. https://sudokupad.app/8l2cabq2sj

Normal sudoku rules apply. The two digit number within the red cage in each coloured region is the sum total of all the digits in that region. title: Another Tic Tac Toe Showdown!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Noughts and Crosses by CraigFJ: https://sudokupad.app/6ykv9wd48f 
Even Steven and Odd Todd are playing noughts and crosses (tic tac toe). Steven plays even digits, Todd plays odd digits. A red line in a sudoku box indicates three cells of the same parity- the winning line in a noughts and crosses grid. This is the only straight line of three cells of the same parity within that box’s borders. If the red line contains even digits, Steven wins the box. If the line contains odd digits, Todd wins the box. To find the overall winner, the completed sudoku grid will contain exactly one straight winning line of 3 boxes won by either Steven or Todd.
Normal sudoku rules apply. White dots separate consecutive digits and black dots separate digits in a 1:2 ratio. X and V separate digits which sum to 10 or 5 respectively.

title: New A.I. Benchmark ANNOUNCED: Our Sudokus!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's sudoku is called Parity Fish and it's been made for us specially by none other than Marty Sears (thanks Marty!).  The backstory behind this puzzle is something we hope you might find interesting:

Llion Jones, one of the innovators of the technology behind ChatGPT, approached us a few months ago with an idea.  He'd realised that it might be possible to improve how well AIs "reasoned" by showing them examples of human being's "thinking" - and our videos represent a huge collection of data in which humans do just that.  

He and his Japan-based company, Sakana AI, announced at yesterday's Nvidia conference in San Jose a new benchmark for assessing how well AIs are "thinking" - a collection of variant sudoku puzzles designed to test exactly that.  If this is something that interests you, let us know! You can read more about it here: https://sakana.ai/sudoku-bench/

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/o0n73yxg22

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply ie fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that digits don't repeat in any row, column, and marked 3x3 box. Two cells adjacent along a red line must contain one even digit and one odd digit. Two cells connected by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Two cells connected by a black dot contain digits where one is double the other.

Simon couldn't resist the Scrabble Sudoku mentioned during today's introduction.  His solve of LMDemasi's puzzle is available on Patreon now!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the best dynamic fog of war sudokus we've seen tonight from pdyxs called Recounting The Rooms.  It is extremely clever as it begins straightforwardly and teaches you how its constraints work so that, by the time the fog clears, it feels easier to finish!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/belm8cdujp

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply in the central 9x9 area of the puzzle. A black dot between two digits means that one is double the other. Clues outside the grid indicate the digit which must be placed in the Nth *revealed* cell along the corresponding row or column, where N is the digit in the first *revealed* cell in that direction. (“Revealed” means “unfogged”.) A digit X in a *revealed* circle appears in *revealed* circles X times. The grid is covered in fog. Once all visible numbered room clues are satisfied, some of the fog will lift to reveal more cells and clues. The digits outside the grid are unstable - that is, they may change values when the fog clears. (Any digits placed inside the 9x9 grid will remain stable.)

description:
Here's where you can try the 6x6 puzzle Killer dots of the Knight by Chip Sounder: https://sudokupad.app/HB7MTHjGmM 
Place the digits 1-6 in each row, column and 2x3 box without repetition. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat (if allowed by other rules). Digits in a dotted cage sum to the given total. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.

title: The Sudoku That Starts Simple And Ends Genius!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Anothing fog-of-war treat this evening - this time from Marty Sears and Ratfinkz.  It involves a new type of constraint, which has similarities to "index lines" but this one is "hitlines".  It's a wonderful puzzle which teaches you its principles as it goes along and saves some genius for the end!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/x75we00sgg

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. Digits along a beige 'hitline' do not repeat. The number on a blue circle (or two-digit pill reading downwards or from left to right) points to the first cell ('position 1') along a hitline, and indicates the total of any digits that equal their position number along that hitline. Eg: on a 4-cell hitline, if the sequence of digits reads 1694 starting from the cell being pointed at, then the blue total would be 5 (the sum of 1 and 4) because 1 is in the 1st position and 4 is in the 4th position, and these are the only digits which match their position numbers.

title: The Friday Night Sudoku Club
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Lots of love tonight to our Friday night viewers who spend the start of their weekends with us!  Some great viewer shoutouts this evening too as well as, of course, a new world-class sudoku puzzle.  This one is called Hyperextension and it's a collaboration between Matt Tressel and ChinStrap.  It involves a couple of new rules, both of which work magically together!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/3gkoee7rau

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages. If the sum of a cage is a 1-digit number, that number must be in the cell pointed at by the cage's northwest corner. If the sum is a 2-digit number, it must be in the domino formed by that cell and the one to its left. (Example: if the sum of the cage in Box 3 was 9, then r1c6 would be 9. If it's sum was 12, then r1c5 would be 1 and r1c6 would be 2.) Every set of 4 adjacent digits on a peach line must contain a digit from each of the X-pair (ten-pair) subsets of {1,9}, {2,8}, {3,7}, and {4,6}. A 5 may not appear on a peach line. Digits on a line may repeat if allowed by other rules.

title: Dungeons & Dragons: A Fog Sudoku Adventure
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A completely stunning experience tonight from Nurator who has created a series of sudoku dungeons for us to explore - all as part of the same solve.  One commentator has described this as their favourite solve ever and we can see why.  It's really pretty extraordinary that there are actually four individually excellent puzzles wrapped up in one grid!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/j22idv1qhe

Rules:
Welcome to the dungeon! Can you find your way through the different rooms of the dungeon and reach all checkpoints with an evolving class?
Normal Sudoku Rules apply.
Digits in cages (rooms) do not repeat and sum to the total if given.
Adventure Path: 
Draw a path starting at the first check point (the green square with a 1) to every visible checkpoint in ascending order. The path only travels orthogonally and must visit each cage (room). 
The path can never travel outside of rooms nor checkpoints and can only enter and exit any cage (room) exactly once.
Dynamic Fog: Each time you determine the exact path and the digit in the highest visible checkpoint cell, put it in to reveal a new checkpoint and new cages. 
Dynamic Classes: Each time you reveal new cells, delete the path and all entered digits that are not on checkpoints. Then change your class, which determines the line type all cells on the path have to obey.

List of classes (you start with Palindrome):
1-2 : Palindrome: Digits on a palindrome path read the same forwards and backwards.
1-2-3: German Whisper: Two cells connected by a German Whisper path must have a difference of at least 5.
1-2-3-4: Region Sum: Box borders divided the path into segments of equal sums.
1-2-3-4-5: Dutch Whisper: Two cells connected by a Dutch Whisper path must have a difference of at least 4.

You have completed the dungeon when all 5 checkpoints are revealed and the complete grid is filled.

title: The Sudoku With Two IMPOSSIBLE Sides
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The last month or so has seen the return of ICHTUES to constructing and this puzzle, Old Maid, is one of his very best.  It's NOT easy - 5/5 for difficulty - but it's pretty unbelievable that this solves at all!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/s8eq4xfzrq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Place doubler-cells into the grid so that there is exactly one doubler-cell in each row, column and box. Each doubler-cell must contain a different digit and the value of a doubler-cell is twice the value of the contained digit. On both marked diagonals there are no repeated VALUES. VALUES along a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive set, in any order. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments which each have the same sum (ie the sum of their VALUES is the same).

title: Please Don't Ignore This Marty Sears Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new week and, luckily for us, a new Marty Sears sudoku!  It's called Please Ignore - but please don't!  (It reminds Simon of his teenage band - which was called The Intermission, in the hope everyone would assume it was a break in proceedings ensuring there would be no audience...!)

It's classic Marty fare - with lovely (and original logic throughout) and only 2/5 for difficulty!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/h1zrlsc75s

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. One digit from 1-9 (to be determined) is 'inactive' and always gets ignored by any line it appears on. Today we're continuing our series where we invite well-known YouTubers to come on the channel and solve a sudoku with us!  We're absolutely thrilled to welcome music icon and all-round polymath @KurtHugoSchneider to tackle Decapitated by Black_Doom, a 5-star rated sudoku - which Kurt will absolutely demolish!!  

Kurt's YouTube channel has over 13.5million subscribers - and his biggest videos boast over 200million views (!!) description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into islands of one or more orthogonally connected cells such that no two islands touch each other orthogonally. All non-island cells are in the ocean which must be a contiguous region of orthogonally connected cells that never completely fills a 2x2 area. Each black dot connects 2 island cells. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Each white dot connects an ocean and island cell. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Each island contains exactly 3 different digits (with potential repeats), with the highest digit being equal to the island’s size.

description:
Sorry about the first attempted upload!
Here's where you can try Sandwich Additives by DiMono: https://sudokupad.app/s7e0q68rum 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are clues outside the grid. Each side either contains all Sandwich clues, or all X-Sum clues. Which side contains which type of clue is to be determined by the solver.
A sandwich clue gives the total of the digits placed between 1 and 9 in the row or column. An X-Sum clue gives the sum of the first X cells that are seen in the row or column from the clue, where X is the first seen cell (i.e. a clue of 8 could be satisfied by 26 or 314 or 341).

title: The Snake that Changes its Mind!
description:
Here's where you can try The Score is Still Q to 12! by Calvinball: https://sudokupad.app/syjv7l5c1o 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a snake in the grid. A snake is a one-cell-wide path of orthogonally connected cells which may not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally. Arrow cells are always on the snake, and count the total amount of snake cells seen in all indicated directions (If R8C6 sees 4 cells up its column and 2 cells along the diagonal then it would be a 6). Arrow cells do not count themselves. Circle cells are the head and tail of the snake, and count the total number of snake cells in their box.
Cages represent different zones which dictate how the snake functions through each zone. In the GW Zone the snake functions as a German Whisper Line, along which adjacent digits differ by at least 5. In the ENT Zone the snake functions as an Entropic Line, along which any three consecutive cells contain a low digit {1,2,3}, a medium digit {4,5,6}, and a high digit {7,8,9}. Where the snake crosses between different zones the connection doesn’t need to be either Entropic or German Whisper. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.

title: The Sudoku With Only 2 Given CAMELS??!
description:
*** MARCH SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION ***
We welcome in the month of March with a brand new sudoku hunt competition from Blobz (who made The Hobbit and the Lord Of The Rings hunts in 2024). It went live on 1 March and the closing date is 20th March!

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
More lunacy today in the form of Help! My Flatmate Is A Camel by Lorena... and a miracle sudoku in all bar name.  With just two given Camels in the grid it doesn't seem likely it can possibly have a unique solution and yet...

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/hj7tmm15ln

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. A camel’s move in fairy chess is a jump of three squares horizontally and one square vertically or three squares vertically and one square horizontally. Any cell a camel’s move away from a camel cell has to contain a digit that is either consecutive or in a 2:1 ratio with the digit in the camel cell. There are exactly seven camel cells in the grid. Two of them are shown; the others are hidden. All the hidden camels are in odd-numbered boxes and contain the digit of the box that they live in.  The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order.

The shaded regions (outlined in red) create a 6x6 grid scattered throughout the big grid. In this 6x6 grid, place the digits 1-6 exactly once in each row, column and region. The unshaded regions create a 10x10 grid scattered throughout the big grid. In this 10x10 grid, place the digits 0-9 exactly once in each row, column, and region.

The squares outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run. description:

We welcome in the month of March with a brand new sudoku hunt competition from Blobz (who made The Hobbit and the Lord Of The Rings hunts in 2024). It went live at 4pm yesterday and the closing date is 20th March!

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Very unusually, Simon went out to lunch today before recording a video. So he attempts Marty Sears' Parity Tic Tac Toe having had one or two libations beforehand :) 
It's fog of war and the usual Marty fare - very original, clever and funny from start to finish!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/11dz689p6l

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid - no guessing is necessary. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other). Todd and Steven are playing a game of Tic-Tac-Toe in a sudoku grid, where they attempt to 'claim' each 3x3 box. It's a very close game, with one player claiming four boxes and the other claiming five. However, the winner isn't necessarily the player to claim most boxes. To win the overall game, a player must claim at least one straight line of three 3x3 boxes (horizontally, vertically or diagonally), without their opponent managing to get a line of three boxes themselves. To determine who claims each 3x3 box, Todd and Steven play a mini game in each box. Todd places odd digits and Steven places even digits. A player claims a 3x3 box by getting at least one straight line of three digits of their parity (horizontally, vertically or diagonally) in that box, and without their opponent managing to get a line of three digits themselves. Here's where you can try Heavy Fog by James Kopp: https://sudokupad.app/umo2rblj9k 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area.
Digits along a purple line are a set of consecutive digits in any order with no repeats. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle of that arrow.
Additionally, adjacent digits on the purple lines and the arrows (including the circles) are different and not consecutive.

And this is where you can attempt the very approachable For Steph by Dan From “WOP-in-jərs”: https://sudokupad.app/h3i7jv9pqj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circled cell. A purple lines contains a set of consecutive digits in a random order. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of 5 or more. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear fog from that cell and certain other cells.

title: Extreme Tetris!
description:
*** MARCH SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION ***
We welcome in the month of March with a brand new sudoku hunt competition from Blobz (who made The Hobbit and the Lord Of The Rings hunts in 2024). It went live at 4pm this afternoon and the closing date is 20th March!

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's Saturday so sometimes we like to take a trip into non-sudoku land and this time we do that to visit Die Hard and his puzzle, Fillomino Knights.  It's one of those puzzles where you need to discover things you've probably never realised - and when you do, it'll make you very happy :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/n8uzh6og6f

Rules:
Normal fillomino rules apply ie Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally-connected cells. Fill each cell with a number equal to its region’s size (ie the number of cells in its region).  No two regions of the same size can share an edge (although they may touch diagonally). Use only region sizes of 1 to 9 and the digit N cannot appear in row N or column N. Two digits separated by a black dot must be in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit should be double the other). Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.

title: A Nurikabe Sudoku Teaser
description:
All dates mentioned in the video are WRONG: we aren't streaming tomorrow, instead we are releasing Blobz's new sudoku hunt, Nurikabe Puzzle Pack, on Patreon. 
Here's where you can play this puzzle, Nurikabe Sight Lines by Blobz: https://sudokupad.app/blobz/nurikabe-sight-lines 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into a number of islands -- orthogonally connected groups of cells. Every island contains a single circled cell; the digit in the circle indicates the number of cells making up the island. The islands are surrounded by a waterway -- a single orthogonally connected group of cells. All caged cells are waterway cells; The digit in a caged cell indicates how many waterway cells are seen orthogonally from that position, including itself (island cells block vision). The waterway cannot form any 2x2 areas.

title: Can You Divide This Square Into Rectangles?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A late gift from Santa today (well, really from Ennead) who made this beautiful sudoku as a present on the Discord server as part of Secret Santa. It's called Shikaku Killer and the basic idea is to divide the grid into rectangles... it sound simple and it sort-of is... but the logic involved is gorgeous. A highly recommended puzzle!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/vhpyfwlo56

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the entire grid into rectangles each containing a single circle and a single cell containing a ‘?’. The digit in the circle gives the number of cells in the rectangle. Digits cannot repeat in rectangles and each rectangle’s digits sum to one of 10, 20, 30 and X (where X is to be determined by the solver).
