title: Go Ahead. Break Your Brain!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Wuschel's twist on yin yang seems like it should be so simple... and yet!!  This is a brilliant sudoku which will force you to think in new ways.  Note there are two options for how you play it: the version Simon attempts in the video is a fog-of-war variant, which cleverly leads you through the puzzle (and is definitely NOT too easy); the other possibility (second link below) is to play the puzzle un-fogged -which is likely harder because you'll have to deduce where next to look at each stage.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

Version Simon attempts:
https://sudokupad.app/hqyaharmuk

Fogless version:
https://sudokupad.app/4et9l5ffrd

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Correctly entered digits may clear parts of the fog. Guessing is not required and discouraged. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. The value of a shaded cell is one greater than its digit, the value of an unshaded cell is one less than its digit. Box borders split blue lines into segments; the sum of the values on a segment is the same for each segment on a line. Different lines may have different totals. On a black dot one value is double the other. On a white dot values differ by 1. Not all dots are necessarily given.

title: Sudoku Marty's Astonishing New Puzzle
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We don't want to say too much about this new sudoku from Marty Sears before you have a chance to try it.  The imagination and craft that's gone into it almost beggar belief... give it a go and join us in the "amazed club"!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/da3cezx5at

Rules:
Quadswallop
by Marty Sears
CHAOS CONSTRUCTION:
Divide the grid into 8 regions each containing 8 orthogonally connected cells, and fill the grid with the digits 1-8 so that digits don't repeat in a row, column or region.
DOUBLERS:
Each row, column and region contains exactly one doubler cell. The value of a doubler cell is double its digit. Each doubler cell contains a different digit.
QUADSWALLOP:
Each digit 1-8 is represented by a different letter of the alphabet, to be determined. In each grey quad circle, 4 of the letters correspond to the digits (not values) in the surrounding 4 cells, but there is also one lying letter which does not correspond to any of the surrounding digits. The purple and green circles on the right can be used to keep track of letters in the grid, and their corresponding digits.
PURPLE X: Values separated by a small purple X sum to 10, and are in the same region.
The two ends of a grey, red or blue line always lie in different regions. Red and blue lines have an additional rule:
PARITY LINES (RED):
Two adjacent cells along a red line contain one even value and one odd value.
REGION SUM LINES (BLUE):
Region borders divide blue lines into segments which each have the same total value.

title: How Many Rinky-Dinks Will Solve This Puzzle?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another excursion into non-sudoku land this Saturday with a puzzle called Starmie by MaizeGator.  This is quite brilliant (whilst not being too hard either) - learn about Masyu and use the skills you learned playing Queens on LinkedIn while at work to solve it :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/04zedl744q

Rules:
Masyu: Draw a closed, non-branching, non-crossing loop along dotted gridlines. The loop must visit all given circles and follow these rules for movements: The loop must turn on black circles, and go straight through at least one vertex on both sides of the turn. The loop must go straight through white circles. It must also turn on at least one of the vertices it visits on either side of the white circle. Gray circles act as either a black or a white circle (the solver must deduce which). Star Battle: The Masyu loop divides the grid into regions. Place exactly one star into each row, column, and region, such that no two stars touch, not even diagonally. For the solution check to work, place a 1 into every cell containing a star in the final grid and a 0 into all other cells.

title: This is Driving me Crazy!
description:
Here's where you can try Crazy Consecutives by LlamaKing14: https://sudokupad.app/wb55wbfd3d 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the marked diagonal, place the digits 1-9 once each in consecutive order in one direction. Within each cage of size N, place the digits 1-N such that the digits form a "consecutive string" where each digit touches all the digits with which it is consecutive, either orthogonally or diagonally. This consecutive string is allowed to cross over itself. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive with each other.

title: Solving The Unsolvable: 9x9 From Just 3x3!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In a week of extraordinary puzzles, we may have found the MOST extraordinary.  Frippe has created a sudoku (called Think Outside The Box) in which the solver is only given a 3x3 that is part of a 9x9 sudoku.  Which part needs to be determined!  It's absolutely phenomenal that a whole 9x9 sudoku can be generated from just an (unspecified) 3x3 section.  Congratulations to Frippe on a VERY memorable debut.  (And apologies for another long video but many of you have requested longer videos this week so we do what we can!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/kjlvev0m76

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. This 3x3 of cells are a part of a standard 9x9 sudoku grid and can be located anywhere in the grid. Fill the 9x9 sudoku with digits from 1-9. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the total in the top left corner of the leftmost cell in the top row of the cage. All cages have a cage total. NB The very bottom right corner of the given 3x3 cells depicts a cage corner (which is there but difficult to see clearly). Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the arrow's circle located at the opposite end of the line as the arrow tip. Arrows do not touch or cross themselves or other arrows (Two arrows never enter the same cell). Arrows do not branch (Only one arrow per circle). The entire grid operates as ‘row indexers’ ie digits in row X indicate the row in which the digit X appears in that column. The goal of the puzzle is to show all of the correct digits, not the cages.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A pretty astonishing sudoku this evening from Shady Moon.  Not only because it seems to contain barely any information in the grid but because this is the first puzzle Shady Moon has ever created!  It's called Humidex and it's weird, wonderful and certainly miraculous!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/jvfdr3d0ag

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit in column 1 indicates the position of the 1 in its row. (eg if R5C1 is a 6, then R5C6 is a 1 as the 1 must appear in the 6th position). Column 5 operates the same way for the digit 5; and column 9 for the digit 9. Each digit in row 1 indicates the position of the 1 in its column. (eg if R1C5 is a 6, then R6C5 is a 1). Row 5 operates the same way for the digit 5; and row 9 for the digit 9. On thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Along the marked diagonal, digits must not repeat.

title: But ... the Given Digit is WHITE!
description:
Here's where you can try Whispers in the mist by pdyxs: https://sudokupad.app/usquoo8ao3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Once the puzzle is completed, any unshaded cells will be revealed, and shaded cells will still be covered in fog. All shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded.
Entering a correct digit in an unshaded cell will clear the fog:* in that cell; * in seen cells - any unshaded cells that can be seen from that cell in an orthogonal direction (with shaded cells blocking vision); and * around corners - any unshaded cells that are orthogonally connected to a seen cell. 
Any two orthogonally connected unshaded cells must have a difference of at least 5. A white dot separates digits which are consecutive. White digits are given, but have not been entered into the grid.

title: Sudoku Won't Help You Solve This SUDOKU!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we feature one of the strangest puzzles we've ever seen.  It's a puzzle where a digit can repeat in a row, column or box but only once!  It's called Fog 6x6 Pseudoku and it's by starwarigami (whose puzzle based off a purple comicbook character we remember well!)  No guessing is required to solve this one but it's VERY easy to make a mistake :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/0zkbctsdwi

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules (mostly) apply: Fill the grid with the digits 1-6 (and 0) so that (almost) no digit repeats in any row, column or box. Each unique digit may appear twice in exactly one row, column OR box. No row, column, or box may contain more than one repeated digit. (eg if a digit repeats in a single box, it must not repeat in any other box, any row or any column). The grid is covered with fog which will lift in a 3x3 area surrounding any correctly entered digit. Numbers outside the grid show the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Digits on a pink line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 relationship (i.e. one is double the other). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We solved this first in this trilogy a few weeks ago and this sequel from Skeptical Mario is every bit as good!  It's no sudoku but it should still make your day :)
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/9mpwvnok73

Rules:
Fillomino: Divide the grid into regions and fill each cell with the size of the region (in number of cells). Regions of the same size cannot share a cell edge. title: Do You Know These Sudoku Secrets?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight's sudoku has been recommended to us about as much as any puzzle we've ever featured.  It's called Whispering Yin Yang, it's by yttrio and it's rated 2/5 for difficulty.  This is seriously brilliant from start to finish - especially if you know a secret or two ;)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/ra3rf0qcnz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. The shaded cells act as a German Whispers line ie if two orthogonally connected cells are both shaded, then the digits in those cells must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a cell with an arrow counts the total number of shaded cells seen in the direction of the arrow (not counting the cell itself).

description:
Here's where you can try 7 Thermosnakes by Nordy: https://sudokupad.app/u9azfq7eta

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
James Sinclair is so reliable in the sense that just all his puzzles are excellent.  This is his latest, called Trickster, and it's a really original take on some well-known rules.  All the comments eulogise about the break-in... can you spot it?!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit in column 1 indicates the position of the 1 in its row (that is, if R5C1 is a 6, R5C6 is a 1). title: This Might Be The Puzzle Of The Year (and it's only February...)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Mark asks Simon to open tonight's puzzle live on camera - which normally means we're in for something unusual and so it proves.  A Tilt At Full Rank by bellal is some sort of Miracle Sudoku in that, at first (and even second) glance, there doesn't seem to be nearly enough information to yield a unique solution.  And yet...

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/u3r1c3ptbf

Rules:
Place a digit from 0-8 in each cell such that no digit is repeated in any row, column or 3x3 box. 5x5 Latin Square: The digits in red circles are all from the same set of five of the numbers from 0-8 (which five are to be determined). None of these repeat in any of the diagonal lines of red circles. Each diagonal of the 5x5 latin square can be read as a 5-digit number and the 20 resulting numbers (each line is read from both directions) can be ranked in numerical order. The position in the rank (lowest is 1, highest is 20) of some of the diagonals are given by the blue cages attached to that diagonal. N.B. Two-digit numbers are read from left to right and do not start with 0. There are no tied ranks in this puzzle. The two digits separated by the white dot differ by 1.

title: A Shiny Brand New Puzzle Ruleset!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
MaizeGator returns to the channel today with a puzzle called Shiny for our Non-Sudoku Saturday series!  The rules are a little involved but please watch the video introduction if you are in any doubt about them.  The payoff is SO worth it.  This is fabulous mash-up of Fillomino, Cave and Suguru (!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/o52m49iwee

Rules:
Cave: Shade some cells such that all orthogonally connected groups of shaded cells (the wall) touch the edge of the grid, and all unshaded cells (the cave) are orthogonally connected. 
Suguru: Each orthogonally connected group of shaded (wall) cells contains the digits 1-N (where N is the size of the group).  Suguru digits may not repeat in a row, column, or shaded group. 
Fillomino: Divide unshaded cells into polyominoes and fill each cell with a digit equal to the size of its polyomino. Polyominoes of the same size may not share an edge. All numbers in the puzzle are 1-9. 
A Fillomino Polyomino may not border a Suguru digit with the same value. An unshaded circled clue indicates the total number of unshaded cells seen in the four orthogonal directions, including the clue cell. A shaded circle clue indicates the size of the shaded region.

title: Connect 4: SOLVED!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This is simply one of the most brilliant and original puzzles you'll ever solve.  Marty Sears invites you to recreate the overall draw that resulted with Simon and Mark faced off at Connect 4!!  This is sudoku perfection.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/q3b8weqj5f

Rules:
Mark and Simon have just finished a game of Connect 4. They are both too clever for each other, and so it resulted in a draw; the board became full of an equal number of red and yellow discs without either of them managing to get any horizontal, vertical or diagonal connected line of 4 discs of their colour. Recreate the end board state by colouring the holes red and yellow. The first two moves have been shown. Fill the discs with the digits 1-7 so that no digits repeat in any row or column. A digit on an arrow disc indicates the total number of discs in the indicated directions (combined) that match its own colour. (The arrow disc itself isn't included in the count.) Two orthogonally adjacent red discs must be of different parity (one odd digit and one even digit.) Two orthogonally adjacent yellow discs must have a difference of at least 3.

title: The Hardest Sudoku I've EVER Solved
description:
As explained in yesterday's video description, Simon recorded this video on Tuesday but did not realise how long it would take to process/upload. Apologies to those whose birthdays were missed - Simon will catch up the birthdays tomorrow.  We decided to release this incredible long video on the channel after the Twitter Poll.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We had so many requests to attempt tonight's sudoku: Taiga by IcyFruit.  Well Simon did try it.  And embarked on the toughest battle he's ever had with ANY sudoku puzzle. With apologies for the ludicrous length of this video and with the utmost respect to IcyFruit's genius...

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/6f3k4btidk

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Identify two "indexer" cells in each row, column, and box, with one indexing in the row and the other indexing in the column. The digit in an indexer cell indicates the position of the other indexer cell in its row or column. Positions are counted left to right in rows and top to bottom in columns. The value of an indexer cell is the digit in the cell it indexes. For all other cells, their value is their own digit. All lines are region-subset lines: ie 3x3 box boundaries divide each line into segments. For any pair of segments on the same line, the values on one of those segments must all appear on the other segment. 
Examples: i) If () represents an indexer cell, then 12(6)34(7)598 would be a valid row of digits, because there are exactly two indexer cells, and one of the cells indexes the other: the (7) is in position 6, and the other indexer cell contains a 6. The value of the (6) cell would be 7, because that is the digit in the cell it indexes. Given that this is a row, we would also know that r7c6 must be an indexer cell, because the (7) cell indexes it. ii) A region-subset line could contain the values 189-8-98-918, where a dash represents a box boundary. This is valid because (8) is a subset of (89) and (189), (89) is a subset of (189), and (189) is a subset of itself.

There is a diagram representing the indexing here:
https://sudokupad.app/vrwxd77q0o

description:

I HAVE TRIED TO FIX THE RULES FOR SOME APPARENT INCONSISTENCIES IN THE BELOW AND THE ATTACHMENT BUT THE CARD IN THE VIDEO REMAINS AS IT WAS
Normal sudoku rules apply. Colors used in this puzzle are green (g), brown (b), and black (k).
A clue outside the grid with an arrow (little killer) shows the sum of the cells on the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a black (kropki) dot have a 1:2 ratio. Clues in colored squares outside the grid (none of which lie) indicate the sum of all cells in that row or column that are shaded the color of the clue. Shading does not need to be contiguous. If a cell is shaded, and if a cell has a clue in the lower right corner, the clue gives the digit in the cell. If a clue is unshaded, then the number in the lower right corner is a lie, so the digit in the cell is not the clue.
Some clues are lying, while others tell the truth. All truthful clues are fully-shaded, lying clues must not be fully-shaded. Note that there are an equal number of truth-tellers and liars for both the little killers and the Kropki dots.

*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION TOMORROW ***
Tomorrow (1 February) at 4pm UK time, we launch a brand new sudoku hunt from the Paint By Numbers Institute.  It's called Where's My Mamma and features 11 new puzzles (and Clocksmith's lovely artwork!). 

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's been a while but what a delight to welcome back ICHTUES to the sudoku fold.  This puzzle is SO good - the way the clues interact is just a delight from start to finish.  And it looks beautiful too :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/ws3dy3a8gi

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ in value by at least 5. The lines and hexagons are double arrows ie Digits on each line sum to the same number as the sum of the digits in the hexagons at the ends. Values at equal distance to the center of a lavender line sum to the central value.

title: Just How GORGEOUS Is This Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most visually arresting sudokus we've seen today (how was this created?!) from aqjhs.  It's called 'an ill omen' - we know not why - and it's not only lovely looking, it's absolutely lovely to solve.  First class from start to finish!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/59fo21vx0w

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by one move of a chess knight may not contain the same digit. For each line, the digits in the two cells marked with dots are ‘look-and-say clues’ ie in at least one way of reading them, one digit indicates how many times the other digit appears on the line. (eg if the marked cells contain 78 it can mean the line has seven instances of 8, or eight instances of 7). Adjacent digits along an orange line must have a difference of at least 4.

title: Flat Mates who Haven't the Foggiest
description:
Here's where you can have a go at Domino Flat Mates by Dorlir: https://sudokupad.app/12bkbyft2r 
Place the digits 0 to 8 exactly once each in every row, column and 3x3 box. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Not all Vs and Xs are necessarily given. Every horizontal domino which sums to 5 must have either the two cells directly above it summing to 1 or the two cells directly below it summing to 9 (it could have both, but it doesn't need both).

title: The Trick That Almost Fooled The Sudoku 'Expert'
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're saying nothing about this puzzle.  It's called Technically Correct.  It's by Lorena.  And Lorena is [insert adjective]! Just a quick reminder, we enjoy the comments, ESPECIALLY when they're kind ;)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/4o3b5oqvf2

Rules:
Fill in the grid with digits, which cannot repeat in any row, column or marked 3x3 box. The digits inside the large circles must appear in the cells that they touch. IN ADDITION, the circles function diagonally as ‘black kropki dots’, i.e. when two digits are separated diagonally by a large circle, one of them is two times the other. Small white dots separate consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are shown.

title: Here's Marty!!! Sudoku Genius Goes Mad
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
(Sincere apologies to Marty for the thumbnail - which is heavily edited!)
Marty Sears bends all the rules with this puzzle: Some Kind Of Chaos - in which sudoku only ends up applying in row 9, column 9 and some region we don't even know the shape or position of at the start of the solve!!

Did we mention it was 5/5 for difficulty.  We didn't... Oh... Well, it is.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/fg8p36r2g0

Rules:
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9. Each row N and column N contain exactly N distinct digits, with the rest of the row / column being filled with repeats. Divide the grid into 9 regions, each containing 9 orthogonally connected cells. The finished pattern of regions will have 180 degree rotational symmetry. The digit in a circle indicates how many distinct digits appear in its region. Eg: A 6 in a circle indicates that the region includes 6 distinct digits (and 3 repeats.) No two circles contain the same digit. Region borders divide blue lines into segments, each of which have the same sum. Each blue line must cross at least one region border.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This is one of those incredibly surprising puzzles!  It's called The Third Law Of Thermodynamics and it's a new fog sudoku from gdc.  The concept is so simple and yet the logic involved is deep and interesting.  Just exceptional!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/29hyhl8ay5

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a grey thermometer increase from the bulb end. Thermometers contain exactly 4 digits, only move horizontally and vertically (never diagonally) and don't branch or overlap. Thermometers are partially invisible (even after the fog is cleared). The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells. Every 2x2 area in the grid contains at least one digit from each of the sets (123), (456), and (789).

title: Hardly Anyone Has Solved This Puzzle.  Why?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
On Saturdays we often like to look at pencil puzzles (either mixed with sudoku or not) and, in that vein, we have had a very strong recommendation from Tyrgannus to take a look at Po-Boy by Sniglett and cornishjohn.  This wonderful sudoku has hardly been solved at all since it was born over 400 days ago.  Let's start putting that right!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/h8znpkd7qs

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells are coral and others are water. The odd digits are all part of the coral. All coral cells are orthogonally connected. The even digits are all part of the water. There may be multiple bodies of water, and all bodies of water are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid. No 2x2 area is entirely coral or entirely water. Clues outside the grid indicate the length of continuous runs of coral or water. A * indicates any positive number of continuous sets. In a row/column where clues are given, all clues are shown. For example, down column 1, there must exist some non-zero number of parity sets, followed by a set of length 1 of one parity type, immediately followed by a set of 3 of the opposite parity, followed by some non-zero number of parity sets. The values given outside the grid also indicate the sum of the digits between 1 and 9 in the respective row/column read as n-digit number read from left to right or top down. For example, down row 1, the digits between 1 and 9 must sum to 13. Digits along the marked diagonal sum to the number given. Digits may repeat along this diagonal.

description:

title: The Diagonals in this Puzzle Upset Me!
description:
Here's where you can try Zodiac Project: Taurus by ThePedallingPianist & Friends: https://sudokupad.app/ksj8nzm463 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw 9 straight diagonal lines, each through the centres of at least 3 cells: Every line contains exactly one Bull and one Red Flag; Different lines do not cross or share cells; The grid is a torus, i.e. row 1 wraps around to row 9 and column 1 wraps around to column 9 as shown.
No two Bulls contain the same digit; The digit on a Bull is the average (mean) of all digits on its line. No two Red Flags contain the same digit; The digit on a Red Flag is friendly, i.e. it equals its own row, column or box number (rows, columns and boxes are numbered 1-9 from top to bottom, left to right, and in reading order respectively).

title: The Sudoku Rat Run Is Back!  (With A Mouse!!)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have got so much pleasure from the Rat Run sudokus of Marty Sears that it was hardly surprising to see another great constructor "mimic" the style!  Tallcat's Mousetrap? is a brilliant homage to Marty's puzzles - featuring a mouse, a cat and some really fantastic logic.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/06vt5y9nwu

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Mus the mouse must reach the cupcake and Felix the cat must reach the escape hole finding paths through the maze. Individually, their paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, both Mus and Felix can move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Importantly, the paths of Felix and Mus can cross each other. This can only happen on even digits and if it does happen, both paths MUST continue on to another cell in a straight line. 
Mus and Felix may only pass through black arrows if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. Cells connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. Digits separated by a green grape have a difference of at least 5. Not all possible grapes have been given. 
For Mus, the path within each box must be a thermometer with the bulb being the first square entered and the tip being the last square in the box. Digits along a thermometer increase from bulb to tip. Repeat visits to the same box are considered separate thermos. For Felix, adjacent cells along the path must be of different parity (odd/even).

title: "This Is A Sudoku Masterpiece".  Simon, 20 Jan 2025.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Myxo has done it again.  A simply mind-blowing sudoku called Thermo Knots (following his Arrow Knots from a couple of weeks ago).  It is worth every moment you may have to spend getting to grips with the ruleset to have a go at this one - it beggars belief.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/4geira1lnl

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine regions, each containing 9 orthogonally connected cells such that each cell is part of exactly one region. Fill the grid with digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column or region. Thermo knots: From each big circle, draw straight horizontal or vertical thermometers in all possible directions, such that each thermo occupies at least two cells (including the circle). Digits along a thermo must increase, starting from the circle. Additionally, all cells along thermos must be part of the same region as their circle. If a thermo doesn't reach the edge of the grid, it MUST keep extending until it reaches the edge of its region, and the cell directly after the tip must be in a different region and must contain a SMALLER digit than the tip. Cells separated by a small white circle must be in DIFFERENT regions and contain consecutive digits.

title: Can we Weigh up the Difficulties of Sudoku? Of Course!
description:
Here's where you can try Weighted Cells by Oddlyeven: https://sudokupad.app/sqdra9pozn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells.
One cell in each row, column and box is lighter than normal. Lighter cells have a value equal to half of their digit. Each digit from 1 to 9 appears once in the set of lighter cells. One cell in each row, column and box is heavier than normal. Heavier cells have a value equal to one and a half times their digit. Each digit from 1 to 9 appears once in the set of heavier cells. No cell is both lighter and heavier.
Box borders divide a line into segments whose values sum to the same number. Lines do not branch, cross or share cells.

title: You CANNOT Only Solve This Puzzle Once!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very original fog sudoku today from pdyxs called Recounting The Counting in which you have to solve the puzzle repeatedly taking into account new information each time.  It's great fun and really very satisfying to sort this one out :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/tc5dhvo13g

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A black dot between two digits means that one is double the other. A white dot between two digits means that they are consecutive. At any point, a digit N in a revealed circle means that the digit appears in revealed circles N times. Cells shaded green are “stable”: their value remains the same throughout the puzzle. All other cells are “unstable”. The grid is partially covered in fog. Fill in all revealed cells based on the revealed clues, leaving any new stable digits until last. Filling in the stable digits will reveal more of the puzzle, at which point all unstable digits will need to be recalculated (ie deleted and then recomputed!).

title: There's an Imposter Among Us!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Box 8 is Sus! by Panthera: https://sudokupad.app/7ry8w31ry3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sums of runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded. The shaded runs must be separated by at least 1 non-shaded cell. The imposter has messed up this Japanese Sums Sudoku! The imposter changed SOME column/row clues to represent the runs of UNshaded cells instead of the shaded ones! And he even erased one of the clues (row 5)! All I remember is that there are less shaded cells than unshaded. 
Note: a row or column clue will only give you a clue about one type of cell: shaded or unshaded. There are no mixed clues within a column or row.

title: The Sudoku Ladder: The Return Of Zetamath
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's always a great day for sudoku when you get to try a new zetamath puzzle.  His new one is called Ladder and, as one commentator described it, 
'solving this is like a beautiful dance'. Enjoy!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/7wxsd2awbv

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along grey (TEN) lines must be broken into one or more non-overlapping segments that each sum to ten. Digits may repeat within such sums if allowed by other rules. For example, 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Any set of three sequential cells along an entropic (ENT) line must contain a low digit (1-3), middle digit (4-6) and high digit (7-9). Digits may repeat on an ENT line, if allowed by other rules. Digits on a purple (REN) line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. Digits do not repeat along a gold (NAB) line. Additionally, no pair of digits anywhere on a gold line can be consecutive. Along green (GW) lines, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one is exactly double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.

title: The Fog Sudoku Theorem
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have to admit that this sudoku from sujoyku and ChinStrap has a slightly longer ruleset than usual BUT this is SUCH a good puzzle we will absolutely forgive that.  A stone-cold classic of the fog sudoku era!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/tuf714ivht

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells. All lines and attached circles are “split pea lines” and, between the circles, the lines function also as “index lines”. 
Digits on a “split pea line” between two circles sum to a two-digit number written using the digits in the circles. For example, 3_346_1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is 1 & 3, the two circle digits. 
Each index line begins in one of the two line cells next to a circle (you must determine which). The digit in the Nth cell along the line (from the start cell) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example, 3214 is a valid index line, the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd digit is a 1, and so on. 
Lines do not cross or share cells with themselves or other lines.  Each connected set of lines and circles has a distinct colour/ style.  Lines have been made thicker to enable solvers to see if a line moves diagonally.

title: One Of The Best Constructed Puzzles We've Ever Seen
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another 100% rated sudoku today - this time from yttrio.  This is actually one of the very best "hybrid" puzzles we've ever seen.  It combines the logic problem "cave" (sometimes called Corral) with sudoku in a new way and, as one commentator noted, every single clue here is "chef's kiss".  Breathtaking.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/vgbfcjxvav

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are connected orthogonally by other shaded cells to the edge of the grid, and the remaining unshaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Note that 2x2 areas that are entirely shaded or entirely unshaded *are* allowed. Digits in circles cannot be shaded, and represent the total number of unshaded cells seen horizontally and vertically from that cell, including itself. Shaded cells block the vision. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must have consecutive values. Additionally, one of those cells must be shaded and the other must be unshaded. Every set of orthogonally connected unshaded cells within a 3x3 Sudoku region acts as a Renban line: ie those cells must contain a nonrepeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Note that a 3x3 region may have more than one such set of cells. Also note that such a set may consist of just one cell.

title: A True Fog Sudoku Odyssey
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the undoubted masters of fog sudoku, gdc, bamboozles Simon tonight in a movie-length episode.  Unsurprisingly, this puzzle is full of surprises with the "usual" one or two moments of absolute genius from one of the channel's favourite constructors! (And why is the puzzle called "Repitition Legitimizes"?)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/i2r7za43kv

Rules:
𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Place 9 non-overlapping 3x3 boxes in the grid. Fill each cell in a box with a digit from 1-9 such that digits don't repeat in rows, columns or boxes. A cell that is not in any 3x3 box should be left blank but its value for the purposes of the loop/palindrome is zero.
𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝗙𝗼𝗴: The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues.
𝗪𝗵𝗶𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗽: Draw a loop through the centers of some cells that moves orthogonally from cell to cell (never diagonally). The loop may touch itself diagonally, but not orthogonally. Adjacent values along the loop differ by 5 or more.
𝗖𝗶𝗿𝗰𝗹𝗲𝘀: Circles are on the loop and in boxes. Their digit counts the number of loop-cells in their box.
𝗣𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀: Cells an equal distance to the circled center of a line have the same value.

title: Index Fingers:  Only 1/5 For Difficulty And Yet Magnificent!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The one and only Marty Sears has come up with something quite wonderful (and ludicrous): Index Fingers - where the fingers do actually index digits in the grid!!  It's only 1/5 for difficulty but don't think it's trivial - the logic is still lovely and the whole thing will put you in a good mood :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/1dm8yvq9jt

Rules:
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 6, once each, into every row, column and 2x3 bold-outlined rectangle). 
Each finger has lost its gold ring! Can you find them? Every row, column and box contains one gold ring, and none of them are located on a finger. Each gold ring contains a different digit.
The digits ABC along a finger, reading towards the fingertip (the C goes on the fingernail), indicates that row A column B contains that finger's missing gold ring, which contains the digit C.

title: The Revenge Of The Miracle Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Ever since the original Miracle Sudoku by Mitchell Lee, constructors have found new and extraordinary ways of putting less and less things in a sudoku grid!  The latest example is apetersen's Sort Of Miraculous - which boasts just a single black dot!  This is a seriously good puzzle - enjoy!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/94c0vtokc3

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The 3x3 boxes in the grid are numbered in normal reading order. In odd numbered boxes, odd digits appear in ascending order (with respect to position within that box). In even numbered boxes, even digits appear in ascending order (with respect to position within that box). (Cells within 3x3 boxes are also numbered in normal reading order.) title: "One of the best puzzles in the last year." Says Mark
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another sensational sudoku this evening.  This time it's Myxo with Arrow Knots - a new idea based on building arrows.  Mark called Simon this morning to tell him this is one of his favourite puzzles of the last 12 months.  And Simon now understands why.  This is ridiculously clever.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/v3zxi1cddk

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine regions each containing 9 orthogonally-connected cells, such that each cell is part of exactly one region. Some region borders have already been given. Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column or region. From each circle, draw some arrows that travel in a straight line either horizontally only or vertically only. The number in the bottom right corner of a circle cell indicates the number of arrows that must be drawn from that circle. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the attached circle. Additionally, all cells along arrows must be part of the same region as the circle they originate from. If an arrow doesn't reach the edge of the grid, the cell directly after the tip must be in a different region than the arrow.

title: Is This The MOST Terrifying Name In Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A movie-length edition of CtC this evening in which Simon is confronted by the new puzzle from none other than Gliperal...  just about as scary a name as you'll find!

The puzzle is called Welcome, 2025 and has a fascinating original ruleset in which killer cages must be divided up into up to 4-digit numbers... 

It's a fantastic idea and execution but it's not completely simple to complete ;)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/hr2psfhzcz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages. If a cage contains a clue in the top left corner, that cage must be comprised of 1-, 2-, 3-, and/or 4-digit numbers that sum to that value. Numbers are made from either horizontally adjacent digits read left-to-right; or vertically adjacent digits read top-to-bottom (ie numbers cannot bend!). Every digit within a cage must be part of exactly one number, and numbers may not cross cage borders.

title: Really Approachable ... Beetles?
description:
Here's where you can try the relatively straightforward German Beetles by Katie Splendor: https://sudokupad.app/9os1agpdp7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.  Digits joined by an "X" sum to 10. Digits joined by a "V" sum to 5. Digits in a cage sum to the total shown. A thin gray line without a bulb is a palindrome and reads the same in either direction.

description:

title: Only one Galaxy in view? What?
description:
Here's where you can try Galactic Census 2 by Blobz: https://sudokupad.app/blobz/galactic-census-2?setting-dashedgrid=1 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into galaxies: orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centers (marked with a small dot). All cells must be part of a galaxy; no galaxies overlap. Grey dots mark "renban" galaxies: those with two or more cells, whose digits form an unbroken consecutive sequence in any order. White dots mark galaxies whose digits do NOT form a consecutive sequence. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy. There is one "dark star" (a single cell galaxy) that is not marked.
As per Galactic Map Standards: All galaxies with at least TWO cells indicate their SMALLEST digit with a diamond icon. All galaxies with at least SIX cells indicate their LARGEST digit with a circle icon. The Galactic Census requires that all galaxies with at least THREE cells must report their star system count (sum of digits in the galaxy).
